people.name: Kiran Mukadam
people.bio: Kiran Mukadam was appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer from 6 May 2025 and is a key managerial personnel. He handles shareholder and exchange matters. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: No executive changes found since the FY26 annual report (16 May 2026). Sameer V. Shah moved to a non-executive role here after the demerger.

companies.styleNote: The founding promoters (U. Shekhar, G. Ramakrishnan, the Shanbhag and Patil families) own about 71% but are not in day-to-day management; U. Shekhar and G. Ramakrishnan sit as non-executive directors. The company is run by long-serving professional managers, and the chairman, Kanwar Bir Singh Anand, is independent. No directors are related to each other.

people.name: K. Natarajan
people.stake: 9,600 shares jointly with his wife (about 0.03%) (FY26 AGM notice)
people.bio: K. Natarajan, 61, has a commerce degree from the University of Mumbai, is a cost accountant (ICWAI) and has done the Advanced Management Programme at Harvard Business School. He joined Galaxy in April 1993 and has headed finance, IT, business creation, business commercial, global sourcing and supply chain. He became Executive Director and COO in October 2016 and Managing Director from February 2024. He also sits on the boards of the Egyptian and US subsidiaries, including TRI-K Industries. His FY26 pay was ₹3.23cr, and he was granted 23,630 performance options in 2025 vesting in August 2028.

people.name: Vaijanath Kulkarni
people.bio: Vaijanath Kulkarni is a chemical engineer and has done the Advanced Management Programme at Harvard Business School. He has been with Galaxy since 1995 and is now Executive Director and COO. He also chairs the Risk Management Committee as Chief Risk Officer. His FY26 pay was ₹2.85cr, and he received 23,630 performance options in 2025 vesting in August 2028.

people.name: Abhijit Damle
people.bio: Abhijit Damle became CFO in July 2022, succeeding K. Ganesh Kamat on his retirement. Before that he was Galaxy's Head of RMU & CG (resource mobilisation, finance and corporate governance). Earlier he was finance head at LANXESS India. He is a University of Mumbai graduate.

people.name: Niranjan Ketkar
people.bio: Niranjan Ketkar is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer and is listed among senior management. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: Rajib Bhattacharjee (VP – Value Acceleration, senior management) resigned on 15 May 2026. Viju Jose joined as VP – Business Creation (July 2025) and Narendra Kumar Saini as Chief Digital Officer (March 2026).

companies.styleNote: Run by its two unrelated co-founders: Edward Menezes (Executive Chairman) and Sunil Chari (MD). Each founder's son now heads a business unit as senior management. Promoters own about 68%.

people.name: Edward Menezes
people.since: Co-founder; on the board since inception
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; father of Mikhail Menezes
people.stake: 29.30% including the Menezes Family Trust (FY26 annual report); Menezes family about 31.4%
people.bio: Edward Menezes has a B.Sc. in chemistry from K. J. Somaiya College (University of Bombay), a B.Sc. (Tech) in textile chemistry from UDCT, and a master's in marketing management from Welingkar Institute. Before co-founding Rossari he worked at Clariant India (formerly Sandoz) in technical services, product development and business development. He has over 40 years in specialty chemicals and remains closely involved in day-to-day operations. His awards include the Hurun India Industry Achievement Award (2022) and the UDCT Distinguished Alumnus award (2013).

people.name: Sunil Chari
people.since: Co-founder; on the board since inception
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; father of Yash Chari; not related to Edward Menezes
people.stake: 22.39% including the Chari Family Trust (FY26 annual report); Chari family about 31%
people.bio: Sunil Chari holds a B.A. from Kakatiya University and a diploma in technical and applied chemistry from VJTI, Mumbai. He has over 35 years of experience, earlier in textile processing and dyestuffs, and co-founded Rossari. As MD he runs daily operations and strategy, and built the sales and distribution network. In FY26 he moved about 9% of his direct holding into the Chari Family Trust and to family members, including his son Yash. VJTI and ICT have honoured him as a distinguished alumnus.

people.name: Ketan Sablok
people.bio: Ketan Sablok is a Fellow Chartered Accountant and a Cost Accountant, with a B.Com (Hons) from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata. He has over 25 years in finance and was earlier CFO of Navin Fluorine International; before that he worked at Shaw Wallace. He joined Rossari as Group CFO in November 2021 and leads finance, treasury, planning, tax and IT, reporting to the MD.

people.name: Mikhail Menezes
people.relation: Son of Executive Chairman Edward Menezes
people.bio: Mikhail Menezes has a master's in chemical engineering from Imperial College London and joined Rossari after graduating. He heads the animal health and nutrition (AHN) and textile businesses and sits on the Risk Management Committee. His FY26 pay was ₹98.8 lakh, approved as a related-party 'office of profit'.

people.name: Yash Chari
people.relation: Son of MD Sunil Chari
people.stake: 4.45% (FY26 annual report), up from 0.30% after a family transfer
people.bio: Yash Chari has a bachelor's in chemical engineering from the University of South Florida and joined Rossari after his studies. He heads the acquired Unitop and Tristar businesses. His FY26 pay was ₹65.6 lakh, approved as a related-party 'office of profit'.

people.name: Puneet Arora
people.role: Business Head – Global Textile & Strategies (senior management)
people.bio: Puneet Arora holds a B.Com from Ambedkar College, University of Bombay, and has been with Rossari since its incorporation. He earlier led M&A and global textile exports, and now heads global textile and strategy.

people.name: Prasad Gadkari
people.bio: Prasad Gadkari holds a diploma in business management from Nagpur University and has been with Rossari since its incorporation. He runs manufacturing operations across the plants.

companies.changes: No KMP changes in FY26 or since. Chief HR Officer Sunil V. resigned in May 2025. Company Secretary is Parul Gupta.

companies.styleNote: Run by its two promoters, Chairman & MD Mahesh Babani and Executive Director D. B. Rao, who are not related to each other; the Babani and Doppalapudi families and their investment companies own 60.6% after selling 9.3% in December 2025. Privi Fine Sciences, owned by the promoters, is being merged in for shares.

people.name: Mahesh P. Babani
people.since: Board since 11 May 2017 (after Privi merged into the listed company); founder of Privi
people.relation: Promoter
people.stake: 6.62% directly plus 4.59% through his HUF (FY26 annual report); promoter group together 60.60%
people.bio: Mahesh Babani, 68, is a commerce graduate with over 40 years of operational and managerial experience. He built Privi from a start-up into one of the world's larger pine-based aroma chemical makers. He sets long-term strategy, business development and financial management, and has travelled the globe for three decades building ties with fragrance houses and suppliers. He also sits on the boards of subsidiaries Prigiv Specialties and Privi Biotechnologies, and of the promoter-owned Privi Fine Sciences. His FY26 pay was ₹6cr, with a 10% rise approved for FY27.

people.name: D. B. Rao (Bhaktavatsala Rao Doppalapudi)
people.since: Board since 11 May 2017; re-appointed for 13 Aug 2026 – 12 Aug 2029
people.relation: Co-promoter; not related to Mahesh Babani
people.stake: 2.17% (FY26 annual report), down from 3.96% after the December 2025 block sale; his family holds about 5.4% more
people.bio: D. B. Rao, 80, is a postgraduate in engineering with over 50 years of experience. He runs operations, R&D, personnel and raw-material sourcing, and built the company's plants quickly and at low cost. He takes a close interest in R&D, especially green technologies. He is also a director of Privi Biotechnologies and of Vivira Investments & Trading, the largest promoter holding company (29.7%). His FY26 pay was ₹24 lakh; the new term allows up to ₹2.1cr a year.

people.name: R. S. Rajan
people.bio: R. S. Rajan is President and has been classified as senior management since August 2020. He is a long-serving member of the core team. The annual report gives no further background.

people.name: Narayan S. Iyer
people.bio: Narayan Iyer has been CFO since August 2020 and also handles investor relations and the earnings calls. He was earlier Senior Vice President – Finance at Privi. The annual report gives no education details.

people.name: Ashwini Saumil Shah
people.bio: Ashwini Shah has been Company Secretary and Compliance Officer since November 2022. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: No changes in KMP or senior management in FY26 or since. D. B. Rao re-appointed for three years from 13 Aug 2026 (AGM approval).

companies.styleNote: A family company (set up in 1973) run by father and son: Padam Kumar Agarwala is Chairman & MD and his son Varun Agarwal is Joint MD. The two of them own about 68%, and promoters 77.15% in all.

people.name: Padam Kumar Agarwala
people.since: Director since 13 March 1995; business head for 12+ years before that
people.relation: Promoter; father of Joint MD Varun Agarwal
people.bio: Padam Kumar Agarwala has a commerce degree from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata. He worked in the company as a business head for more than 12 years before joining the board in 1995, and has over 40 years in industrial gases. He oversees the eastern region, sets strategy and governance, and is also a director of family companies including Ellenbarrie Cryogenics, Ellenbarrie Agro Products and several tea businesses. He and Varun have personally guaranteed some of the company's loans.

people.name: Varun Agarwal
people.relation: Son of Chairman & MD Padam Kumar Agarwala
people.bio: Varun Agarwal holds a B.Sc. in economics from the London School of Economics and an M.Phil. from the University of Cambridge. He began his career at Lehman Brothers before joining the family company in 2008, and has over 15 years of experience. He runs the southern region and focuses on financial performance and growth strategy. He delivered the AGM statement alongside his father in September 2026.

people.name: K. Srinivas Prasad
people.since: Joined Dec 2013 as Controller – Finance; CFO since 1 Nov 2014
people.bio: K. Srinivas Prasad has a commerce degree from BJB College, Bhubaneswar (Utkal University). He is a chartered accountant and company secretary (ICAI and ICSI associate) and has qualified as a cost accountant. Before Ellenbarrie he worked at Air Liquide North India. He joined in December 2013 and became CFO in November 2014.

people.name: Sanjay Basak
people.bio: Sanjay Basak holds an M.Tech in cryogenic engineering from IIT Kharagpur and did an executive programme in operations management at IIM Calcutta. He earlier worked at BOC India and Bhushan Steel. He joined in 2016 and heads projects and engineering.

people.name: Aditya Keshri
people.bio: Aditya Keshri is an associate member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. He earlier worked at Alcove Developers, Grameen Shakti Microfinance and Jiwanram Sheoduttrai Industries, and joined in March 2024.

companies.changes: No KMP changes in FY26. Sujoy Sen was appointed Chief Information Officer (senior management) from 1 Aug 2026. Subir Sen is GM – HR (senior management).

companies.styleNote: The Vaze family runs Keva: third-generation Kedar Vaze is Whole-time Director & Group CEO. His father Ramesh Vaze, the non-executive Chairman and a master perfumer, died on 15 Sep 2026; his mother Prabha Vaze is a non-executive director. Promoters own 54.87%, with about 50 lakh promoter shares pledged. No new chairman had been named as of 29 Sep 2026.

people.name: Kedar Vaze
people.role: Whole-time Director & Group Chief Executive Officer
people.since: With Keva since Oct 1996; Group CEO since 2014; re-appointed 1 Sep 2025 – 31 Aug 2028
people.relation: Promoter; son of the late Chairman Ramesh Vaze and of director Prabha Vaze
people.stake: 9.44% (1,30,60,131 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 54.87%
people.bio: Kedar Vaze holds an M.Sc. in chemistry from IIT Bombay and completed Stanford's Global Managers Program. He joined the family business in October 1996 and worked as Chief Technology Officer and then Group COO before becoming Group CEO in 2014. He is a trained perfumer with several fragrance and flavour patents. His FY26 pay was ₹4.4cr; shareholders were asked to waive recovery of excess pay he received for FY25.

people.name: Jagdish Agarwal
people.bio: Jagdish Agarwal has over 28 years in finance across manufacturing, telecom and banking. He was Executive Director and CFO of Huhtamaki India for about four years, and before that spent over 15 years at Owens Corning India in finance roles including CFO. Earlier he worked at Reliance Communications and ICICI Bank. He joined Keva as Group CFO in December 2025 after a four-month gap filled by an interim CFO.

people.name: B. Ramkrishnan
people.bio: B. Ramkrishnan heads the fragrance business in Asia and the USA and is listed first among senior management. The annual report does not give his background.

people.name: Amit Gulati
people.role: Chief Operating Officer – Asia (Fragrance & Flavours) (senior management)
people.bio: Amit Gulati is COO for fragrance and flavours in Asia and is part of the senior management team. The annual report does not give his background.

people.name: Deepti Chandratre
people.since: Joined 11 April 2025; Company Secretary since 1 May 2025
people.bio: Deepti Chandratre joined as Global Legal Counsel in April 2025 and became Company Secretary and Compliance Officer from May 2025. She also served as interim CFO from 7 Oct to 1 Dec 2025, between the exit of Rohit Saraogi and the arrival of Jagdish Agarwal.

companies.changes: Chairman Ramesh Vaze died on 15 Sep 2026; no successor announced yet. CFO Rohit Saraogi left on 30 Jul 2025 and Group CHRO Nishant Kolgaonkar in Apr 2025. Ranjeet Agrawal joined as EVP – Sales (India subcontinent) on 20 Aug 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Tibrewala family company: founder Surendrakumar Tibrewala is Chairman & MD, his son Sanjay is Executive Director & CFO and his daughter Aarti Jhunjhunwala is an Executive Director. The three family members are the only executives listed as senior management. Promoters own about 62%.

people.name: Surendrakumar Tibrewala
people.relation: Founder-promoter; father of Sanjay Tibrewala and Aarti Jhunjhunwala
people.stake: 52.28% (FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 62%
people.bio: Surendrakumar Tibrewala, son of the late Deviprasad Tibrewala, holds a commerce degree from R. A. Poddar College (University of Mumbai) and a law degree from Government Law College. He started in specialty chemicals at 20 and has over four decades of experience making chemicals and enzymes for textiles, construction, water treatment, leather, paper and paints. As Chairman & MD he sets the long-term strategy. He chairs the board's Administrative Committee, which handles day-to-day business matters and is made up only of the three family executives.

people.name: Sanjay Tibrewala
people.since: Promoter since inception; re-appointed for 1 Oct 2025 – 30 Sep 2030
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD; brother of Aarti Jhunjhunwala
people.bio: Sanjay Tibrewala graduated from Narsee Monjee College of Commerce and Economics (University of Mumbai) in 2001 and then studied textile processing and chemistry at SASMIRA, Mumbai. He has been with the company since inception and has over two decades in textile chemicals. As Executive Director and CFO he leads new markets and the product range. The company moved into oilfield chemicals by buying US-based CrudeChem in December 2025. His pay matches his father's (both 23.9 times the median employee).

people.name: Aarti Jhunjhunwala
people.relation: Daughter of the Chairman & MD; sister of Sanjay Tibrewala
people.bio: Aarti Jhunjhunwala, 42, holds a master's in accounts and taxation from Narsee Monjee College. She has over 16 years in the business, covering business development, sales, branding and global alliances, and led the push into international textile markets. She won the 'Women at Work Leadership Award' at the Asia Pacific HRM Congress. Her FY26 pay was ₹1.07cr, up 24%.

people.name: Sunny Parmar
people.bio: Sunny Parmar is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer and the only non-family member of senior management. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: No changes in KMP or senior management in FY26 or since the annual report. Independent director Navin Mittal completed his term in Sep 2025.

companies.styleNote: A subsidiary of Germany's BASF SE, which owns 73.33%. It is run by BASF group executives on rotation: a German MD, a long-serving BASF finance head as CFO and a manufacturing head, all whole-time directors. The chairman, Pradip P. Shah, is non-executive. No directors are related to each other.

people.name: Alexander Gerding
people.bio: Alexander Gerding, born in Bremen in 1979, joined BASF in 2000 through a dual-study programme and earned an MBA from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro in 2005. He has held roles in Argentina, the US and Germany, mostly in crop protection; before India he was Vice President, Business Management for Agricultural Solutions, EMEA East (from 2019). He chairs the Risk Management Committee. His background is in the agri business that is now being demerged into BASF Agricultural Solutions India. His FY26 pay was ₹9.97cr, including BASF SE share-based incentives.

people.name: Narendranath J. Baliga
people.since: CFO since 1 Jan 2015; whole-time director 1 Jan 2025 – 30 Jun 2027
people.bio: Narendranath Baliga is a chartered accountant and a business management graduate from Mysore University. He joined BASF in 1994 and has worked in India, Singapore, China and Germany in finance, controlling, supply chain and process and enterprise architecture. He has been CFO of BASF India since 2015 and also heads Global Business Services. He joined the board as a whole-time director in January 2025. His FY26 pay was ₹3.46cr.

people.name: Anil Kumar Choudhary
people.bio: Anil Kumar Choudhary has a bachelor's in mechanical engineering and a postgraduate qualification in marketing management. He joined BASF in 2004 and was Managing Director of BASF Catalysts India and then Business Director for Performance Materials. He now oversees all manufacturing sites (as Occupier under the Factories Act) and the materials, industrial solutions and surface technologies segments. His FY26 pay was ₹3.04cr.

people.name: Manohar Kamath
people.role: Director – Legal, General Counsel (India) & Company Secretary
people.bio: Manohar Kamath is BASF India's general counsel and Company Secretary and sits on the management committee. He is secretary to the board committees. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: No executive changes in FY26 or since. Non-executive BASF nominee Marcelo R. Lu resigned on 30 Nov 2025 and was replaced by Andrew Postlethwaite. Sunita Sule is the fifth member of the management committee.

companies.styleNote: Founder Dr. A. N. Gupta (80) is non-executive Chairman; his wife Dr. Kailash Gupta and daughter Shonika Prasad are non-executive directors. Day-to-day the company is run by professional executives, led by MD T. V. Chowdary. The Gupta family holds 41.33% (now largely through the AKS Family Trust), which Apollo Micro Systems has agreed to buy, with an open offer due in Q3 FY27, so control and possibly the management team will change.

people.name: T. V. Chowdary
people.since: Board since 31 Aug 2005; MD since 14 Feb 2022 (term to 13 Feb 2027)
people.bio: T. V. Chowdary, 69, holds a B.Sc. (Tech) in petroleum and is a chemical engineer with over 40 years in making explosives, detonators and solid propellants. He joined the board in 2005 and was Deputy MD until the board made him MD in February 2022 as part of the succession plan. He leads operations and strategy, with focus on execution, safety and customers. His current term ends in February 2027, around when Apollo Micro Systems is due to take control.

people.name: Y. Durga Prasad Rao
people.since: With the company since 1 July 1989; board since 10 Aug 2019 (term to 9 Aug 2027)
people.bio: Durga Prasad Rao, 63, has a B.Tech in mechanical engineering from Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati. He joined Premier in July 1989 and has 36 years in explosives, propellants, refractories and factory management. He heads manufacturing at the Peddakandukuru and Katepally plants and is central to plant discipline and delivery.

people.name: B. M. Vijay Kumar
people.bio: Buddhavarapu Mahadeva Vijay Kumar is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, the Institute of Cost Accountants and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, and a law graduate. He has more than 30 years of experience in accounts, finance, management, secretarial and legal work. He became CFO in November 2024.

people.name: K. Jhansi Laxmi
people.bio: K. Jhansi Laxmi is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer and secretary to the audit and nomination committees. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: Apollo Micro Systems is buying the promoters' 41.33% (announced 9 Jul 2026; open offer pending), so board and management changes are likely. Independent director Dr. Kumuda Raghavan resigned on 31 Jul 2026. No executive changes since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 1955 by Keshavlal V. Bodani and now run by the third generation: brothers Dharmil Bodani (Chairman & MD) and Shyamal Bodani (Executive Director), who own 37.08% each. A hired Group CEO, Parag Satoskar, runs day-to-day operations under them. Promoters own 74.17% with no pledge; the two brothers were paid ₹8.5cr in FY26.

people.name: Dharmil A. Bodani
people.relation: Promoter, third generation; brother of Shyamal Bodani
people.bio: Dharmil Bodani has over three decades in flavours, fragrances and aroma chemicals and trained in perfumery in Grasse, France. He leads the company's strategy and has built it into one of the few integrated flavour, fragrance and aroma chemical makers in India, with a focus on research. His FY26 pay was ₹4.74cr, even though profit fell to about ₹3cr.

people.name: Shyamal A. Bodani
people.since: Career began 2003; current term to 15 Aug 2027
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Dharmil Bodani
people.bio: Shyamal Bodani began his career in 2003 and has over two decades in the industry. He oversees domestic and international marketing, sales and exports, contributes to financial management, and leads project planning and execution across the group. He also chairs the CSR committee. His FY26 pay was ₹3.79cr.

people.name: Parag K. Satoskar
people.bio: Parag Satoskar holds a bachelor's in pharmaceutical science from the Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai. He was earlier a partner at Arofine Chemical Industries. He has been CEO since May 2019, signs the code-of-conduct and CFO-CEO certifications, and sits on the risk committee.

people.name: Satish Kumar Ray
people.bio: Satish Kumar Ray holds an MBA and has 25–30 years of experience across manufacturing operations, procurement, sales, supply chain, HR, insurance and claims. He is the legal Occupier of the plants at Ambernath, Bareilly and Vadodara, the Mahad subsidiary plant, and the Chandivali R&D centre. His FY26 pay was ₹41.6 lakh.

people.name: Girish Khandelwal
people.bio: Girish Khandelwal is a chartered accountant and a long-serving finance executive of the company; he earlier worked in finance and accounts when it was called Camphor & Allied Products. He is the CFO and a key managerial personnel.

people.name: Anita P. Satoskar
people.bio: Anita Satoskar is Chief Technology Officer and a key managerial personnel. The annual report gives no further background.

people.name: Kiranpreet Gill
people.bio: Kiranpreet Gill is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: No KMP changes in FY26. Senior managers Pravin Varade (Projects, Oct 2025) and Savita Dalvi (VP Sales, F&F, Nov 2025) resigned; Nitin Bhuduvalekar joined as VP – Sales Fragrance on 1 Aug 2026. Independent director Deepak Ramachandra resigned in May 2026, replaced by John Gloster.

companies.styleNote: Founder Anil Jain is Chairman & MD and the only promoter on the board; no directors or KMP are related to him. Promoters own about 56.6%, almost all through Refex Holding, and a large share of it (over 40%) is pledged. The CFO and Company Secretary are paid by the promoter's holding company, not by Refex Industries.

people.name: Anil Jain
people.relation: Founder-promoter
people.stake: 25.41% as ultimate beneficial owner (FY26 annual report); promoter group about 56.6%
people.bio: Anil Jain, 50, is a commerce graduate who built the Refex group from a refrigerant-gas refiller into a group spanning renewables, ash and coal handling, mobility, pharma, medical technology, airport transport and venture capital. He set up Refex Capital, a Category-I AIF that has backed over 30 start-ups, and was Secretary General of the Jain International Trade Organization. He also sits on the boards of Refex Renewables & Infrastructure, Venwind Refex Power, Refex Green Power, Lee Pharma and Emco. In December 2025 SEBI fined him ₹10 lakh for an alleged 2023 insider-trading breach (stayed on appeal by SAT), and the Income Tax department searched the company that month. His FY26 pay was ₹1.5cr.

people.name: Dinesh Kumar Agarwal
people.since: With the group since 2014; WTD & CFO since 1 June 2024 (earlier non-executive director)
people.bio: Dinesh Agarwal is a chartered accountant with over 22 years in corporate finance, audit, accounting, tax planning and fund-raising; he says he has helped raise over ₹3,000cr of debt and equity. He earlier worked with Aircel and Brisk and advised start-ups, SMEs and NGOs. He joined Refex in 2014 and is also CEO and CFO of Refex Holding, the promoter company, which pays his salary. He moved from non-executive director to WTD & CFO in June 2024.

people.name: Tarun Arora
people.role: Chief Business Officer – Ash & Coal Handling (senior management)
people.bio: Tarun Arora has a B.E. in chemical engineering from Thapar Institute, Patiala (2004) and an executive MBA from SPJIMR, Mumbai (2015). He spent 2011–2022 at Hindustan Zinc and Vedanta as SBU head, silver business head and Chief Commercial Officer, then was VP and Head of Operations at Karam Chand Thapar & Bros. He joined in April 2025 to run the ash and coal business, now the main earner.

people.name: Ankit Poddar
people.bio: Ankit Poddar is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer; like the CFO, his salary is paid by the promoter company Refex Holding. The annual report gives no further background.

companies.changes: Lalitha Uthayakumar moved from President – Refrigerant Gas to GM – Accounts from 1 Aug 2026 after the gas business was shut, and left senior management. Anil S. Kulkarni was named Chief Business Officer (RMC division) and Prasad Jakkaraju VP – ESG in Aug 2026. Jagdish Jain is Business Head – Ash & Coal and Sahil Singla President – Corporate Finance (both senior management since Aug 2025).

companies.styleNote: Promoters own 56.8%: Fairfax (through Fairbridge Capital Mauritius, 34.1%, and HWIC Asia Fund, 0.5%) and the founder Ajit Isaac (12.0% himself plus 10.3% through Isaac Enterprises LLP). Ajit Isaac is the non-executive Chairman; the business is run by a hired Group CEO, Lohit Bhatia, who joined as a sales manager in 2011. No director is related to another.

people.name: Lohit Bhatia
people.since: Joined 2011; CEO from 1 January 2026; Executive Director & Group CEO from 1 June 2026
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in economics, a master's in marketing and sales and an advanced systems diploma in computers. He has over 28 years of experience; before Quess he worked in textiles, auto components and services, in sales, product and business development roles. He joined Quess in 2011 as General Manager – Sales (Staffing) and led the staffing business as it grew from 13,000 to about 4.8 lakh associates, later becoming President – India and Global Operations. He led three overseas acquisitions in the Middle East, Singapore and Sri Lanka, which now give about 20% of group EBITDA. He was President of the Indian Staffing Federation for three terms (2020–2026) and sits on the board of the World Employment Confederation for Southern APAC.

people.name: Neeraj Jain
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary with over 20 years in finance. He was previously global CFO of Startek, then a NYSE-listed customer-experience company working in 12 countries, where he was part of the team that took it private and restructured it. Before that he held finance roles at Microsoft, Tech Mahindra, Comviva and Convergys, also running IT, legal, procurement, risk and compliance teams. He is a member of ASSOCHAM's National Council of CFOs. He replaced Sushanth Pai, who left in October 2025 after about six months.

people.name: Nitin Dave
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Runs the general staffing business, the largest part of Quess by revenue. He has over 25 years of experience and previously held senior sales and marketing roles at TNT Express, G4S and the Tenon Group, working in the Netherlands, Singapore, Vietnam and India.

people.name: Kapil Joshi
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Runs the IT staffing business, which now earns a large share of group profit. He has over 25 years of experience across IT services, workforce solutions and banking and financial services, and is an alumnus of Harvard Business School's Senior Executive Leadership Program. The company does not name his previous employers.

people.name: Sanjay Shetty
people.role: Chief Business Officer – Recruitment, GCC and International Services
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Leads recruitment, services for global capability centres and the overseas businesses. He has over 20 years of leadership experience, including senior roles at Randstad India. He holds a master's in personnel management from Pune University, an MBA in marketing from the Canadian School of Management, and attended INSEAD's Senior Executive Program.

people.name: Sunitha Karthikeyan
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Heads HR for teams in India, the US, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, with over 20 years in HR. She spent 16 years at Wipro in roles in India and the Middle East, working on change management, integration after mergers and talent strategy. She holds a postgraduate diploma in HR from Symbiosis Institute of Management, Pune, and completed a general management programme in business finance at IIM Calcutta.

companies.changes: Guruprasad Srinivasan, Group CEO until December 2025, stayed as Executive Director and resigned on 31 May 2026; he now advises the company as a consultant. CFO Sushanth Pai resigned in October 2025 after joining in April 2025. Mohit Mathur (Chief Business Officer, Origint) resigned in January 2026. Fairfax nominee Chandran Ratnaswami left the board on 31 May 2026 and was replaced by Anish Thurthi.

companies.styleNote: There has been no promoter since the private-equity owner Baring sold out in 2023–24; the largest holders are funds. The company is run by Rajiv Kaul, a hired CEO since 2009 who now owns 6.4% through stock options. The board has a non-executive chairperson and two non-executive non-independent directors; no director is related to another.

people.name: Rajiv Kaul
people.role: Executive Vice Chairman, Whole-time Director & CEO
people.stake: 6.43% (1,05,78,702 shares at 31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); built up mainly through stock options
people.bio: Holds a computer science degree from Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, and a PGDM from XLRI. He was Managing Director of Microsoft India, becoming its CEO at 33, and was later a private-equity partner at Actis Capital in London. He has run CMS since 2009, taking it through its 2021 IPO and the promoter's exit, and growing it into India's largest ATM cash-management company with managed services, remote monitoring and software businesses. He was paid about ₹9.8cr in FY26 (salary and bonus, excluding options). He also mentors start-up founders and invests in early-stage B2B technology companies.

people.name: Pankaj Khandelwal
people.since: CFO of the predecessor CMS Computers from May 2006; with CMS Info Systems since July 2009
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a commerce degree from the University of Rajasthan. He joined the group as CFO of CMS Computers in May 2006 and moved to CMS Info Systems when the business was separated in 2009. He is responsible for finance, legal and secretarial work, and attended every audit committee meeting in FY26. He has been CFO through the 2021 IPO, the promoter's exit, the 2026 buyback and the recent acquisitions (Securens, FSS Managed Services).

people.name: Anush Raghavan
people.since: Joined October 2009; Chief Business Officer from July 2025
people.bio: Holds a law degree from the University of Mysore and a PGDM from IIM Ahmedabad. He has spent about 17 years at CMS and built the cash logistics business into the market leader as its President. In July 2025 his role was widened to Chief Business Officer, driving sales across all business lines after a restructuring that brought the businesses under one leadership. He is President of the Cash Logistics Association and the Currency Cycle Association, industry bodies that work with the RBI and banks on standards.

people.name: Puneet Bhirani
people.bio: Holds an engineering degree from Punjab Engineering College, a master's in marketing from S. P. Jain Institute of Management & Research, and attended Wharton's Advanced Management Program. He spent over 18 years at Mphasis in sales, operations and shared services, sat on its executive council and was CEO of its US subsidiary Digital Risk. He then ran Ola Fleet as CEO, became COO of Ola Cabs and worked on setting up the Ola Electric gigafactory, and was COO of Byju's, where he built its hybrid learning centres. At CMS he runs service delivery and operations across all business lines.

people.name: Rajeev Bhatia
people.bio: Heads technology at CMS and is listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company does not publish his education or earlier career, so no further detail is given here.

companies.changes: Chief Human Resource Officer Sanjay Singh retired on 31 March 2026; Saurabh Chaudhuri, Senior VP and Head of HR, now leads HR. Chief Marketing Officer Pankaj Rawat left in April 2025 and stays on as an adviser. Will Poole, a former Microsoft executive, joined as an independent director in August 2026.

companies.styleNote: A government company under the Ministry of Steel; the President of India owns 64.75%. There is no family promoter: the Chairman & MD and the two functional directors (finance and commercial) are appointed by the government, and a Ministry of Steel official sits on the board as a nominee. No director is related to another.

people.name: Manobendra Ghoshal
people.bio: An engineer from the Indian Railways Service of Mechanical Engineers (SCRA 1985 batch), with a bachelor's in engineering from the Institution of Engineers (India), of which he is a Fellow. He spent 23 years in Indian Railways in workshop management, rolling-stock operation and design, then 10 years at RITES, the last two as Chief Strategy Officer, where he worked on restructuring and led exports of trainsets and coaches to Sri Lanka worth over $200 million. He took charge of MSTC in January 2024 and oversaw the closure of its trading (marketing) business from FY27. He also chairs Mahindra MSTC Recycling, the 50:50 scrapping joint venture.

people.name: Subrata Sarkar
people.since: Joined MSTC May 2001; on the board since 1 December 2018
people.bio: A chartered accountant (ICAI associate) with a BSc (Honours) from Bhagalpur University. Before MSTC he was a partner at Sarkar Mitra & Mitra, chartered accountants. He joined MSTC in May 2001 and has spent his career in its finance and accounts function, becoming Director (Finance) and CFO in December 2018. He is also a director of the Mahindra MSTC Recycling joint venture.

people.name: Bhanu Kumar
people.bio: Holds a master's in science from the University of Delhi and a management degree. She has spent more than three decades at MSTC in trading, contracts, commercial operations, recycling and e-commerce, and the company highlights her experience in digitising commercial transactions. As Director (Commercial) she oversees all business operations and business development.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the annual report. Government nominee director Sudershan Mendiratta was replaced by Santosh, Statistical Adviser at the Ministry of Steel, in August 2026. Independent director Ramesh Kumar Soni's term ended in April 2026; two new independent directors (Siraiong Singpho and Niwas Mandal) joined in July 2026.

companies.styleNote: SEBI has classed Redington as a listed company with no promoter since July 2019. Its largest holder is Taiwan's Synnex Technology (24.1%), which has 'significant influence' but does not run it; HDFC Mutual Fund holds 9%. The chairman is a non-executive, non-independent director, and a hired MD & Group CEO runs the business. No director is related to another.

people.name: V S Hariharan
people.since: Group CEO from 11 September 2023; MD & Group CEO from 5 February 2025 (to 2030)
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in mechanical engineering from IIT Madras and an MBA from IIM Bangalore. He spent about three decades in sales, marketing and general management, including at Wipro Infotech and in global and Asia-Pacific leadership roles at Hewlett-Packard, where he grew its printer business. He then founded Third Wave Power (Third Wave Power Pte Ltd), a seller of solar lighting products to off-grid rural homes that reached over 6 million customers; Redington lists it as a related party in which he has an interest. He was an independent director of Redington until he resigned on 1 September 2023 to become Group CEO, and joined the board as MD in 2025. He is paid by an overseas subsidiary, so his pay is not disclosed in the Indian report.

people.name: S V Krishnan
people.since: On the board since 22 May 2019; re-appointed to May 2031
people.bio: Before Redington he worked at Ashok Leyland. He has been with Redington since before its 2007 listing and worked on its equity raising and IPO. He has been a whole-time director designated Finance Director since May 2019 and is the group's global CFO. The board re-appointed him for five more years from May 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Ramesh Natarajan
people.since: At Redington about 28 years; CEO – India & Middle East from 1 July 2025
people.bio: A long-serving Redington executive with more than 28 years at the company in IT distribution. As CEO of Redington India he built its consumer and enterprise businesses, moved into new segments and set up key vendor partnerships. From July 2025 he runs both India and the Middle East, the group's two largest markets, and is a KMP.

people.name: Rajat Vohra
people.since: 1 July 2025 (previously Chief Sales Officer, Redington India)
people.bio: Has over 20 years in business development, sales strategy and sales leadership across consumer and enterprise products. Before Redington he held senior roles at HP Inc., Samsung and Shell, and was Country General Manager for India and South Asia at Newell Brands. He joined as Chief Sales Officer for Redington India and was promoted to run Indian operations in July 2025.

people.name: V Ravi Shankar
people.bio: Joined Redington in 2002 from EY's business advisory practice. He has over 20 years of experience in advisory work, due diligence, valuation, investigations, mergers and acquisitions, GST implementation and SAP systems. He is a KMP and signs the CEO/CFO certificate with the Group CEO.

people.name: Serkan Çelik
people.role: CEO – Turkey, Africa, Egypt and CIS
people.since: At Arena Group (Redington Turkey) since 2007; its CEO since 2018
people.bio: Studied at Istanbul University's School of Economics and attended Harvard Business School's General Management Program. He was a tax, financial law and accounting consultant at PwC from 1998 to 2007, then joined Arena, Redington's Turkish arm, as CFO in 2007 and became CEO in 2018. He chairs its subsidiaries Paynet and Arena Mobile. The Turkish business is currently loss-making, so his results matter to group profit.

companies.changes: No executive exits since the annual report. Ramesh Natarajan and Rajat Vohra were promoted in July 2025. Ajay Rotti joined as an independent director in June 2026.

companies.styleNote: Co-founders Manish Sabharwal and Ashok Reddy are the promoters: jointly 25.27% through HR Offshoring Ventures, plus 7.15% (Reddy, via NED Consultants) and 0.86% (Sabharwal, via Hansini) — about a third in all. In February 2026 the company moved from founder-led to board-managed: Suparna Mitra, hired from Titan, became MD & CEO; Ashok Reddy stayed as Executive Vice Chairman; Manish Sabharwal became a non-executive director. The chairman, Narayan Ramachandran, is a non-executive former independent director. The founders are not related.

people.name: Suparna Mitra
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in electrical engineering from Jadavpur University and an MBA from IIM Calcutta. She began as a management trainee at Hindustan Lever and was business head for Lee at Arvind Brands. She joined Titan in 2006 as global marketing head and rose to CEO of its Watches & Wearables division, which doubled revenue in three years to about ₹4,500cr in FY25 and built a wearables business. She has over 30 years of experience and has led teams of over 3,000 people. She is an independent director of Swiggy and on the board of governors of IIM Kozhikode. Early on she withdrew the 'over 20%' EBITDA growth target, saying it may or may not be met.

people.name: Ashok Reddy
people.since: Co-founder, 2002; MD until 1 February 2026; Executive Vice Chairman since 2 February 2026 (term to August 2030)
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter
people.stake: Nil direct; 7.15% through NED Consultants LLP plus a share of the 25.27% held by HR Offshoring Ventures (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds a commerce degree from Shri Ram College of Commerce, Delhi, and a diploma in management from IIM Bangalore. Before TeamLease he co-founded India Life Pension Services, a payroll and pension firm sold to Hewitt Associates in 2002. He co-founded TeamLease in 2002 and led it for about 24 years, through its 2016 listing, the 2008 recession and the pandemic, and into apprenticeships, specialised staffing, HR technology, compliance technology and education. He now focuses on long-term strategy, partnerships and cross-business projects, and still represents the company with major clients.

people.name: Ramani Dathi
people.role: Chief Financial Officer & Chief Operating Officer
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant with a commerce degree and a diploma in information systems audit. She worked in audit and assurance at Deloitte and PwC before joining TeamLease as financial controller in 2014. She became Deputy CFO and took over the finance function in April 2021, and is now CFO and COO. She is a key voice on earnings calls, explaining margins, cash and client exits.

people.name: Neeti Sharma
people.since: About 20 years in the TeamLease group
people.bio: Holds an MA from SNDT Women's University. She has been with the TeamLease group for about 20 years, co-founding TeamLease EdTech with Shantanu Rooj and leading TeamLease Skills University. She now runs TeamLease Digital, the IT and specialised staffing arm, which earns higher margins than general staffing.

people.name: Vamsikrishna Ithamraju
people.bio: Joined in January 2026 to lead digital transformation and technology for the employment businesses. He has over 20 years in technology leadership across financial services, fintech, capital markets and consulting, most recently as CTO of Axis Mutual Fund, where he led large technology teams and built its digital platforms.

companies.changes: Founder Ashok Reddy handed the MD & CEO role to Suparna Mitra on 2 February 2026, and Manish Sabharwal moved from Executive Vice Chairman to non-executive director the same day. Navin Patil was made Head of HR in May 2026. Independent directors were re-appointed for a second term by postal ballot in June 2026.

companies.styleNote: Control sits with Reco Berry Pvt Ltd of Singapore, which owns 63.92% and names two non-executive directors, both with GIC backgrounds. The original Sagar family are also promoters, and Rahul Sagar, brother of promoter Kunal Sagar, runs the company as Executive Director & CEO. The company has only three employees, all KMP; the office park is run through Nirlon Management Services, a firm in which Rahul Sagar is a director and member, and which was paid about ₹28cr in FY26 — the auditor's key audit matter. The chairman, Rajinder Pal Singh, is independent.

people.name: Rahul V. Sagar
people.since: Director since June 2006; Executive Director since 1 July 2009; also CEO since 12 November 2018; re-appointed to January 2031
people.relation: Promoter; brother of promoter Kunal V. Sagar
people.stake: 13,29,750 shares, about 1.5% (FY26 annual report); Reco Berry separately holds 63.92%
people.bio: Holds a BA in economics. Before joining Nirlon he was Chief Operating Officer of Sempertrans Nirlon Pvt Ltd. He joined the board in June 2006, became Executive Director in July 2009 and was also made CEO in November 2018, running the Nirlon Knowledge Park office campus in Goregaon, Mumbai. He was paid ₹3.04cr gross in FY26. He is a member and director of Nirlon Management Services, the related party that manages the park, which is why the promoters abstain from approving those contracts. He holds no other listed or public company directorships.

people.name: Manish B. Parikh
people.bio: A commerce graduate with 41 years of experience. The annual report gives 1 April 2023 as the start of his current employment and lists Nirlon itself as his previous employer. He is one of only three employees, all of whom are KMP; he was paid ₹1.27cr gross in FY26.

companies.changes: No change in KMP in FY26 or since. Rahul Sagar was re-appointed for five years from 1 February 2026 at the September 2025 AGM.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 1989 by the late Chandrakant P. Sanghvi. His son Rishi Sanghvi is Managing Director and owns 28.8%; with his mother Mina (11.6%), Niyoshi C. Sanghvi (5.8%) and his wife Maithili (1.0%), the promoter group holds about 47%. Maithili Sanghvi sits on the board as a non-executive director. The company says it is moving from promoter-led to professionally managed: it hired its first CEO (Gaurang Desai) in 2025 plus a new CFO and COO, but the MD still leads.

people.name: Rishi C. Sanghvi
people.since: MD since 2019; re-appointed for five years from 11 April 2024
people.relation: Promoter; son of founder the late C. P. Sanghvi and Mina Sanghvi; husband of director Maithili Sanghvi
people.stake: 28.82% (2,49,50,494 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group about 47%
people.bio: Holds a BS in mechanical engineering with a minor in economics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, New York, and an MBA from Cornell University. The company describes his experience as spanning business development, maintenance, heavy-lift and technical support, imports, logistics, purchasing and land acquisition. He became MD in 2019; since then the company has grown from crane hire into wind and project EPC and overseas work, including a Saudi Arabian subsidiary, under its 'Elevate 2030' plan. He was paid ₹6.46cr in FY26, above the listing-rule limit for promoter directors, so shareholders were asked to ratify it at the 2026 AGM. He is also MD of the renewables subsidiary Sangreen Future Renewables.

people.name: Gaurang Desai
people.bio: Has over 20 years in leadership roles across industries, with a focus on P&L management, growth and operations. He previously held senior roles at UMSL, Jindal Poly, Parksons Packaging and Welspun Corp, where he worked on business expansion, SAP roll-outs, backward integration in manufacturing, international expansion and automation. He is the first hired CEO and a KMP, and is not related to any director. The company does not disclose his education.

people.name: Pradeep Mehta
people.bio: A chartered accountant with over 30 years in finance and business leadership at multinationals and listed companies; the company does not name his earlier employers. He replaced Sham Kajale, a former Joint MD who stayed on as CFO until June 2025. He oversees funding of the large capex plan, including rupee and dollar loans for India and Saudi Arabia.

people.name: Saumil Dave
people.bio: Holds a commerce degree from Mumbai University, with certificates in marketing and management from Ryerson University, Canada, and in project management. He previously worked at IFS Logistics, Canadian Tire Corporation, Quantum Mail Logistics Solutions India and Flipkart. He was appointed COO and senior management in April 2026.

people.name: Mohammed Almanaseer
people.role: Managing Director, Sanghvi Movers Middle East
people.bio: Runs the Saudi Arabian subsidiary, where about half of FY27 capex is going. He has over 25 years of international supply-chain and operations experience in automotive, heavy machinery, construction and healthcare, and holds a PhD in supply chain management and optimisation and a master's in industrial and manufacturing systems engineering.

companies.changes: CFO Sham Kajale resigned in June 2025 (Pradeep Mehta from August 2025); company secretary Rajesh Likhite left in August 2025 (Vinav Agarwal replaced him). Saumil Dave joined as COO in April 2026. Independent director Amitabha Mukhopadhyay resigned on 7 September 2026, citing other commitments.

companies.styleNote: Run by its two founders: Umesh Kumar Sahay is Chairman & MD and owns 38.7%; co-founder Abhishek Narbaria (20.5%) is a non-executive director who leads group operations. Promoters hold 60.4% after the merger share issue. Both founders also sit on, and run, the related listed companies TCC Concept (Sahay is MD) and Belding India (Narbaria is MD), with which EFC deals. The board says no director is related to another. Sahay's pay rose 1,245% in FY26 and Narbaria's 880%.

people.name: Umesh Kumar Sahay
people.relation: Founder and promoter
people.stake: 38.74% (5,31,83,250 shares at 31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoters together 60.44%
people.bio: A first-generation entrepreneur with an MBA from Pune and over 20 years in real estate, data-centre infrastructure and IT/ITeS. He built EFC into a managed-office, design-and-build and office-furniture business and has won awards such as Outlook Business's CEO of the Year (2022) and Times 40 under 40 (2022). He is also MD of TCC Concept and a non-executive director of Belding India and Capfin India. His pay rose 1,245% in FY26 to about 179 times the median employee's; shareholders approved it with 97.5% of votes cast.

people.name: Nikhil Dilipbhai Bhuta
people.since: Re-appointed for five years from 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2030
people.bio: A chartered accountant with over 25 years of entrepreneurial and leadership experience, including roles as CFO, country head and CEO. He has worked in real estate, infrastructure, hospitality, agritech, mining and oil and gas, in India and abroad, and has helped companies raise capital on the BSE, the Toronto Stock Exchange and London's AIM. The company does not name his earlier employers.

people.name: Uday Tushar Vora
people.since: CFO as of the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Holds a master's in finance from Symbiosis International University, Pune, and has over ten years of experience in finance and corporate management. He runs financial strategy, treasury, internal controls, risk management and reporting. The company has no credit rating and converts only about 29% of operating profit to cash, so the finance function is under scrutiny.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the annual report. The statutory auditor resigned in April 2026 and a new internal auditor was appointed in May 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Amit Ramani is Chairman & MD and the only promoter left, owning about 17% (Peak XV was reclassified from promoter to public in 2025). He appointed a CEO, Sumit Lakhani, in May 2025 to run day-to-day operations, but remains the executive chairman. No director is related to another.

people.name: Amit Ramani
people.relation: Founder and sole promoter
people.stake: 17.0% (1,21,63,084 shares at 31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); no stock options
people.bio: An architect by training, with a master's in architecture from Kansas State University and a master's in real estate and workplace strategy from Cornell University. He founded Awfis in 2015 and built it into India's largest flexible-workspace network by centres, with a design-and-build arm (Transform), and took it public in 2024. He was named Entrepreneur of the Year – Real Estate at the ET Entrepreneur Summit and one of The Economic Times' Most Promising Business Leaders of Asia 2019–20. His holding rose slightly in FY26 (from 1.21 to 1.22 crore shares).

people.name: Sumit Lakhani
people.bio: Holds an MBA from S. P. Jain Centre of Management. Before Awfis he worked in investment banking at Yes Bank, at Tesco, and at ST Asset Management in Singapore. As CEO he runs the P&L, business operations and customer initiatives. He has been named CXO of the Year and appeared in Realty+'s '40 Under 40'.

people.name: Sumit Rochlani
people.bio: A chartered accountant (ICAI, 2009) with an IFRS diploma from ACCA and about 15 years in finance. He previously worked at Boeing India, Stryker India and PwC, across audit, controllership, planning and analysis, corporate finance and indirect tax. He replaced Ravi Dugar, who resigned as CFO in January 2026.

people.name: Manu Dhir
people.bio: Has over 25 years of experience and joined Awfis in its founding year, 2015, leading expansion and operations. He previously held leadership roles at The Oberoi Group and worked in hospitality, entertainment and healthcare. He focuses on technology-led customer experience and operating efficiency across the centres.

people.name: Deepayan Sen
people.bio: With Awfis since 2015, he handles supply strategy — signing new buildings and landlord partnerships — and growth forecasting. He has over 16 years in real estate, with earlier roles at Staples Future Office Products, METRO Cash & Carry India, Pantaloon Retail and Radhakrishna Consumer Services.

companies.changes: CFO Ravi Dugar resigned (left 2 February 2026); Sumit Rochlani took over on 3 February 2026. Non-executive director Arjun Shanker Bhartia resigned on 9 April 2026; Abhishek Poddar joined as an independent director in July 2026.

companies.styleNote: The Lad family controls and runs the company. Krystal Family Holdings owns 69.96%; the family directors hold only nominal shares directly. Neeta Prasad Lad is Chairperson & MD, and her daughter Saily and son Shubham are whole-time directors. Prasad Minesh Lad holds a paid 'Chief Mentor' office (a related-party appointment up for renewal at the 2026 AGM). A hired CEO, Sanjay Dighe, sits on the board as a whole-time director. The chair is executive and a promoter, so half the board is independent.

people.name: Neeta Prasad Lad
people.since: Director since 1 April 2006; re-appointment proposed at the 2026 AGM
people.relation: Promoter; mother of whole-time directors Saily and Shubham Lad
people.stake: 2 shares directly (nil %); family holds 69.96% through Krystal Family Holdings (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds an executive MBA in finance management from the Indian School of Business Management and Administration. She has been with the company since April 2006 and oversees its overall business operations and the planning and delivery of workforce welfare for its roughly 42,000 on-site workers. She chairs the CSR committee. She, Saily and Shubham Lad and Prasad Lad have given personal guarantees on the company's bank loans.

people.name: Sanjay Suryakant Dighe
people.bio: A mechanical engineer who spent most of his earlier career with the Aditya Birla Group. He joined Krystal's board in December 2010 and as CEO runs core business management, long-term growth and strategic planning. He is also the board's nodal person for audit and financial reporting matters, and retires by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Saily Prasad Lad
people.relation: Promoter; daughter of the Chairperson & MD; sister of Shubham Lad
people.bio: Holds a BA in strategic management and consulting from Nottingham Trent University and an MSc in business consulting from Royal Holloway, University of London. She has been on the board since October 2015 and is involved in key business decisions and in setting and executing strategy.

people.name: Shubham Prasad Lad
people.relation: Promoter; son of the Chairperson & MD; brother of Saily Lad
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in business management (HRM) from Royal Holloway and Bedford New College, University of London. He has been with the company since March 2019 and contributes to its strategic direction.

people.name: Pravin Ramesh Lad
people.relation: Classed as an executive (non-promoter) director; the company reports no family relationship with other directors
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in management studies (HRM) and an executive master's in business (operations management) from the Indian School of Business Management and Administration. On the board since October 2009, he oversees government and special-projects operations — the hospital, school, airport and municipal contracts that make up most of the business.

people.name: Barun Dey
people.bio: The KMP in charge of finance and the main contact for the statutory auditors. The company does not publish his education or earlier career. Since August 2026 a Joint CFO has worked alongside him; in the same period receivables reached 118 days and CRISIL cut the rating to BBB+ (negative).

people.name: Naveen Kumar Amar
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary with a PGDM in financial management and over 28 years in finance, treasury and governance. He has worked at SpiceXpress, MSD Wellcome Trust Hilleman, GE India, Marconi Telecommunications, Quatroo BPO Solutions and eDirect, most recently as a virtual CFO with Practus and interim CFO of Collective Newsroom. His strengths are fund-raising, project finance and IPO readiness.

companies.changes: Naveen Kumar Amar joined as Joint CFO on 5 August 2026. Company secretary Stuti Maru left in January 2026 (Manishkumar Sangani replaced her). There were several senior-management changes in FY26, including new presidents for business development and group operations. In May 2026 the board proposed re-appointing the MD and whole-time directors.

companies.styleNote: Founder Raghunandana Tangirala is Chairperson & MD. His daughter-in-law Jigyasa Sharma is a whole-time director. The Tangirala family owns 59.1%: Raghunandana 24.1%, Shanthi Tangirala 20.0%, Tangi Facility Solutions 10.7%, Anjan Sarma 3.5% and Jigyasa Sharma 0.75%. In April 2026 former non-executive director Amitabh Jaipuria became a full-time Senior Executive Director. The finance chief has changed three times in a year.

people.name: Raghunandana Tangirala
people.since: Founding director since incorporation (2003); CMD term to December 2026, re-appointment to 2031 proposed
people.relation: Founder and promoter; father-in-law of whole-time director Jigyasa Sharma
people.stake: 24.12% (1,61,52,010 shares, FY26 annual report); family and group together 59.1%
people.bio: A first-generation entrepreneur with a commerce degree from the University of Madras and decades in integrated facilities management. He is one of the founding directors and has been on the board since the company was set up, focusing on governance, organisation building, capital allocation and strategy. He took the company public in 2023 and led its acquisitions, which include the material subsidiary Denave India. He draws ₹1.92cr a year, and the board has proposed a new five-year term from January 2027, during which he will turn 70.

people.name: Amitabh Jaipuria
people.since: Non-executive director earlier; Senior Executive Director from 1 April 2026 for three years
people.bio: Has over 37 years across FMCG, telecom, financial services, industrial products, agriculture and business services, including roles as CEO, managing director and president at Indian and multinational companies. As a non-executive director of UDS he worked on strategy, M&A, investor relations and governance, and led the 2023 listing. He was founding CEO of Accelerate India Philanthropy and still advises it pro bono. Shareholders approved his move to a full-time role by postal ballot in June 2026.

people.name: Jigyasa Sharma
people.relation: Promoter group; daughter-in-law of the Chairperson & MD
people.bio: Holds an economics degree from the University of Delhi, a master's in applied economics from the National University of Singapore and a master's in public policy from the University of California, Berkeley. She has worked with senior executives in Asia and the US on economics and policy. At UDS she handles strategy, marketing, branding, people, technology, internal audit and risk governance. Her pay rose to ₹96 lakh a year from July 2025.

people.name: Ram Praveen Radhakrishnan
people.bio: A commerce graduate and chartered accountant with about 23 years in finance across agri-solutions, manufacturing, IT services and banking. He worked at Coromandel International (as corporate controller and CFO of Coromandel Chemicals), Caterpillar India, Cognizant and IndusInd Bank, and completed ISB's Senior Leadership Development Programme. He is the third group CFO in a year, after Radha Ramanujan left in September 2025 and interim CFO Surinder Kumar left in March 2026.

people.name: Rajeev Bhardwaj
people.bio: Holds a commerce degree from the University of Calcutta and has over 38 years in operations, general management, business transitions, sales and facilities management in telecom, retail and facilities services. Before UDS he was Director – Operations (national operations head) at Compass India, running its pan-India operations and revenue and EBITDA targets.

people.name: C. R. Saravanan
people.since: Joined 2016; COO from January 2024; Chief Growth Officer from 12 August 2026
people.bio: Joined UDS in 2016 as Director – Business Operations and was COO from January 2024, running pan-India operations, where the company credits him with productivity and cost gains. As Chief Growth Officer he now owns new business, new services and markets, partnerships, international expansion, bids and pricing, with a mandate to move UDS into higher-margin areas.

companies.changes: Group CFO Radha Ramanujan resigned in September 2025; Surinder Kumar was group CFO from December 2025 to March 2026; Ram Praveen Radhakrishnan took over on 17 March 2026. Rajeev Bhardwaj joined as COO and C. R. Saravanan became Chief Growth Officer on 12 August 2026. Chief HR Officer Samriti Malhotra left on 7 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by the Virwani family's Embassy group: Embassy Buildcon LLP and Karan Virwani together hold 49.35% after the 2025 IPO, and Embassy still has de facto control. Karan Virwani is MD & CEO; his father Jitendra Virwani is the non-executive Chairman. WeWork Global's 1 Ariel Way Tenant holds 15.2% and has a nominee director. About 15% of shares are pledged for promoter-group debt. Many senior managers came from Embassy Property Developments.

people.name: Karan Virwani
people.since: MD & CEO; current terms approved by the board in September 2024 and shareholders in October 2024
people.relation: Promoter; son of Chairman Jitendra Virwani
people.stake: 63,051 shares, about 0.05%, in his own name; with Embassy Buildcon LLP 49.35% (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in business administration from the University of Kent. He started at Lounge Hospitality LLP, a restaurant, club-house and catering start-up that is now a related party of the company, and then worked in the Chairman's Office at Embassy Property Developments. He has over 10 years in real estate and runs WeWork India's operations and growth, taking it to about 1.34 lakh desks and a 2025 listing. He was on the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia list (2019) and was named Entrepreneur of the Year at the ET Business Awards 2025. He has personally guaranteed ₹65cr of one lease, and his pay was raised in FY26 after a benchmarking study.

people.name: Clifford Noel Lobo
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Bangalore University and a fellow chartered accountant. Before WeWork India he was director of finance and administration at ESPN Digital Media India and director of finance at i2 Technologies India, and earlier worked at Bharti Cellular and SmithKline Beecham Pharmaceuticals. He runs financial strategy, operations and compliance, and was paid ₹1.37cr in FY25.

people.name: Santosh Martin
people.bio: Holds a BSc from Bangalore University and a PGDBA from Xavier Institute of Management & Entrepreneurship, Bangalore. He was chief marketing officer at Bagmane Developers and CEO of Shyamaraju & Company, the flagship of the DivyaSree Group, and earlier worked at JLW (India). He leads sales and revenue strategy and was paid ₹2.37cr in FY25.

people.name: Arnav Singh Gusain
people.bio: A BA graduate of Indira Gandhi National Open University. He was General Manager – Commercial Real Estate at Embassy Property Developments and earlier Head – Commercial and Retail at SJR Prime Corporation. He finds and signs new buildings and runs expansion, design and project management.

people.name: Vinayak Parameswaran
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in electrical and electronics engineering from NIT Calicut and a PGDCM from IIM Calcutta. He was deputy general manager – corporate affairs at Embassy Property Developments before joining. He handles financial strategy, M&A, fund-raising and new projects. VR Partners, a firm in which he is a partner, holds shares in the company.

people.name: Raghuvinder Singh Pathania
people.bio: Holds a BSc from the University of Jammu and completed an MBA programme at Dr. Vikhe Patil Foundation's Institute of Management, Pune. He was Vice President – Sales & Marketing at Divyasree Infrastructure Projects and earlier held roles at Mantri Developers. He oversees member experience and building operations across the centres.

companies.changes: No changes in the MD, CFO or other KMP since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: A founder-run company. Co-founder Rishi Das is Chairman, Executive Director & CEO; his wife Meghna Agarwal is Executive Director & COO; his brother Anshuman Das is a non-executive director. The three promoters own 53.5% (Rishi 15.9%, Meghna 15.9%, Anshuman 21.8%) after selling some shares in the July 2025 IPO. The chairman is also the CEO.

people.name: Rishi Das
people.since: Co-founder; with the company since incorporation (2015)
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; husband of COO Meghna Agarwal; brother of director Anshuman Das
people.stake: 15.85% (3,35,91,373 shares at 31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoters together 53.54%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in electrical engineering from the University of Roorkee (now IIT Roorkee), which gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award. Before IndiQube he co-founded Careernet Technologies, where he was COO, and was CEO of Hirepro Consulting; he also co-founded Hirepro Technologies and Innoprop Spaces, and still sits on all four boards. He built IndiQube into a managed-office platform of about 10.6m sq ft and took it public in July 2025. He and Meghna Agarwal featured in the IDFC FIRST Private & Hurun India list. The board revised his pay in FY26.

people.name: Meghna Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; wife of Chairman & CEO Rishi Das
people.stake: 15.88% (3,36,66,053 shares at 31 March 2026, FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds a postgraduate diploma in executive management from IMT Ghaziabad and passed the company secretary final exam (ICSI) in 2001. She was a vice president at Careernet Technologies and co-founded Ultrafine Minerals before joining IndiQube in 2018. As COO she runs operations, and she is a director of Innoprop Spaces. She has been recognised by Forbes India W-Power, Fortune India and Entrepreneur India.

people.name: Pawan J. Jain
people.since: Joined 11 July 2019 as VP – Finance; now CFO
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a commerce degree from Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati University, Ajmer, and about 22 years in finance. He was head of banking relations at Twenty Fourteen Hotels India, senior VP finance at Vikram Logistic and Maritime Services and Coast Liners, and a partner and audit manager at Anil N. Jain. He joined as vice president of finance in 2019 and now runs the company's finances; the company declined to give Q1 FY27 cash flow until the half-year audit.

people.name: Deepak Dadhich
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in metallurgical engineering from the University of Roorkee. He was a vice president at Hirepro Consulting (a firm Rishi Das ran), a senior project manager at Infosys and a graduate engineer trainee at Hindalco. At IndiQube he heads facilities and building operations and is a KMP.

companies.changes: Company secretary Pranav Ayanath Kuttiyat left on 25 February 2026, and a senior manager (Bhavana S) left the same day; Bhasker Dubey became company secretary on 20 May 2026. No change in the CEO, COO, CFO or CBO.

companies.styleNote: Founder Neetish Sarda is Managing Director and co-founder Harsh Binani, his brother-in-law, is Executive Director. Promoters own about 58%, mostly through NS Niketan LLP (37.0%) and SNS Infrarealty LLP (21.2%), both controlled by Neetish Sarda and Saumya Binani; the founders hold only small amounts in their own names. The chairman, Atul Gautam, is non-executive. The company paid ₹108.7cr in FY26 to a related party, Talbotforce, for housekeeping and security.

people.name: Neetish Sarda
people.since: Founder; re-appointed MD for five years from 8 March 2026
people.relation: Founder and promoter; brother-in-law of Executive Director Harsh Binani
people.stake: About 43,000 shares (0.04%) in his own name (FY26 annual report); controls, with Saumya Binani, NS Niketan LLP (37.0%) and SNS Infrarealty LLP (21.2%)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in science from the University of London. He founded Smartworks and oversees sales, business development, operations, product and technology, building it into one of India's largest managed-campus operators with about 10.4m sq ft running, and took it public in July 2025. He has been named ET Young Entrepreneur of the Year 2026, India's Impactful CEO 2024 by ET Edge, and among the ten youngest founders on the IDFC FIRST Private & Hurun India self-made list. His pay was revised at the 2025 AGM.

people.name: Harsh Binani
people.since: With the company since 2017; current term to 30 September 2027
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; brother-in-law of MD Neetish Sarda
people.bio: Holds a BA (Hons) in economics from Shri Ram College of Commerce, Delhi, and an MBA in finance from the Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University. He worked at McKinsey & Company in Chicago, joined Smartworks as co-founder in 2017, and has about 14 years across consulting and flexible workspaces. He runs finance, investor relations, marketing, HR and support functions.

people.name: Sahil Jain
people.since: Rejoined 2022 (also with the company in its early days)
people.bio: A fellow chartered accountant and company secretary with a commerce degree from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata; he completed an executive programme at IIM Bangalore and two levels of the CFA. He previously worked at Religare Finvest and Vision Comptech. He handles accounting and corporate banking and signs the financial statements as CFO.

people.name: Pratik Ravindra Agarwal
people.bio: Holds a BSc and a diploma in economics from the University of London. With the company since 2016, he runs corporate sales, business development, account management and enterprise leasing, the engine of its large-client growth.

people.name: Anirudh Tapuriah
people.role: Chief of Strategy and Investor Relations
people.bio: A chartered accountant who cleared the ICSI final and IBBI valuation and insolvency exams, and completed IIM Calcutta's executive programme in business management. He spent over 14 years at Shyam Steel, SBI Capital Markets and Grant Thornton before joining in 2021. He handles fund-raising, investor relations, M&A, business finance and strategy.

people.name: Kalpana Devnani
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in computer science and a postgraduate diploma from MDI Gurgaon. She held HR leadership roles at Jubilant FoodWorks, Esme Consumer and ICICI Bank before joining in 2024.

people.name: Siddharth Banerjee
people.bio: Holds a BE in computer science from Visvesvaraya Technological University and has nearly 20 years as a CTO and technical architect, including senior roles at Wowlabs, Cosine Labs and Kandola Network. He leads technology, digital infrastructure and product.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the annual report. Independent directors Rajeev Krishnamuralilal Agarwal (June 2026) and Dilip Deshmukh (September 2026) joined the board.

companies.styleNote: A family company. The founder-promoter Bikramjit Ahluwalia, 87, is Chairman and Managing Director (and signs the accounts as CEO). His son Vikas Ahluwalia and son-in-law Shobhit Uppal are whole-time directors, Uppal as Deputy MD. The promoter group owns 55.3%, the largest holder being his wife Sudershan Walia (30.5%); nothing is pledged. Sanjiv Sharma, an ex-CPWD engineer, is the one non-family executive director.

people.name: Bikramjit Ahluwalia
people.relation: Founder-promoter; father of Vikas Ahluwalia, father-in-law of Shobhit Uppal; husband of promoter Sudershan Walia
people.bio: A civil engineer, aged 87, who has been in construction for more than five decades. The business began in 1965 (his father Karam Chand Ahluwalia is credited as the original founder), and the company was incorporated in 1979, taking over four construction partnerships. He has been Managing Director since 1979 and later Chairman as well. Under him the company grew from Delhi civil works into a national building contractor, with jobs such as the IFCI Tower, the Commonwealth Games village housing, AIIMS hospitals and the Central Vista projects. He is also a director of group companies Capricon Industrials, Ahluwalia Builders & Development Group and Tidal Securities.

people.name: Shobhit Uppal
people.since: With the company since 1994; Deputy MD, reappointed for 2026-2031
people.relation: Son-in-law of Bikramjit Ahluwalia; brother-in-law of Vikas Ahluwalia
people.stake: 6.43% (FY26 annual report); his wife Rachna Uppal holds a further 1.83%
people.bio: An electrical engineering graduate from NIT Kurukshetra, aged 59, with about 32 years in construction across towers, townships, hospitals, hotels, factories and pipelines. The company credits him with leading its big order wins and turning it from a plain civil contractor into an EPC (design-and-build) company. He has overseen the Central Vista projects, several AIIMS and IIM campuses and the Bangalore Metro work. He is a past President of the Indian Buildings Congress, an industry body. He is the highest-paid director (Rs 1.92cr in FY26) and was reappointed from April 2026 to March 2031.

people.name: Vikas Ahluwalia
people.since: With the company since 2002 (in the business since 1996); reappointed for 2026-2031
people.relation: Son of Bikramjit Ahluwalia; brother-in-law of Shobhit Uppal
people.bio: A civil engineer (BE), aged 52, in the construction business since 1996. He chairs the company's Project Monitoring Committee. He has overseen jobs such as Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun, the Mumbai Metro depot, Sion Hospital in Mumbai, the CSMT and Chandigarh station upgrades and the company's Assam projects. He is also a director of several family companies, including Ahlcon Ready Mix Concrete, Capricon Industrials and Tidal Securities. He was reappointed from April 2026 to March 2031.

people.name: Sanjiv Sharma
people.since: Joined August 2019; whole-time director (last reappointed August 2022)
people.bio: Holds a master's in civil engineering (with honours) from IIT Roorkee, aged 57, with about 33 years in construction. He spent 1993 to 2007 in the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) as an engineer-in-charge on government projects. At Ahluwalia he has run the Mumbai and Pune work, including the Mumbai Metro depot, Sion Hospital and the SEBI building at Bandra Kurla Complex. He is not related to any other director.

people.name: Satbeer Singh
people.bio: The company's CFO and a key managerial person; he signs its accounts and the fund-use certificates. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier career. Vipin Kumar Tiwari is GM (Corporate) and Company Secretary.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel found since the FY26 annual report (dated 14 Aug 2026). Senior VP (Finance & Accounts) Bharat Srivastava retired on 31 Mar 2026. The AGM on 29 Sep 2026 votes on reappointing Uppal and Vikas Ahluwalia to 2031.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 2012 by Rahul Katyal with Subir Malhotra; Rahul's brother Rohit Katyal is Executive Chairman. All three founders are executive directors. The promoter group owns 31.69% (March 2026) and part of it is pledged, though pledged shares fell by about 30% in FY26. Rohit Katyal's son Asutosh Katyal works in the company as Chief Technology Officer. After the operations CEO quit in August 2026, the day-to-day work was split into four business units, each under a hired CEO.

people.name: Rahul Katyal
people.since: Founder; director since 9 August 2012; MD reappointed for five years from 4 September 2025
people.relation: Founder-promoter; brother of Executive Chairman Rohit Katyal
people.stake: 9.34% (78,97,953 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 31.69%
people.bio: The founder and promoter, aged 51, with over three decades in civil construction; his formal education listed in the annual report is the Maharashtra higher secondary certificate. He leads strategic planning, business development, client relations and operations, and is the company's highest authority on sustainability matters. He took the company from its 2012 start to one of Mumbai's main builders of high-rise towers, including public-housing contracts. He is also a director of group companies such as Capacit'e Engineering, Katyal Ventures, Katyal Merchandise and TCC Construction. He was paid Rs 3cr in FY26.

people.name: Rohit Katyal
