people.since: Director since 1 March 2014; Chairman since June 2024
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; brother of MD Rahul Katyal; father of CTO Asutosh Katyal
people.stake: 5.91% (50,00,000 shares, FY26 annual report); his wife Sakshi Katyal holds a further 4.49% in her own and joint names
people.bio: A commerce graduate from the University of Mumbai, specialising in financial accounting and auditing, with over three decades in construction and finance. He looks after the finance, commercial and accounts functions, including financial planning, compliance and governance. He was a whole-time director until the board made him Chairman in June 2024. He also chairs the board's CSR committee. He was paid Rs 3cr in FY26.

people.name: Subir Malhotra
people.since: Founding member; director since 9 August 2012; term renewed for five years from November 2026 (subject to AGM approval)
people.relation: Co-founder and named promoter; not related to the Katyals
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree (honours) in civil engineering from BITS Pilani and has over three decades in construction; he is 60. A founding member and promoter, he leads business development and operations, particularly in northern India. He is also a director of group companies Katyal Ventures, Katyal Merchandise, Capacit'e Engineering and the subsidiary CIL MMEPL Ekatha. He was paid Rs 1.8cr in FY26 and lent the company Rs 2.5cr during the year.

people.name: Rajesh Das
people.bio: A finance professional with over two decades in infrastructure, banking and retail, holding an MBA from Deakin University, a postgraduate programme from IMT Ghaziabad and a US CMA qualification. Before Capacit'e he was CFO of the roads business at Reliance Infrastructure (2015 to 2022) and earlier worked at ICICI Bank, Tata Motors Finance and Pantaloon Retail. At Capacit'e he handles corporate finance, treasury and project funding; the company says its borrowing rate fell from about 12.5% to 9.65% over two years as ratings improved. He was paid about Rs 1.23cr in FY26.

people.name: Amit Govil
people.bio: A civil engineer with over 33 years in construction. He has worked at Kalpataru Ltd, Tricon Infra Buildtech, Vascon Engineers and Shapoorji Pallonji, among others. He was elevated from within to run one of the four new business units after the operations CEO left.

people.name: Rakesh Kumar Singh
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate with over 23 years in construction, who has done a senior leadership programme at XLRI. He has worked at B.L. Kashyap & Sons, Shapoorji Pallonji, JMC Infraprojects and Tata Projects, among others. He was elevated from within to run a business unit in September 2026.

people.name: Vishnudas Shanbhag
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in civil engineering from the University of Mysore and a doctorate from Thames International University. He has over three decades in construction, with senior roles at JMC Projects and Godrej & Boyce. He was CEO-Operations at Capacit'e until he resigned in April 2024; the company's September 2026 filing describes him as elevated to head a business unit, so he is back in its ranks.

companies.changes: Rajendra K Jain, Director-Operation & CEO (senior management, not a board member), resigned effective 18 Aug 2026 for personal reasons. On 9 Sep 2026 the board made four business-unit CEOs senior management: Amit Govil, Rakesh Kumar Singh, Vishnudas Shanbhag and a new hire, Ram Mohan Rai (26 years' experience; ex-HCC, R.L. Dalal, Adani Enterprises and an earlier stint at Capacit'e). Independent director Arun Karambelkar died in Nov 2025.

companies.styleNote: The Shah family runs it. Parag K. Shah, who joined the business in 1991 and is the largest holder (29.66%), is now a non-executive Chairman Emeritus; his son Manan P. Shah is Managing Director. The promoter group owns 62.46% with nothing pledged. The board chair has been lawyer Berjis Desai (non-executive), but he is not seeking re-election at the 2026 AGM. The only other executive director is the CFO, Ashok Mehta.

people.name: Manan P. Shah
people.since: Director since May 2014; MD, reappointed at the 2024 AGM
people.relation: Son of Chairman Emeritus and promoter Parag K. Shah
people.stake: 8.74% (3,52,77,245 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 62.46%
people.bio: Holds an International Baccalaureate diploma from RBK International Academy and a BBA (Hons) from Kingston University, London. He runs business development and overall operations, and is closely involved in design and marketing of the group's Mumbai real estate projects, which are now its main business alongside construction contracts. He was on the 2024 Hurun India Under 35 list. He also chairs the board's CSR and risk committees. He was paid Rs 2.5cr in FY26 (Rs 2.9cr in FY25).

people.name: Ashok M. Mehta
people.since: Board since 11 September 2019; current term to September 2029
people.bio: A Fellow chartered accountant and University of Mumbai commerce graduate, aged 62, with over 37 years in finance, accounts, systems and commercial work in India and abroad, mainly in trading and manufacturing companies. Before MICL he was Chief Executive Officer of Doshi & Co. (Hardware) Ltd from 1990 to August 2008. At MICL he oversees finance, accounts, audit, tax and property matters. He is also a director of group companies Man Realtors and Holdings and MICL Realtors. He was paid Rs 1.8cr in FY26 including commission; from April 2026 he gets Rs 1.43cr a year plus 0.5% of consolidated profit.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26 or since. Non-executive chairman Berjis Desai is not seeking reappointment at the 2026 AGM. Rajiv N. Sheth, the group's former Group CFO (retired 2022), joined the board as an independent director on 3 Jul 2026.

companies.styleNote: The founder Prahaladbhai S. Patel is Chairman & MD; his daughter Pooja Patel is CEO and his son Sagar Patel is an executive director. Since August 2025 Adani Infra (India) owns 34.41% and is a co-promoter with joint control; it has a non-executive nominee on the board (Kattunga Srinivasa Rao) and the Adani group supplies most of the order book. The Patel family owns about 34.4% (the founder 22.04% after selling to Adani); all promoters together hold 68.82%.

people.name: Prahaladbhai S. Patel
people.since: Founder; CMD (was also CEO until 5 August 2025)
people.relation: Founder-promoter; father of CEO Pooja Patel and Executive Director Sagar Patel
people.stake: 22.04% (87,35,574 shares, FY26 annual report); Patel family about 34.4%; with co-promoter Adani Infra, 68.82%
people.bio: A first-generation entrepreneur, aged 63, with over 40 years in construction and a civil engineering degree from Lukhdhirji Engineering College, Saurashtra University. He started with a proprietorship doing civil construction before founding PSP Projects in Ahmedabad, and built it into a large Gujarat-based building contractor. His story is told in the book 'Business Game Changers: Shoonya se Shikhar'. In 2025 he sold a large part of his stake to Adani Infra and, under the share purchase and shareholders' agreements, handed the CEO title to his daughter while staying Chairman & MD. He chairs the CSR and ESG committees.

people.name: Pooja P. Patel
people.since: With the company since 2015; CEO since 6 August 2025 (whole-time director until 5 August 2025)
people.relation: Daughter of the founder Prahaladbhai Patel; sister of Sagar Patel
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from L. J. Institute of Engineering and Technology (Gujarat Technological University) and a postgraduate diploma in financial management from the Ahmedabad Management Association. She has been with the company since 2015, working on project planning, execution and strategic buying of raw materials. She resigned as a whole-time director in August 2025 to take the hands-on CEO role when Adani came in. Shareholders approved raising her pay from Rs 3cr to Rs 3.6cr a year at the June 2026 AGM.

people.name: Sagar P. Patel
people.relation: Son of the founder Prahaladbhai Patel; brother of CEO Pooja Patel
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from L. J. Institute of Engineering and Technology (Gujarat Technological University) and has over eight years in construction. He runs the company's precast concrete business, with a focus on bringing in new technology, and also works on project planning, tendering and execution. He was re-elected as a director at the June 2026 AGM. He was paid Rs 2.7cr in FY26.

people.name: Hetal Patel
people.bio: A chartered accountant (ICAI member) with a master's in commerce from Gujarat University, who is also a certified internal auditor (Institute of Internal Auditors, USA). She had 18 years of accounts and finance experience when the company first presented her as CFO in early 2019. She has run the finance function through the Adani deal; her FY26 pay rose 10%.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel since the FY26 annual report (April 2026). The June 2026 AGM re-elected Sagar Patel and approved a pay rise for CEO Pooja Patel and about Rs 5,400cr of related-party contracts with Adani group companies.

companies.styleNote: A family company. The founder Jagdishkumar M. Gupta is Executive Chairman, and his two sons Kamal and Nalin are joint Managing Directors. A long-serving HR executive, Pravin Ghag, is the only non-family whole-time director. Promoters own 46.64%, with no pledge.

people.name: Jagdishkumar M. Gupta
people.relation: Founder; father of Kamal J. Gupta and Dr. Nalin J. Gupta
people.stake: 14.50% (1,09,71,947 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 46.64%
people.bio: He founded the business in 1980 with a first contract worth ₹15,000, and built it into a Mumbai contractor for metros, flyovers, roads, tunnels and marine works with about 7,300 staff. The company's website says he personally oversees every part of its operations. He was earlier Chairman & Managing Director and is now Executive Chairman, a whole-time director re-appointed by shareholders in May 2024. His formal education is not disclosed.

people.name: Kamal J. Gupta
people.since: Re-appointed MD in May 2024; nearly two decades with the company
people.relation: Son of the Chairman; brother of Dr. Nalin J. Gupta
people.bio: He has nearly two decades of experience on the company's projects: flyovers, metros, road over-bridges, expressways and marine works. The company credits him with bringing in segmental construction with overhead launchers and sensor-paver concrete roads. He oversaw the building of a large multi-specialty hospital and flyovers the company describes as the tallest and fastest-built. His formal education is not disclosed.

people.name: Dr. Nalin J. Gupta
people.since: Projects Head from 1996; re-appointed MD in May 2024
people.relation: Son of the Chairman; brother of Kamal J. Gupta
people.bio: A commerce graduate and a member of the Indian Institution of Bridge Engineers. He became Projects Head in 1996. He started the ready-mix concrete division with one plant in Pune and grew it to 16 plants with an R&D centre. He also built the piling division from one rig to 44 hydraulic rigs and set up the tunnelling side, which runs seven tunnel-boring machines.

people.name: Pravin R. Ghag
people.since: With the company about 15 years; on the board since March 2024
people.bio: He has worked at the company for about 15 years in human resources and administration. He has run HR planning, manpower, HR policy, statutory compliance, industrial relations, training and staffing. He joined the board as a whole-time director in March 2024 and is up for re-appointment by rotation at the 2026 AGM. He holds no other directorships. His education is not disclosed in the annual report.

people.name: Vasant Savla
people.bio: A chartered accountant (ICAI, 1993) with over three decades in project accounting, financial management, tax, ERP roll-outs and cost control. Before J. Kumar he worked mainly at Larsen & Toubro, Essar Projects (India) and the audit firm B. P. Jain & Co. The board appointed him CFO on 6 August 2024.

companies.changes: Milind Gopalrao Wani joined as Chief Human Resources Officer (senior management) on 15 September 2026. New statutory auditors (S P M L & Associates) from the 2026 AGM. No change in directors or CFO since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founder S. Kishore Babu is Chairman & MD, and his son Rohit Sajja is a whole-time director and President who runs the main business lines. Promoters own 58.41%. Lakshmi Sajja, a promoter, left the board as a non-executive director in August 2026.

people.name: Sajja Kishore Babu
people.since: 1999 (founder); re-appointed CMD for five years from April 2026
people.relation: Founder; father of Rohit Sajja
people.stake: 24.01% (75,90,884 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 58.41%
people.bio: A mechanical engineering graduate from Nagarjuna University. He spent his first 14 years at Indwell Construction, setting up power plants and rising to joint managing director. He founded Power Mech in 1999; its long ties with BHEL and NTPC gave it a steady flow of power-plant erection work. He has since set up more than a dozen subsidiaries and joint ventures, and he chairs the group. He also runs a charitable trust based in Vijayawada.

people.name: Rohit Sajja
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD
people.bio: He holds a B.Tech in mechanical engineering from VIT, a master's in engineering management from the University of Southern California, and an MBA from the University of Oxford. He joined in 2013 as executive assistant to the CMD and set up the first overseas branch in the UAE. He won the company's first overseas power-plant order in 2014 (Shuqaiq, Saudi Arabia) and worked on the 2015 IPO. He now leads overseas business, operations and maintenance, EPC, mining and renewables. He joined the board as a whole-time director in August 2025.

people.name: N. Nani Aravind Nallamothu
people.bio: He has more than 22 years in senior finance roles in construction and infrastructure. Before Power Mech he worked at BSCPL Infrastructure, B. Srinivasarao & Co, GMR Energy, GKC Projects and KSSR Infra Projects and IJM. His focus is working capital, project finance, bank limits and investor relations. He oversees finance across the whole Power Mech group.

companies.changes: Promoter Lakshmi Sajja resigned as a non-executive director on 8 August 2026. Independent director Lasya Yerramneni finished her term in June 2026 and Vivek Paranjpe retired in August 2026; Vasundhara Sinha joined as an independent director in June 2026. No change in the executive team.

companies.styleNote: Run by four Alluri brothers, the founding family: A A V Ranga Raju is MD, and A G K Raju, A S N Raju and A V N Raju are executive or whole-time directors. A fifth whole-time director, J V Ranga Raju, is in the promoter group but not a legal relative of the others. The board chairman is an independent director (R. M. Malla from May 2026). The promoter group owns only about 23%, most of it through holding companies; the Rare (Jhunjhunwala) group is a large outside holder with a board seat.

people.name: A A V Ranga Raju
people.relation: Promoter; brother of A G K Raju, A S N Raju and A V N Raju
people.bio: He joined the family construction business early in his career and has been Managing Director for more than 30 years. The company credits him with its growth into one of India's largest listed contractors, with a consolidated order book of about ₹83,000cr at March 2026. He has over five decades of experience in construction and infrastructure. His formal education is not disclosed in the annual report or on the website.

people.name: A G K Raju
people.relation: Promoter; brother of A A V Ranga Raju, A S N Raju and A V N Raju
people.bio: Holds an MBA from the University of Pune. A promoter who has been with the company since it began, he joined the board in March 1990. As Executive Director he runs finance, materials management, HR, administration and corporate communications. He has about four decades in construction. He is also a director of NCC Urban Infrastructure, a group company.

people.name: A S N Raju
people.relation: Promoter; brother of A A V Ranga Raju, A G K Raju and A V N Raju
people.bio: He has more than four decades in construction and is known inside the company for project execution. He oversees the Buildings Division and chairs the CSR committee. His formal education is not disclosed.

people.name: A V N Raju
people.since: With the company since 1999; board since June 1999; re-appointed to May 2031
people.relation: Promoter; brother of A A V Ranga Raju, A G K Raju and A S N Raju
people.bio: An undergraduate by qualification (as the AGM notice states), he has about four decades in construction. He heads the Electrical and Irrigation divisions. He also oversees key projects such as the smart-meter contracts and the BharatNet rural broadband programme. The board re-appointed him for five years from 30 May 2026. He is a director of Suguna Holiday Resorts, a private company.

people.name: J V Ranga Raju
people.relation: In the promoter group (holds shares as a promoter) but, per the annual report, not a relative of the other directors
people.bio: He has four decades in the construction industry, and the company says his experience helped make it one of India's leading builders. He also has business interests in hospitality and education. His formal education and role details are not disclosed.

people.name: Sanjay Pusarla
people.bio: A fellow chartered accountant (FCA) with more than 33 years in finance, accounts, audit and tax, mostly at engineering and construction companies. Before NCC he worked at the Shapoorji Pallonji group, Lanco and Rashtriya Ispat Nigam (Vizag Steel Plant). He became CFO and a key managerial person on 1 June 2023.

companies.changes: Kausalya Bhupathi Raju, a promoter-group member, became Director (Commercial) in senior management from 1 September 2026. A. Karthik became Company Secretary on 15 May 2026 after Sisir K. Mishra resigned. Independent chairman A. S. Durga Prasad's term ended on 23 May 2026; R. M. Malla became chairman. Senior EVP (Commercial) N. Bangar Raju died in February 2026.

companies.styleNote: The Tantia family runs every top job. Shree Gopal Tantia is MD and his son Amrit Jyoti Tantia is Director (Projects). Brothers Atul and Vaibhav Tantia, sons of the late chairman D. P. Tantia, are Joint MD & CFO and Director & COO. Non-executive Chairman Dr. Om Tantia, a surgeon, joined the board in September 2025 after D. P. Tantia died. Promoters own 69.37%, 48% of it through GPT Sons, which has pledged shares.

people.name: Shree Gopal Tantia
people.relation: Promoter; father of Amrit Jyoti Tantia
people.stake: 3.96% (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 69.37%, including 48% through GPT Sons
people.bio: A commerce graduate with more than 41 years in infrastructure and civil construction in India and abroad. He heads the group's EPC business and leads client relationships. The company credits him with its reputation for reliable project delivery. He was re-appointed MD at the July 2024 AGM.

people.name: Atul Tantia
people.since: Executive Director & CFO; Joint MD since September 2025
people.relation: Son of the late Chairman D. P. Tantia; brother of Vaibhav Tantia
people.bio: He holds a B.S. in Economics (finance) from the Wharton School and a B.S. in Systems Engineering from the University of Pennsylvania. He has more than 21 years of leadership experience across manufacturing, infrastructure, finance and banking. He runs manufacturing (concrete sleepers), finance and accounts, and handles lenders, investors and overseas customers. He was promoted from Executive Director & CFO to Joint MD & CFO on 24 September 2025.

people.name: Vaibhav Tantia
people.relation: Son of the late Chairman D. P. Tantia; brother of Atul Tantia
people.bio: He holds a bachelor's degree in finance from the Wharton School and a civil engineering degree from the University of Pennsylvania. He has more than 21 years of experience in infrastructure execution, engineering, project management and legal matters. He drives the EPC segment's project execution and growth and handles legal and arbitration matters. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Amrit Jyoti Tantia
people.relation: Son of the MD, Shree Gopal Tantia
people.bio: He holds a commerce degree in marketing management from St. Xavier's College and a master's in management, organisations and governance from the London School of Economics. He has more than 11 years of experience in infrastructure in India and abroad. He monitors key project execution, including client dealings and material buying. His current term as a whole-time director began in May 2024.

companies.changes: Chairman D. P. Tantia died on 17 August 2025; Dr. Om Tantia became non-executive Chairman on 24 September 2025, and Atul Tantia was made Joint MD & CFO the same day. No executive changes since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Formerly ITD Cementation. The Adani group bought control from Italian-Thai Development in 2025 and owns 67.46% through Renew Exim DMCC. The company is run by a career insider, MD Jayanta Basu, who joined as a trainee in 1986. The chairman, Dr. Malay Mahadevia, and director K. S. Rao are non-executive Adani executives. No director is related to another.

people.name: Jayanta Basu
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate from Bengal Engineering College (now IIEST Shibpur), Calcutta University, with over 40 years in heavy civil engineering, project and contracts management. He joined the company as a graduate engineer trainee in 1986, rose to Chief Operating Officer in 2017 and became MD on 23 April 2019. He is a specialist in marine structures and led the company's growth in revenue, profit and overseas work. He has served on the National Council of the Construction Federation of India. He stayed on as MD after the Adani takeover in 2025.

people.name: Nitesh Sharma
people.role: Joint Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer
people.bio: A chartered accountant with more than 23 years of post-qualification experience. He came from the Adani group, where he was Associate Vice President and Finance Controller at Adani Connex. There he handled financial reporting, planning, project finance and borrowing, treasury, capex, contract negotiation, budgeting and tax. He replaced the long-serving CFO Prasad Patwardhan as part of the Adani takeover and became CFO in mid-June 2025.

companies.changes: Abizer Diwanji joined as an independent director on 29 April 2026. Independent director Pankaj Jain died in March 2026. No change in the MD or CFO since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Since CMD Rupen Patel died in July 2024 (and founder Pravin Patel in July 2025), no family member holds an executive role. Janky Patel of the promoter family is non-executive Chairperson. The company is run by a hired MD, Kavita Shirvaikar, formerly its CFO. Promoters own 31.49%, most of it pledged. No director is related to another.

people.name: Kavita Shirvaikar
people.since: On the board since April 2017; MD since August 2024
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant (ICWAI) with over 28 years in finance, infrastructure and strategy. She joined Patel Engineering as Vice President (Finance) and joined the board in April 2017. As CFO and whole-time director she handled treasury, debt restructuring and equity raising, and she oversaw key project sites. The company calls her the architect of its financial turnaround. She became MD after Rupen Patel died, and the company credits her with keeping its sites running without disruption. She is also a director of Patel KNR Infrastructures and several group hydro-power companies.

people.name: Kishan Lal Daga
people.bio: A civil engineer with more than 50 years of experience in India and abroad, including work in Dubai, Tashkent, Muscat, Mauritius and Mozambique. He was president of the Indo African Chamber of Commerce and Industries for about 12 years. He joined in November 2005 as Special Director – Projects and now heads Contracts, handling all contractual, legal and arbitration matters across the project portfolio.

people.name: R V R Kishore
people.bio: Holds a B.E. in Construction from Shivaji University (1989, first class with honours) and a Diploma Masters in Construction Management from NICMAR, Mumbai. He has more than 35 years in tunnelling, marine, power, EPC, BOT and PPP projects. He previously held CXO-level roles at other infrastructure companies and managed a project portfolio of over ₹40,000cr. He joined the board as whole-time director for operations for three years from 22 September 2025.

people.name: Rahul Agarwal
people.bio: He took over as CFO on 6 July 2024, when Kavita Shirvaikar moved up after the CMD's death. He also chairs a board-level management committee. The annual report and company website do not give his education or past employers.

companies.changes: Founder and Chairman Emeritus Pravin Patel died on 1 July 2025. Senior management member Dimitrius D'Mello resigned in May 2025. Independent directors Sunanda Rajendran and Ashwin Parmar left in March–April 2026 at the end of their terms; Sudha Navandar joined in March 2026. No executive change since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: The Shapoorji Pallonji group owns 50.17%, all of it pledged against group debt, but no Mistry family member is an executive. Shapoorji Mistry moved from Chairman to Chairman Emeritus in August 2025; family members sit on the board only as non-executive directors. The company is run by two long-serving hired executives who joined in 2002: Executive Chairman S. Krishnamurthy and MD P. Srinivasan. No executive is related to another.

people.name: Subramanian Krishnamurthy
people.since: Board since November 2002; Executive Chairman since 28 August 2025; re-appointed to June 2028
people.stake: 0.04% (1,30,150 shares, FY26 annual report); also 4,67,289 ESOPs
people.bio: Holds a B.E. (Hons) in mechanical engineering from Regional Engineering College, Trichy (University of Madras) and a postgraduate diploma in industrial engineering from NITIE. He has over four decades in project planning, execution, contracts and corporate planning. He was Afcons' MD from 2002 to 2018, then Executive Vice Chairman, and became Executive Chairman in August 2025. He holds an honorary D.Litt. from KIIT and won the Construction World Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025. The board kept him on to 2028 partly to handle large arbitration cases.

people.name: Srinivasan Paramasivan
people.since: Board since June 2002; re-appointed MD to June 2028
people.stake: 0.03% (98,222 shares, FY26 annual report); also 3,73,831 ESOPs
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Madurai University, a fellow of the Institute of Cost Accountants and the Institute of Company Secretaries, a CAIIB, and a Stanford Certified Project Manager. He has over four decades in infrastructure, with a background in banking, finance and business development. As MD he runs day-to-day operations, finance, commercial matters and order winning. He co-chairs FICCI's roads and highways committee and sits on the Construction Skill Development Council of India. He was re-appointed for two years from July 2026.

people.name: Giridhar Rajagopalan
people.stake: 0.01% (20,385 shares, FY26 annual report); also 2,49,221 ESOPs
people.bio: A civil engineer from Sardar Patel College of Engineering, Mumbai, with over 46 years of experience. Before Afcons he worked at Peninsula Land (Ashok Piramal group) and V Karma Capital (DLF). He heads technical functions: planning, design, construction methods, quality, safety, training and knowledge management, and handles technically difficult projects. He led the company's lean-construction and knowledge-management drive, which won global MAKE and MIKE awards. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Ramesh Kumar Jha
people.bio: He is the company's CFO and a key managerial person, and co-signs the accounts and the CEO/CFO certificate with the MD. There was no change in KMPs during FY26. The annual report does not give his education or past employers.

companies.changes: Sandeep Badhe became Business Unit Head – Oil & Gas on 6 February 2026, replacing Ashwini Kumar Venkatesh, who stepped down. No change in the executive directors or CFO since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: A Sethi family company. The Sethi brothers have stepped back to non-executive roles: Subhash Chand Sethi (Chairman, formerly whole-time director) and Sushil Sethi (Vice Chairman). A younger family member, Abhinandan Sethi, became MD in September 2025. The annual report says these three are related to one another. Finance is run by a hired executive director and CFO, Manoj Digga. Promoters own 40.51%, mostly through group companies, and a lender (NARCL) has a nominee director.

people.name: Abhinandan Sethi
people.since: Chief Operating Officer until September 2025; MD since 3 September 2025
people.relation: Member of the Sethi promoter family (reclassified as a promoter in FY26); related to Chairman Subhash Chand Sethi and Vice Chairman Sushil Sethi
people.stake: nil directly (July 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 40.51%
people.bio: An alumnus of La Martiniere School, Kolkata, with a B.Sc. in Business Administration from Boston University and an MBA from London Business School. He was the company's Chief Operating Officer before becoming MD on 3 September 2025. As MD he runs strategy, operations and corporate finance, and leads the push into new areas such as battery energy storage (BESS). He also guides project management and company policies.

people.name: Manoj Kumar Digga
people.since: CFO; on the board since May 2024
people.bio: A chartered accountant, company secretary and cost accountant with about 34 years in finance, accounts, tax and corporate transactions, including equity raising and acquisitions. He is the company's CFO and joined the board as an executive director on 30 May 2024. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM. The annual report does not name his earlier employers.

companies.changes: T. S. Sivashankar joined as an independent director in June 2026. No executive change since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Ahmedabad-based M&B Group and run by three related promoter households. Chirag Patel and Malav Patel are joint MDs; Malav's father Girishbhai Patel and Chirag's wife Birva Patel are whole-time directors; Aditya Patel is a whole-time director and his father Vipinbhai Patel is a non-executive director. The board chair is an independent director. Hired professionals run the two divisions (Pankaj Naresh at Phenix, Mayur Patel at Proflex) and finance. Promoters own 70.61%.

people.name: Chirag Hasmukhbhai Patel
people.relation: Promoter; husband of Whole-time Director Birva Patel
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate (B.E.) with more than 30 years in civil projects. He joined the company in May 1993 and is one of its two joint MDs and its highest-paid director. Together with Malav Patel he led the company to its August 2025 listing and to FY26 revenue of ₹1,260cr, with exports up sharply. He also sits on the board's committees.

people.name: Malav Girishbhai Patel
people.relation: Promoter; son of Whole-time Director Girishbhai Patel
people.bio: A BBA graduate with more than 25 years in civil projects. He joined the company in February 2001 and is joint MD alongside Chirag Patel. The two jointly present the company's results and strategy, including its push into export markets such as North America.

people.name: Girishbhai Manibhai Patel
people.since: With the company since December 1984; re-appointed to March 2029
people.relation: Promoter; father of Joint MD Malav Patel
people.stake: 27.16% (June 2026 shareholding pattern); the largest single shareholder
people.bio: A hydraulic engineer trained in the USA, aged 78, with more than 50 years of technical experience in civil projects. He has been with the company since December 1984 and is its largest individual shareholder. He was re-appointed as a whole-time director for three years from April 2026.

people.name: Birva Chirag Patel
people.relation: Promoter; wife of Joint MD Chirag Patel
people.bio: A commerce graduate and company secretary with over 16 years in compliance. She was the company's Company Secretary until March 2024 and became a whole-time director in April 2025. The board cites her expertise in company law and SEBI rules. She is proposed for re-appointment for 2027–2030.

people.name: Aditya Vipinbhai Patel
people.relation: Promoter; son of non-executive Director Vipinbhai Patel
people.bio: An electronics and communications engineer (B.E.) with over 14 years in strategic planning and international operations. He joined the company in April 2011. The board cites his work in business development and overseas operations and has proposed re-appointing him for 2027–2030.

people.name: Pankaj Naresh
people.bio: He holds a BE in electrical engineering, a master's in industrial engineering and management, and an MBA. He has more than 30 years in sales, marketing and operations. He came from Reliance Industries and joined in November 2019 to run the Phenix division (pre-engineered buildings), which brings in about 80% of orders.

people.name: Keyur Bachubhai Shah
people.bio: A commerce graduate, chartered accountant and US CPA with over 30 years in finance and accounts. Before M&B he worked at Shree Ambica Decoprints. He joined in January 2007 and is the company's CFO and a key managerial person.

companies.changes: No change in directors or key managers since the annual report. Mayur Satishbhai Patel (with the company since 2003, diploma in plastics engineering) is CEO of the Proflex self-supported roofing division.

companies.styleNote: Run by two promoter families, the Singhanias and the Bothras (the same group behind EPACK Durable). Sanjay Singhania is MD & CEO and Nikhil Bothra is a whole-time director. Chairman Bajrang Bothra and Ajay DD Singhania (Sanjay's brother) are non-executive directors; Nikhil's father Laxmi Pat Bothra is a promoter but not on the board. The MD says he is moving the company to a more professionally managed structure. Promoters own 64.95%.

people.name: Sanjay Singhania
people.since: With the company since it began in February 1999
people.relation: Promoter; brother of non-executive Director Ajay DD Singhania
people.bio: He holds a B.Com from Gauhati University and an MBA from Swinburne University of Technology, Australia, and is on Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management programme (2026–2028). He has been with EPack Prefab since its start in February 1999 and grew it from one plant to a multi-plant listed company. He leads strategy, capital allocation and stakeholder relations and is overseeing the shift to a professionally managed structure. He is Vice President of PHDCCI and a non-executive director of EPACK Durable.

people.name: Nikhil Bothra
people.relation: Promoter; son of promoter Laxmi Pat Bothra (brother of Chairman Bajrang Bothra)
people.bio: He has been with EPack Prefab since 2012 and has more than 14 years across the business. As executive director he drives business growth, market development, customer relationships and expansion, and he heads marketing. His formal education is not given in the annual report.

people.name: Rahul Agarwal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with more than 19 years in finance and strategy. He was earlier CFO of Asian Footwears, Joint Vice President – Business Strategy at JPFL Films and Jindal Poly Films, Associate Vice President – Business Planning at Burger King, Senior Manager – Finance at Ambuja Cements, and Senior Associate at PwC. He joined in 2024, worked on the GEF Capital fund-raise and the 2025 IPO, and now runs financial controls, treasury, use of IPO money and investor communication.

companies.changes: Preeti Chauhan became Company Secretary in April 2026. Senior managers Anoop Kabra (February 2026), P. V. Subbarao (May 2026) and Sunil Kumar Singh, VP – Sales & Business Development (July 2026), resigned.

companies.styleNote: Its two promoters, both with the company since it was set up in 1983, still run it: Arvind Nanda is MD and Gautam Suri is whole-time director. Their sons, Viraj Nanda and Ishaan Suri, sit on the board as non-executive directors. Day-to-day business is led by a hired CEO, Manish Kumar Garg, who joined the board in February 2026. The chair is an independent director. Promoters own 59.44%.

people.name: Arvind Nanda
people.since: With the company since its incorporation (1983)
people.relation: Promoter (with the company since incorporation); father of non-executive Director Viraj Nanda
people.bio: A promoter director, aged about 71, who has been with the company since it was incorporated. He leads overall business decisions and financial oversight. With about 30 years in pre-engineered steel buildings, he built the company's business model and helped grow the PEB industry in India. He holds no other listed or public-company directorships. His formal education is not disclosed in the annual report.

people.name: Gautam Suri
people.since: With the company since its inception (1983)
people.relation: Promoter (with the company since incorporation); father of non-executive Director Ishaan Suri
people.bio: A promoter director, aged about 73, who has been with the company since its start. He leads the technical and engineering functions and shaped its technology base. He has more than three decades in pre-engineered steel buildings. He received the CIDC Vishwakarma Industry Captain Award in 2024. His formal education is not disclosed in the annual report.

people.name: Manish Kumar Garg
people.since: CEO; executive director since 2 February 2026 (term to 2031)
people.bio: A civil engineer from Delhi with an MBA, and an alumnus of Harvard Business School. He has about three decades in metal and pre-engineered buildings. Before Interarch he worked at Safal Building Systems in Nairobi, Kenya. As CEO he drives strategy, operations and financial performance, and he joined the board as an executive director in February 2026. He received the CIDC Vishwakarma 'Industry Doyen' award in 2025.

people.name: Pushpendra Kumar Bansal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a B.Com from Ajmer University and about 27 years of experience. Before Interarch he worked at Microtek International. He joined as CFO during FY2024-25 and is a key managerial person.

companies.changes: CEO Manish Kumar Garg joined the board as an executive director on 2 February 2026 (approved by shareholders in March 2026). DGM – Safety Sumesh Sehgal resigned in August 2026. The FY26 annual report file on NSE could not be opened in full, so some details come from the FY25 report.

companies.styleNote: Founder-run. Gopal Rajaram Kabra, the main promoter, is Chairman, MD and CEO and owns about 76%. A second promoter, founding member Mehul Shah, is whole-time director and COO. The two are not related, and no director is related to another. Promoters own 79.2% in all.

people.name: Gopal Rajaram Kabra
people.since: With the company since 2008 and on the board since incorporation; MD since December 2024
people.relation: Founder and main promoter
people.stake: 76.17% (15,44,94,540 shares; June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 79.2%
people.bio: Holds a B.Com from Swami Ramanand Teerth Marathwada University, Nanded, and an MBA in marketing from Vishwakarma School of Business Management & Research. He has about 20 years in the solar industry and has been with GK Energy since it started operations in 2008. He runs overall operations and business development for its solar water-pump business. He received the Udyog Ratan award from the Institute of Economic Studies in 2013. He became MD in December 2024, ahead of the September 2025 IPO.

people.name: Mehul Ajit Shah
people.since: Employee since 2008; director since April 2011; WTD & COO since December 2024
people.relation: Promoter and founding member; not related to the Chairman
people.bio: Holds a B.Com and an MBA from the University of Pune. He is a founding member and promoter, has worked at the company since 2008 and joined the board in April 2011. With about 18 years in solar power, he runs project planning, administration and execution. The board raised his pay from April 2026, citing his work on strategy, execution and growth.

people.name: Sunil Kamalkishor Malu
people.bio: A fellow chartered accountant with a B.Com from the University of Pune and more than 14 years in finance, accounting and management consulting. Before joining GK Energy he worked at the CA firms Toshniwal Malu & Associates and Sunil K. Malu & Co. He is the company's CFO and a key managerial person.

companies.changes: Shubham S. Jain became Company Secretary on 16 March 2026 after Jeevan Innani resigned. Independent director Chandra Iyengar resigned in February 2026. No change in the executive directors or CFO.

companies.styleNote: A Hyderabad family company. Aditya Rao of the promoter family is Vice Chairman & MD; the veteran promoter J. V. Nrupender Rao is Chairman Emeritus, and the annual report lists him as a relative of a KMP. The board chairman is an independent director. K. Lavanya Kumar Rao, from the promoter group, is the other executive director. The annual report says no director is related to another. Promoters own 39.67%.

people.name: Aditya Narsing Rao
people.relation: Promoter; Chairman Emeritus J. V. Nrupender Rao is listed as a relative of a KMP
people.stake: 6.67% (FY26 annual report and June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 39.67%
people.bio: He is Vice Chairman and MD and leads the company's growth strategy, organisation, controls and team building. The company's website says his aim is a business whose units keep growing revenue and profit with tight risk controls, and consistent EPS growth. He is also a director of the promoter company Pennar Holdings and of the US subsidiary Pennar Global. His formal education is not disclosed on the website or in the annual report.

people.name: K. Lavanya Kumar Rao
people.relation: Promoter group (Kondapally family); per the annual report not a relative of other directors
people.stake: 0.13% directly, plus 0.06% through his HUF (June 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: A law graduate from Kakatiya University with more than three decades in law, construction, corporate affairs and dealing with government authorities. He joined the Pennar group in 1987 and is an executive director of Pennar Industries.

people.name: Shrikant Bhakkad
people.bio: He is the company's CFO and a key managerial person, and co-signs the MD/CFO certificate on the accounts. The annual report and website do not give his education or past employers.

companies.changes: Non-executive director P. V. Rao (a former joint MD) resigned on 10 April 2026. No change in the executive team.

companies.styleNote: Reliance New Energy is the largest promoter at 32.49%, alongside the Shapoorji Pallonji group and the Daruvala family; promoters own 45.73% in all. No promoter holds an executive job and the company has no MD. It is run by a hired Manager and Global CEO, Chandra Kishore Thakur. Promoter-side directors such as Khurshed Daruvala (Chairman of the Sterling & Wilson group) sit on the board as non-executive directors.

people.name: Chandra Kishore Thakur
people.since: Joined 2018 as COO – International; Manager re-appointed to August 2027
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from NIT Jamshedpur with an MBA from IGNOU. He spent about 22 years at NTPC, then was COO of the EPC vertical at Lanco Infratech and President and CEO of the power and infrastructure business at Punj Lloyd. He joined in 2018 as COO – International, running projects across the Middle East, Africa and Latin America. He is now Global CEO and the statutory Manager, leading strategy and operations in India and abroad; he was re-appointed as Manager for two years from 1 September 2025.

people.name: Ajit Pratap Singh
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. and an LLB from Kanpur universities, an M.Sc. in finance from ICFAI University, Tripura, and a PG diploma in business administration from Symbiosis. He is a company secretary and cost accountant, a member of the UK's CIPFA, and a US certified management accountant. Before Sterling and Wilson he worked at Transrail Lighting, OPG Power Generation, Vedanta Aluminium, JSW Bengal Steel, Jaypee Minerals and South African Coal Mine Holdings, among others. He took over as CFO in March 2025 from interim CFO Sandeep Mathew.

companies.changes: Sandeep Mathew, SVP – Investor Relations (and former interim CFO), resigned effective 31 July 2026. Sunil Kumaran ceased to be senior management in June 2026. Vikas Gulati joined as Chief Procurement Officer on 1 June 2026, and Rajesh Mittal as SVP – IT in January 2026. The statutory auditor resigned in July 2026.

companies.styleNote: Promoter-led: Kartik Teltia is Chairman and MD and the only executive director. His father, Mangal Chand Teltia, sits on the board as a non-executive director. Sushil Kumar Jain and his son Rishabh Jain (a whole-time director until early 2026) are also non-executive directors. Promoters own 65.77%, including 32.01% held through Pioneer Facor IT Infradevelopers.

people.name: Kartik Teltia
people.since: Director since July 2013; also Chairman since mid-2026
people.relation: Promoter; son of non-executive Director Mangal Chand Teltia
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a background in management and commerce. He has been a director since July 2013 and leads the company's strategy and operations. His experience in finance, business planning and renewable energy has shaped the company's growth as a solar EPC contractor. He took it public in September 2025 and IPO money is now going towards a planned 2.4 GW solar-cell facility. He added the chairman role after the independent chairperson resigned in May 2026.

people.name: Mukut Goyal
people.bio: He has more than 12 years in accounting, financial management and corporate finance. He earlier worked at Rama Paper Mills, Tokai Imperial Hydraulics India, Janna Auto Industries, Jindal Poly Films, Samvardhana Motherson International, MB Power (Madhya Pradesh) and Dalmia Cement (Bharat). He leads the finance function. His formal qualifications are not stated in the annual report.

companies.changes: Rini Chordia resigned as Chairperson and independent director on 26 May 2026; four new independent directors joined on 1 May 2026. Rishabh Jain moved from whole-time director to non-executive director during FY26.

companies.styleNote: An RPG Group company: the Goenka-led promoter group owns 50.10%. Harsh V. Goenka, RPG's chairman, has been non-executive Chairman since 2006 and holds about 50.4 lakh shares jointly with family (he also takes a large commission, Rs 4.4cr for FY26). The business is run by a hired MD & CEO, Vimal Kejriwal, now on one-year extensions. Named senior management also includes Somraj Roy (CHRO & Executive Director), Ganesh Srinivasan (President, T&D), Raman Kapil (President, Civil) and Ankur Dev (Executive Director, Transportation and Renewables); the company gives no biographies for them.

people.name: Vimal Kejriwal
people.since: Board since 1 January 2015; MD & CEO since 1 April 2015; latest one-year term to 31 March 2027
people.stake: 875 shares, held jointly as second holder with his wife (FY26 annual report); negligible
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary, aged 65, who did an advanced executive programme at the Kellogg School of Management and is also an NMIMS alumnus. He has over four decades of experience across infrastructure, oil and gas, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers and investment banking. He joined KEC's board as a whole-time director in January 2015 and became MD & CEO in April 2015, since when KEC has grown beyond power transmission into civil, railways, oil and gas pipelines, renewables and cables, with acquisitions and new plants. He is also on the board of Raychem RPG and KEC's subsidiaries, and on IEEMA's executive council. He is now reappointed one year at a time (April 2026 to March 2027, approved at the August 2026 AGM); he was paid Rs 12.57cr in FY26.

people.name: Rajeev Aggarwal
people.bio: KEC's CFO and key managerial person since September 2014, a tenure of 12 years. The annual reports do not give his education or earlier career. He co-signs the CEO/CFO compliance certificate and the accounts; his pay rose 12% in FY26.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26 or since the annual report (July 2026). Among senior management, Executive Directors Kaushal Kodesia (Transportation), Nagesh Veeturi (Civil) and Anand Kulkarni (Business Operations) retired, and Manjit Singh Sethi (Renewables) resigned; Somraj Roy, Raman Kapil and Ankur Dev were newly named senior management.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Munot family's Kalpataru Group. The founder Mofatraj P. Munot, 81, is non-executive Chairman (9.57%) and his son Parag Munot, MD of the group's real estate company Kalpataru Ltd, is a non-executive director (0.37%); they are the only related directors. The promoter group owns 33.58%, and 24.55% of that is pledged (8.24% of the company). Day-to-day the company is run by hired professionals: MD & CEO Manish Mohnot and Deputy MD Shailendra Kumar Tripathi.

people.name: Manish Mohnot
people.since: Board since 1 November 2006; MD & CEO since at least 2017; current term April 2025 to March 2028
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant, aged 53, who attended the Advanced Management Programme at Harvard Business School. He has nearly three decades in energy, infrastructure, oil and gas, consulting, banking and PPP projects. He has been on the board since 2006 and, as MD & CEO, turned the company into an asset-light EPC group, merged JMC Projects into it and bought businesses in Sweden (Linjemontage) and Brazil (Fasttel). He has chaired the CII transmission line committee, and ICAI named him a CA Business Leader in 2025. He is well paid: Rs 25cr in FY26, of which Rs 19cr was commission/incentive.

people.name: Shailendra Kumar Tripathi
people.since: Board since 4 January 2023 (on the JMC merger); term renewed to 21 October 2028
people.bio: A civil engineer, aged 61, with nearly four decades in buildings, heavy civil infrastructure, industrial plants and PPP projects. He was MD & CEO of JMC Projects (India) until it merged into Kalpataru, and built its civil business across housing, factories, airports, metros, water supply and highways. At Kalpataru he runs the civil (B&F and infrastructure) business and has taken it into Africa and South East Asia. He was paid Rs 8.26cr in FY26.

people.name: Ram Patodia
people.bio: He became CFO on 1 April 2019, succeeding Kamal Kishore Jain, having earlier been President (Finance & Accounts) at the company. He co-signs the accounts and CEO/CFO certificate and sits on the share transfer committee. The annual reports do not give his education or earlier employers.

people.name: Sanjay Dalmia
people.since: With the company since at least 2018; was on the board from 8 August 2018
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary with more than three decades in power, infrastructure, textiles, mining and business development, including work in the Far East, Africa, the CIS and the Middle East. He joined the board as an Executive Director in August 2018 and now holds the Executive Director title as senior management without a board seat.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26 or since the annual report (June 2026). Sriram Pechiappan (President, Group Assurance) was named senior management in Oct 2025. Gautam Mehra joined as an independent director on 9 Jun 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Bansal family company from Kolkata. The founder Sajan Kumar Bansal is Chairman & MD and his three sons Sharan, Devesh and Siddharth are whole-time directors, each running a business line. The promoter group owns 66.50%, mostly through family trusts (three SK Bansal trusts at 9.64% each) and group companies such as Skipper Plastics (17.76%); the family members hold only token shares in their own names. The only non-family executive director is Yash Pall Jain (commercial).

people.name: Sajan Kumar Bansal
people.since: Founder (company set up 1981); with the company since 26 October 1984 per the annual report
people.relation: Founder-promoter; father of Sharan, Devesh and Siddharth Bansal
people.stake: 0.09% in his own name (FY26 annual report); promoter group 66.50%, including the SK Bansal Heritage Trust (9.64%) where he is trustee
people.bio: A commerce graduate, aged 67, with about 40 years in the business. He set up Skipper in 1981 as a maker of Hamilton poles and grew it into a multi-plant group making power transmission and distribution structures, where it is among the world's top five makers, plus polymer pipes. He took the company's shares to listing on BSE and NSE in 2014-15. He is active in tribal and village development in Jharkhand and was National President of Friends of the Tribal Society, which runs One Teacher Schools, from 2015 to 2021. He was paid Rs 4.8cr in FY26.

people.name: Sharan Bansal
people.relation: Son of the founder Sajan Kumar Bansal; brother of Devesh and Siddharth Bansal
people.stake: 0.01% in his own name (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: A mechanical engineering graduate from Georgia Tech, Atlanta, aged 46. He started Skipper's power transmission business in 2003 and built it into India's largest maker of transmission and distribution structures; Skipper won PGCIL's largest tower supplier award three years running. He focuses on expanding the business abroad. He has served on IEEMA's national executive council and was President of the Entrepreneurs' Organisation, Kolkata chapter. He was paid Rs 2.4cr in FY26.

people.name: Devesh Bansal
people.relation: Son of the founder Sajan Kumar Bansal; brother of Sharan and Siddharth Bansal
people.stake: 0.01% in his own name (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: A B.Com graduate from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata (2004) with a master's in international business and management from De Montfort University, UK (2005), and Harvard's three-year OPM programme; aged 43. In over 22 years at Skipper he has headed several businesses and now runs telecom, railways, transmission monopoles and the expansion of polymer products. He is also designated partner of Skipper's micro-irrigation joint venture and sits on the EEPC regional committee. He was paid Rs 2.4cr in FY26.

people.name: Siddharth Bansal
people.relation: Son of the founder Sajan Kumar Bansal; brother of Sharan and Devesh Bansal
people.stake: 0.01% in his own name (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in entrepreneurship from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and a master's in international business from Aston University, Birmingham; aged 38. For about a decade he has run procurement, operations and marketing of the polymer (pipes) division. He is on the executive committees of the Indian Plastics Federation and the Young Presidents' Organisation, Calcutta chapter. He retires by rotation and is up for reappointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Yash Pall Jain
people.since: Joined 6 September 2017; current term to 5 September 2028
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Punjab University, aged 67, with about four decades in manufacturing. He came from Bhushan Power & Steel. At Skipper he handles dealings with government bodies, power boards, district administrations and tax authorities, raw material buying, commercial operations of the plants, internal audit and administration. He was reappointed for three years in September 2025.

people.name: Shiv Shankar Gupta
people.bio: A chartered accountant, aged 56, with about 31 years of experience. Before Skipper he worked at West Coast Optilinks, a unit of West Coast Paper Mills. As CFO he leads the finance function; his pay rose 25% in FY26 to about Rs 1.28cr.

people.name: Jalaj Kumar Malpani
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant (AICWA), aged 60, with about 35 years of experience. He joined Skipper from ArcelorMittal. As COO he is leading a re-organisation of how the business runs, including an SAP S/4HANA roll-out, as Skipper scales up capacity.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26 or since the annual report (August 2026).

companies.styleNote: Run by the promoter P. P. Gupta as Managing Director, with Ankit Saraiya as Whole-time Director & CEO; Gupta, Saraiya and non-executive director Avantika Gupta are relatives of each other (the annual report does not spell out the exact link). The promoter group owns 56.92%, almost all through group companies such as Varanasi Commercial (21.16%), Kusum Industrial Gases (12.55%) and Techno Leasing & Finance (11.86%). Gupta took no pay in FY26. The board also has a non-executive professional director, James Trout, founder of US data-centre firms CleanArc and Vantage, reflecting the data-centre push.

people.name: Padam Prakash Gupta
people.since: On this company's board since 25 July 2018 (after the group merger); has led the Techno group for over four decades
people.relation: Promoter; relative of Whole-time Director Ankit Saraiya and director Avantika Gupta
people.stake: 0.01% (6,000 shares) in his own name (FY26 annual report); promoter group 56.92%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in engineering and an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. Early in his career he was a management consultant at BHEL and worked in the merchant banking division of ANZ Grindlays Bank, Kolkata. He has over 45 years in the power sector and has built Techno into an EPC contractor for power transmission, substations and flue-gas desulphurisation, and more recently a developer of data centres (its Chennai hyperscale facility is running). He was Vice President of IEEMA. He voluntarily waived his pay in FY26.

people.name: Ankit Saraiya
people.relation: Relative of MD Padam Prakash Gupta and director Avantika Gupta (per the annual report)
people.stake: 0.19% (2,16,000 shares, FY26 annual report); counted in the promoter group
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in corporate finance and accounting, with a minor in computer information systems, from Bentley University, Massachusetts. He has over 12 years of financial and commercial experience and has been a whole-time director since 2012, now designated CEO. He sits on the board's risk, CSR and stakeholder committees. He was paid Rs 24 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Pradeep Kumar Lohia
people.since: CFO (key managerial personnel); start date not disclosed
people.bio: The company's CFO and a key managerial person; he co-signs the accounts and the CEO/CFO certificate with the MD. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26 or since the annual report (August 2026). Independent directors Krishna Murari Poddar and Arun Duggal resigned in Nov and Dec 2025; K. K. Rai retired Sep 2025; ex-PowerGrid director Shailesh Kumar Mishra joined as an independent director in Feb 2026.

companies.styleNote: The founder Digambar C. Bagde, who started Transrail in 1984, is Executive Chairman; the company's holding company Ajanma Holdings owns 69.91% and promoters together 71.12%. Sanjay Kumar Verma, a named promoter, is non-executive Vice Chairman. Day-to-day it is run by a hired MD & CEO, Randeep Narang, an ex-KEC executive. No director or KMP is related to another.

people.name: Digambar C. Bagde
people.relation: Founder-promoter
people.stake: 0.67% (8,98,540 shares, FY26 annual report); promoters together 71.12%, mainly via Ajanma Holdings (69.91%)
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate from the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda with five decades in power transmission and distribution. After about a decade at another T&D company he started Transrail in 1984 and has led it since, building it into a maker of towers, conductors and poles and an EPC contractor for transmission lines in India and abroad. He leads the board and management on growth strategy.

people.name: Randeep Narang
people.since: MD & CEO since at least 2023; current term as MD from 15 December 2025
people.bio: A Delhi University commerce graduate with a postgraduate diploma in marketing from the Institute of Marketing Management, New Delhi, and over 36 years of experience. He was Chief Operating Officer (West) at Bharti Airtel and MD & CEO of CEAT Kelani Holdings in Sri Lanka. Before Transrail his last job was President - International (T&D, Solar) and Cables at KEC International. He is the highest-paid director (58.7 times the median employee's pay in FY26); shareholders approved a pay rise for him in September 2023.

people.name: Suryanarayana Dhulipala
people.since: With the company since its incorporation; whole-time director since 5 August 2025
people.bio: Holds a diploma in mechanical engineering and has long experience in power transmission and distribution. Before Transrail he worked at Karuna Cables. He has been with the company since its incorporation and was Chief Operating Officer, Domestic Business, before joining the board, and has been key to growing the domestic business. He retires by rotation and is up for reappointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Deepak Khandelwal
people.bio: A key managerial person who became CFO during FY26 (the annual report calls it a fresh appointment). He co-signs the accounts and the CEO/CFO certificate. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier career.

people.name: Rajesh Neelakantan
people.since: Named senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Listed by the company as senior management with the title Chief Strategy Officer & Group CFO, above the company CFO. The annual report gives no biography.

companies.changes: Deputy MD Raman Rajagopalan (appointed 5 Aug 2025) left the post on 31 Jul 2026. Independent director Vinod Dasari left the board on 9 Aug 2026. Company Secretary changed in May 2025 (Monica Gandhi replaced Gandhali Upadhye); CHRO Sonal Raj joined Aug 2025. Ex-POWERGRID CMD I. S. Jha became a non-executive (non-independent) director from 2 Feb 2026 because he also advises the company.

companies.styleNote: A Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; the Government of India (President of India) owns 51.32% and appoints the CMD and functional directors, usually career EIL engineers picked by the PESB. There is no promoter family and no director is related to another. Two ministry officials sit on the board as non-executive government nominees.

people.name: Atul Gupta
people.role: Chairman & Managing Director (also additional charge, Director (Commercial))
people.since: Board since 16 August 2022 as Director (Commercial); CMD since 29 June 2026
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, who joined EIL as a management trainee in 1992. Over three decades he worked in project execution, construction management, business development and commercial roles, leading teams on large projects in India and abroad. As Director (Commercial) from 2022 he pushed overseas consultancy (a record overseas order book in FY26, a new branch in Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia) and new areas such as data centres, nuclear, renewables, metals and defence. The PESB picked him for CMD in November 2025 and he took over on 29 June 2026. He is also part-time Chairman of the subsidiary Certification Engineers International.

people.name: Sanjay Jindal
people.bio: A B.Com (Hons) graduate from Delhi University and a member of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India. He joined EIL in 1992 and has over 33 years in finance and cost accounting in the hydrocarbon sector, covering project bidding to contract closure, project finance, investments, tax, internal controls and reporting. He also served as CFO of Ramagundam Fertilisers and Chemicals (RFCL), an EIL joint venture. He received the CMA CFO award from the Institute of Cost Accountants of India.

people.name: Rajiv Agarwal
people.bio: A chemical engineer from IIT Roorkee (then University of Roorkee) with over 36 years in process design and engineering of refineries, petrochemicals, fertilisers, gas processing, offshore facilities and coal gasification plants. He runs the technology, R&D, engineering and equipment divisions. He leads EIL's push into green hydrogen, green ammonia, sustainable aviation fuel, biofuels, carbon capture and nuclear, and its AI and digital tools for project monitoring. He is part-time Chairman of Ramagundam Fertilisers & Chemicals. He retires by rotation and is up for reappointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Subhas Balakumar
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate (1988) from Government College of Engineering, Tirunelveli, with about 38 years of project execution. He joined EIL in 1991 on the Digboi refinery modernisation in Assam. He led the commissioning of the 650,000-barrel-a-day grassroots refinery and petrochemical project in Nigeria and worked on EIL's Mongolia refinery and Guyana gas projects. In India he oversaw HPCL's Vizag and Rajasthan refinery projects and IOCL's Panipat expansion; as Executive Director (Projects) he also took EIL into data centres, R&D campuses and the high-speed rail project. He is a Fellow of the Institution of Engineers (India).

people.name: Rupesh Kumar Singh
people.bio: A civil engineer from IIT Kanpur with an MBA in finance from IGNOU and SHRM-CP and PMP certifications, with over 34 years at EIL. He joined as a management trainee in 1991. Before becoming Director (HR) he was Executive Director and head of the construction division, overseeing projects worth nearly USD 25bn at about 60 sites in India, Mongolia, Guyana and the Middle East, and led EIL's Namami Gange site team (2016-18). He is on the board of the subsidiary Certification Engineers International.

companies.changes: CMD Vartika Shukla retired on 1 Mar 2026; MoPNG Additional Secretary Praveen M. Khanooja held interim charge until Atul Gupta became CMD on 29 Jun 2026. The Director (Commercial) post is vacant (the CMD holds it as additional charge from 30 Jun 2026) and the PESB has invited applications for it. New independent directors Kahuli Sema and Ashish Kumar Gupta joined on 14 Aug 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Ministry of Railways PSU; the Government of India (President of India) owns 65.17% and appoints the CMD and functional directors. There is no promoter family and no director is related to another. The CMD post is held on additional charge by RVNL's CMD, Saleem Ahmad, for up to a year from 1 July 2026, pending a regular appointment. Two Railway Board officials sit as government nominee directors, and the board is short of independent directors.

people.name: Saleem Ahmad
people.since: 1 July 2026 (additional charge for up to one year)
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate from Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi, with over 35 years in construction, specialising in bridges, tunnels and residential and commercial buildings. He has been CMD of Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL), the rival railway construction PSU, since December 2025 and runs Ircon alongside that job. Before RVNL he was Director (Projects) at NBCC from April 2023 to December 2025, and earlier Executive Director (Civil) at Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, where he worked on last-mile connectivity; he also worked at Mumbai Port Trust. He is proposed to be regularised as a director at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Ragini Advani
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant, a rank holder in both exams, with about 30 years of finance experience. Before Ircon she worked at Engineers India, NTPC SAIL Power Company (NSPCL) and KPMG. Her work spans accounting, finance concurrence, internal audit, treasury, financial closures, budgeting, valuations, tax and financial restructuring. She retires by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Ajit Kumar Mishra
people.bio: An Indian Railway Service of Engineers (IRSE) officer and IIT Kanpur alumnus with an MBA in international business and an LL.M. in international dispute resolution; he is a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators and a FIDIC adjudicator. He has over 25 years in railway and transport projects. Before Ircon he held senior posts at Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation (DFCCIL), leading major rail works and then its contract management department. At Ircon he runs railway, high-speed rail, metro, bridge, tunnel and track projects, including the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail track package, and the Bangladesh, Malaysia and Nepal projects.

people.name: Rajesh Naik
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate with over 34 years of experience, including more than 12 years abroad in Oman, Bangladesh, Guyana, Botswana, Paraguay, Uruguay and the Philippines, across railways, highways, bridges, tunnels, buildings and port links. He has worked at RITES, Indian Port Rail & Ropeway Corporation, Engineering Projects (India), Kalpataru Power Transmission, Ircon itself and Konkan Railway. Just before joining Ircon's board he was Executive Director (Strategy & Corporate Communication) at RITES, serving as its Chief Strategy Officer and COO of RITES Expocon. He is to be regularised as a director at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Alin Roy Choudhury
people.role: Chief Financial Officer & Chief Investor Relations Officer (Chief General Manager, Finance)
people.since: CFO since 1 January 2025 (with Ircon about 27 years)
people.bio: A cost and management accountant (CMA) with over 30 years in infrastructure and construction finance, about 27 of them at Ircon, where he rose to Chief General Manager (Finance). He has worked on overseas projects such as the Sri Lanka rail projects and an Ethiopia road project. He led Ircon's move to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and its SAP S/4HANA finance roll-out.

companies.changes: CMD Hari Mohan Gupta retired on 30 Jun 2026; RVNL CMD Saleem Ahmad holds additional charge from 1 Jul 2026. Director (Works) Parag Verma retired Apr 2025 (Ajit Kumar Mishra from May 2025); Director (Projects) Anand Kumar Singh retired Dec 2025 (Rajesh Naik from Feb 2026). Ircon says it has no official information on reported merger talk with RVNL.

companies.styleNote: A Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; the Government of India (President of India) owns 61.75% and appoints the CMD, functional directors and independent directors. There is no promoter family and no director is related to another. Two ministry officials sit as government nominee directors. The Director (Projects) post has been vacant since December 2025.

people.name: K. P. Mahadevaswamy
people.bio: A civil engineering graduate from Mysore University with an M.Tech (research) and an executive leadership programme from IIM Calcutta, and over 33 years in construction. As CEO of NBCC's subsidiary Hindustan Steelworks Construction (HSCL) he turned the loss-making PSU into a profitable Miniratna. At NBCC he has led the redevelopment of seven government housing colonies in Delhi, the Supreme Court-monitored completion of stalled Amrapali homes, and the real estate, business development, procurement and overseas divisions. He also chairs subsidiaries HSCL and HSCC and the public-sector body SCOPE. He held the Director (Projects) job as well from December 2025 to March 2026.

people.name: Anjeev Kumar Jain
people.bio: A Fellow cost accountant (CMA) with a law degree from Delhi University and a PG diploma in finance management, with nearly three decades in finance. He began in the Defence Audit wing of the CAG, then held finance roles at NHPC, DFCCIL and RITES, covering corporate finance, audits, cost accounting, FIDIC contracts and World Bank and JICA funding. He was a director on the board of REMC, a RITES subsidiary. He was named the Railway Minister's Employee of the Year in 2017.

people.name: Suman Kumar
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in civil engineering from BIT Sindri, a master's in civil engineering from IIT Kanpur, a master's in computer science from BIT Mesra and a PhD in civil engineering, plus an executive MBA from IIM Ranchi. He spent more than two decades at Coal India and was then Chief Engineer and ex-officio director of Jharkhand Police Housing Corporation. Since joining NBCC in 2016 he has worked on the Amrapali completions, the Delhi colony redevelopment, the World Trade Centre at Nauroji Nagar, AIIMS Deoghar and IIM Ranchi.

companies.changes: Director (Projects) Saleem Ahmad left on 23 Dec 2025 on becoming CMD of RVNL; the CMD held that charge until 22 Mar 2026. The PESB recommended Ashutosh Gautam (Member (Technical), Inland Waterways Authority of India) for the post on 16 Jun 2026; he had not joined the board as of the latest board listing.

companies.styleNote: A Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Railways; the Government of India (President of India) owns 72.20% and appoints the CMD, functional directors and independent directors, mostly from the Indian Railways services or RITES' own ranks. There is no promoter family and no director is related to another. Two Railway Board officials sit as government nominee directors.

people.name: Rahul Mithal
people.since: 7 October 2021; tenure extended to his superannuation on 30 June 2027
people.bio: An Indian Railway Service of Mechanical Engineers officer (SCRA 1985 batch), aged 59, with a mechanical engineering degree from the Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical & Electrical Engineering, Jamalpur, and an MBA in finance from Jamnalal Bajaj Institute, Mumbai; he is a Fellow of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers (UK). He spent over 20 years in Indian Railways, then more than 10 years at CONCOR, where he was the functional director for Projects & Services from September 2017 to October 2021 and oversaw more than 20 logistics parks and warehouses. He is also Chairman of REMC, a RITES subsidiary. In August 2026 the Railway Ministry extended his term beyond October 2026 to June 2027.

people.name: Krishna Gopal Agarwal
people.bio: A Fellow member of both the Institute of Cost Accountants (ICMAI) and the Institute of Company Secretaries (ICSI), with over three decades in financial management, reporting and treasury. He began his career at Nerolac Paints and then spent more than 26 years at SAIL, largely in finance at the Bhilai Steel Plant. He joined RITES as General Manager (Finance) in June 2021 and became Director (Finance) in August 2023. He also sits on the boards of REMC, GPCL Consulting Services and Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation.

people.name: Deepak Tripathi
people.bio: A former Indian Railway Service of Mechanical Engineers officer (1990 batch), aged 58, with a mechanical engineering degree and a postgraduate degree and doctorate in operations management from IIM Mumbai. Over 35 years in Indian Railways and Konkan Railway he worked in traction and rolling stock, railway operations and maintenance, quality assurance, technology projects, marketing and international business. He developed the patented 'SMART Yard' technology and wrote the book 'Smart Lean Management', which won the Lal Bahadur Shastri Award. He also held the Director (Projects) charge from May 2025 to March 2026 and is up for reappointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Prem Singh Meena
people.bio: An Indian Railway Service of Electrical Engineers officer (1990 batch), aged 58, with an electrical engineering degree from MNIT Jaipur. He has over 34 years in traction distribution, traction rolling stock and electrical services in the Railways and in rail infrastructure and metro work at RITES. Before joining the board he was RITES' Executive Director (Rail Infra, Metro and Project Co-ordination), handling railway electrification, sidings, signalling and metro project management. He has attended management programmes at INSEAD Singapore and ICLIF Malaysia. He is also a nominee director of REMC.

companies.changes: Director (Projects) Arun Kumar Singh resigned on 5 May 2025; Prem Singh Meena took the post on 19 Mar 2026. Company Secretary Ashok Mishra resigned on 19 Mar 2026 (Nikhil Agarwal appointed). CMD Rahul Mithal's term was extended on 20 Aug 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.

companies.styleNote: Run by the Agarwal brothers of Udaipur, whose father Gumani Ram Agarwal founded the business. Ajendra Kumar Agarwal is Chairman and MD since the eldest brother, Vinod Kumar Agarwal, resigned in November 2025 for health reasons (he has since died). Two more brothers are Presidents, a nephew and a third-generation family member are whole-time directors, and another nephew is Director (Operations). A hired CFO has run finance since 2011. Promoters own 74.69%, including 31.80% through Lokesh Builders.

people.name: Ajendra Kumar Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Devki Nandan, Mahendra Kumar and Purshottam Agarwal and of the late Vinod Kumar Agarwal; uncle of whole-time director Vikas Agarwal
people.stake: 5.55% (30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 74.69%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from Jodhpur University and has nearly 40 years in road construction; he is 62. He has been on the board since 2006 and, as MD, runs the company day to day. He heads the in-house design team and pushes value engineering on projects. He added the Chairman's role on 11 May 2026 after his elder brother left the board. He was paid ₹856 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Vikas Agarwal
people.relation: Son of President Devki Nandan Agarwal; nephew of the Chairman & MD
people.bio: Has about 20 years in infrastructure, mostly running execution of large and mega national-highway projects for the company. He is 45 and was paid ₹510 lakh in FY26. His brother Pankaj Agarwal is Director (Operations) in the senior team.

people.name: Ashwin Agarwal
people.role: Whole-time Director (heads power transmission & distribution and ropeways)
people.relation: Third generation of the founding family, per the company; the company says he is not a 'relative' of any current director as defined in company law
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. in economics (Honours) from Penn State University. He has been with the company for more than six years and leads its power transmission and distribution and ropeway businesses, the main diversification away from roads. He joined the board as a whole-time director in May 2026, and shareholders approved him in July 2026.

people.name: Devki Nandan Agarwal
people.relation: Brother of the Chairman & MD; father of Vikas and Pankaj Agarwal
people.bio: A founding family member with about 48 years of experience; he is 70. He runs the company's large fleet of plant and equipment and is listed as senior management.

people.name: Mahendra Kumar Agarwal
people.relation: Brother of the Chairman & MD
people.bio: A founding family member with about 41 years of experience; he is 63. He runs procurement and is listed as senior management.

people.name: Anand Rathi
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary (associate member of both institutes); he is 50 with about 29 years of experience. He was a vice president at Reliance Infrastructure before joining. As CFO he handles funding, financial models, strategy including mergers and acquisitions, and bank relationships, and he explains the numbers on earnings calls.

people.name: Sudhir Mutha
