The company credits him with consistent revenue growth and better margins through new marketing programmes and strong execution, and with rebuilding Orient Bell's finances, operations and brand since he joined in 2018. He reached retirement age on 31 July 2026, and the board extended his employment for five more years.

people.name: Anuj Arora
people.bio: A chartered accountant with more than 23 years in manufacturing, retail and hospitality. He has worked at Uflex, Apollo International, Reliance Retail and Ballarpur Industries, in business partnering, controllership, financial reporting and tax, and has set up internal controls and risk systems and run procurement and logistics. He replaced Himanshu Jindal, who left in May 2025.

companies.changes: CEO Aditya Gupta's tenure was extended to July 2031 (board decision 15 Jul 2026). Chief Sales Officer Munish Tandon left in April 2025 and CFO Himanshu Jindal in May 2025; Anuj Arora became CFO in August 2025. Independent director Sameer Kamboj left the board in July 2026.

companies.styleNote: Run by Saurabh Mittal's branch of the Mittal family (Greenply and Greenpanel are run by other branches). Saurabh Mittal is MD & CEO and his wife Parul is a whole-time director; his father Shiv Prakash Mittal is the non-executive chairman. Hired professionals run finance, India sales and manufacturing. Promoters own 50.98%, mostly through SM Greenlam Investments (37.78%).

people.name: Saurabh Mittal
people.relation: Promoter; son of non-executive Chairman Shiv Prakash Mittal; husband of whole-time director Parul Mittal
people.stake: 11.33% in his own name (30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 50.98%, including 37.78% through SM Greenlam Investments
people.bio: An alumnus of Mayo College, Ajmer, and a commerce graduate from the University of Madras, with about 29 years in wood panels and surfaces. He joined in 2002 from HG Industries. The company calls him the main architect of its rise to Asia's largest laminate maker and one of the top three laminate brands in the world, sold in over 120 countries, and of its expansion into plants across five states, including a large chipboard plant. He personally leads manufacturing, brand, distribution, exports, finance and investor relations. He was paid ₹9.9cr in FY26. He is 50.

people.name: Parul Mittal
people.relation: Wife of MD & CEO Saurabh Mittal; daughter-in-law of Chairman Shiv Prakash Mittal
people.bio: A commerce graduate who specialises in brand management. Before joining Greenlam she led brand building at national and international level, handling marketing strategy, research agencies and advertising partners; her previous employer was Greenply Industries. At Greenlam she leads brand-building in India and abroad and also covers CSR, ESG, people practices, administration, procurement and supply chain. She was paid ₹5.7cr in FY26. She is 48.

people.name: Ashok Kumar Sharma
people.bio: A chartered accountant with about 33 years of experience. He joined Greenlam in December 2013 from Su-Kam Power Systems and is now its CFO, a key managerial person who signs the accounts and writes the CFO's review in the annual report. He was paid ₹1.9cr in FY26. He is 57.

people.name: Puneet Sharma
people.bio: A commerce graduate from the University of Rajasthan with an MBA from IIPM Delhi, and more than 20 years in building materials and infrastructure products. He has run P&Ls, sales and marketing, distribution networks and new-product launches in leadership roles at building-materials companies (the filing does not name them). He was hired to lead revenue across Greenlam's India businesses.

people.name: B L Sharma
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc., an LLB and an MBA, with about 45 years of experience. He joined Greenlam in September 2013 from Stylam Industries and leads manufacturing excellence across the plants; he is named senior management. He was paid ₹3.2cr in FY26. He is 69.

companies.changes: Head of HR, Admin & CSR Prashant Srivastava resigned on 30 May 2026; Nishit Bansal joined as Chief HR Officer on 22 Sep 2026. Puneet Sharma (Chief Revenue Officer, India) and Mohit Gupta (Head of Internal Audit & Chief Risk Officer) were added to senior management in early 2026. No change in KMP during FY26.

companies.styleNote: Run by the Thakkar family. Founder Krupesh Thakkar is Executive Chairman and his son Rushil is MD (re-appointed to August 2029). A long-serving laminate-plant head sits on the board as whole-time director, and a hired CEO and CFO run strategy and finance. Promoters own 55.10%.

people.name: Krupesh G. Thakkar
people.relation: Founder; father of MD Rushil Thakkar
people.stake: 13.99% in his own name plus 9.15% through his HUF (30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern); he is also a partner in Rushil International, which holds 13.11%; promoter group together 55.10%
people.bio: A commerce graduate with more than 30 years in laminates. He founded Rushil Decor and led its change from a single-product laminate maker into a wider wood-panel company with MDF and exports. He is the best-paid director, at about 25 times the median employee's pay in FY26.

people.name: Rushil K. Thakkar
people.since: Board since August 2021 (whole-time director); MD since September 2024; re-appointed from 13 Aug 2026 to 12 Aug 2029
people.relation: Son of Chairman Krupesh Thakkar
people.stake: 5.12% (1,50,27,960 shares, of which 1,10,00,000 are locked in; FY26 AGM notice and 30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: A commerce graduate (B.Com.) with more than 10 years at Rushil Decor. The company calls him the key architect of its strategic planning, the growth of the MDF division, business expansion, logistics and exports. He is a director of Surya Panel and other family companies and of the Indian Laminates Manufacturers Association. He was paid ₹96 lakh in FY26. He is 34.

people.name: Ramanik T. Kansagara
people.bio: Has more than 32 years in the laminate industry, starting in 1994. He runs production at the laminate plants, raw-material buying and new projects in Gujarat. He is not a member of the promoter family.

people.name: Keyur M. Gajjar
people.bio: An engineer (B.E.) with an MBA and more than 23 years of experience. As CEO he is responsible for strategic planning, running the business and operating efficiency, and he co-signs the CEO/CFO certificate on the accounts.

people.name: Hiren B. Padhya
people.bio: A chartered accountant, company secretary and cost accountant with more than 32 years in financial management. He runs finance as CFO and signs the accounts.

companies.changes: Rushil Thakkar was re-appointed MD for three years from 13 Aug 2026 (approved at the 28 Sep 2026 AGM). No KMP resignations filed in 2026. The statutory auditor declined a second term and a new auditor was appointed in September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Run by Shiv Prakash Mittal and his son Shobhan, one branch of the Mittal family behind Greenply and Greenlam. Shiv Prakash Mittal is Executive Chairman and Shobhan Mittal is MD & CEO; the other four directors are independent. Hired executives run finance, sales, plants, HR and IT. Promoters own 53.26%, mostly through Prime Holdings (39.24%).

people.name: Shiv Prakash Mittal
people.since: Promoter; re-appointed as a director at the August 2025 AGM
people.relation: Promoter; father of MD & CEO Shobhan Mittal; also father of Greenlam's MD Saurabh Mittal (per Greenlam's annual report)
people.stake: nil in his own name (FY26 annual report); promoter group together 53.26%, including 39.24% held by Prime Holdings
people.bio: A science graduate from the University of Calcutta with more than 53 years in the wood-panel industry, covering plywood, laminates, MDF and related products. He spent over two decades at Kitply Industries and then co-founded Greenply Industries. He is also the non-executive chairman of Greenlam Industries. He was paid about ₹1.4cr in FY26.

people.name: Shobhan Mittal
people.since: MD & CEO; retires by rotation and seeks re-appointment at the 2026 AGM
people.relation: Son of Executive Chairman Shiv Prakash Mittal
people.stake: 13.72% (1,66,59,180 shares; FY26 annual report and 30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern, held as a non-resident)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in business administration and has more than 21 years in the wood-panel industry, covering strategy, marketing, manufacturing and business development. He led the building and commissioning of the company's MDF plants at Rudrapur (Uttarakhand) and Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh). Before Greenpanel, he was Joint MD & CEO of Greenply Industries. He was paid about ₹1.5cr in FY26.

people.name: Himanshu Jindal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with more than 22 years in finance, tax, audit, planning, reporting, controls and risk, across consulting, pharmaceuticals, commodity trading, building materials and cable distribution. He previously worked at Orient Bell (as CFO until May 2025), Den Networks and HeidelbergCement India. He took over from long-serving CFO Vishwanathan Venkatramani, who moved to President – Finance and then retired in January 2026.

people.name: Prakash Tripathi
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Gujarat State University with 29 years in sales and distribution. Before joining Greenpanel he was Senior Vice President – Sales at Astral Pipes for about three and a half years, and he has also worked at Ashirvad Pipes, Fischer Building Materials and Pidilite. He replaced Sunil Singh as head of sales in 2025.

companies.changes: No KMP changes filed in 2026. In 2025: CFO Vishwanathan Venkatramani moved aside in June and retired on 1 Jan 2026 (Himanshu Jindal became CFO); President – Strategy Neeladri Basu and Chief Sales Officer Sunil Singh left in May 2025; CIO Jayanta Bhowmik was replaced by Vineet Bansal in August 2025.

companies.styleNote: The listed company is a holding company with no executive directors: promoter Sandip Somany is its non-executive Chairman and a hired professional, Naveen Malik, is both CEO and CFO. But the main business (bathware and pipes) sits in the material subsidiary Hindware Limited, where Sandip Somany is Chairman & MD and his son Shashvat becomes Joint MD from 1 Oct 2026. So the family runs the operating business directly. Promoters own 52.74%, mostly through Somany Impresa (43.31%).

people.name: Sandip Somany
people.role: Chairman (non-executive) of the listed company; Chairman & MD of subsidiary Hindware Limited
people.since: Promoter; non-executive Chairman of the listed company
people.relation: Promoter; father of Shashvat Somany
people.stake: 8.75% in his own name plus 0.14% through his HUF (30 Jun 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 52.74%, including 43.31% through Somany Impresa
people.bio: A commerce graduate with a diploma in ceramic manufacturing technology from the US, and more than four decades in the ceramics and glass industry. The Somany Impresa group also includes glass-packaging maker AGI Greenpac, where he is Chairman & MD. He is a past President of FICCI, of the International Chamber of Commerce's India chapter and of the PHD Chamber, and chairs the Indian Council of Sanitaryware Manufacturers. He also sits on the boards of JK Paper, HEG and Indraprastha Medical. He is about 62.

people.name: Shashvat Somany
people.role: Joint MD of subsidiary Hindware Limited (from 1 Oct 2026); non-executive director of the listed company (from 1 Jul 2026)
people.since: Listed-company board from July 2026; Joint MD of Hindware Limited for five years from October 2026
people.relation: Son of Chairman Sandip Somany
people.bio: Holds an MBA in technology and analytics from London Business School and a BA in economics and psychology from UCLA. He worked in consulting, advising consumer-appliance, FMCG and telecom clients. He is Head of Strategy for the Somany Impresa group (AGI Greenpac and Hindware) and founded Tattva, the group's corporate venture-capital arm. He is being brought in as Joint MD of Hindware Limited, the bathware and pipes business, and joined the listed company's board as a non-executive director.

people.name: Naveen Malik
people.role: Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer
people.bio: A chartered accountant, LL.B. and Delhi University commerce graduate with more than 29 years of experience in project finance, investor relations, foreign-currency borrowing, treasury, overseas subsidiaries, indirect tax, insurance, ERP roll-outs, internal audit and accounts. He was the company's CFO and was also made CEO in May 2024 after CEO Salil Kapoor resigned in March 2024. He signs the accounts and the CEO/CFO certificate.

companies.changes: Shashvat Somany joined the listed board on 1 Jul 2026 and becomes Joint MD of subsidiary Hindware Limited on 1 Oct 2026. Vice President (sourcing & NPD) Nikhil Maheshwari resigned from 30 Jun 2026. President – Sales Mahesh Choudhary left in October 2025; Nitesh Raj became Business Head – Consumer in August 2025. Non-executive director Girdhari Lal Sultania left in March 2026 and Ram Babu Kabra joined.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Jhunjhunwala family's LNJ Bhilwara group. Since the split on 1 September 2026 the listed share is HEG Advanced Materials, and Riju Jhunjhunwala, the third generation, is its Chairman, MD and CEO. His father Ravi Jhunjhunwala, who ran HEG as MD from 1989, now runs the electrode company HEG Graphite and sits on this board as a non-executive director. Group CFO O.P. Ajmera is also a non-executive director. Hired professionals run finance and the two battery businesses. After Bhilwara Energy merged in, promoters own 60.72% (8 Sep 2026), mainly through Redrose Vanijya LLP (28.40%), LNJ Spark Advisory LLP (12.29%) and RSWM (4.82%).

people.name: Riju Jhunjhunwala
people.since: Board as Vice Chairman before the split; CMD & CEO since 1 Sep 2026 (five years to Aug 2031, subject to shareholder approval)
people.relation: Promoter; son of Ravi Jhunjhunwala (non-executive director here; CMD of HEG Graphite); grandson of group founder L.N. Jhunjhunwala
people.stake: 6,782 shares in his own name, a negligible fraction (8 Sep 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 60.72%
people.bio: Holds a degree in business management studies from the University of Bradford, UK. He joined the family's LNJ Bhilwara group after graduating and was Joint MD and then MD of RSWM, the group's textile company, from October 2003 to April 2009. He was an executive director of HEG from April 2009 to July 2010, then MD of Bhilwara Energy from August 2010 until it merged into this company. He was HEG's non-executive Vice Chairman before the split and now leads its anode, graphene, battery-pack and green-power businesses. He is also Chairman & MD of RSWM, so his time is split across group companies.

people.name: Neha Rajvanshi
people.since: CFO since 1 Sep 2026; joined Bhilwara Energy in April 2026
people.bio: A chartered accountant with an MBA from Amity University, master's and bachelor's degrees in commerce, and a management programme from IIM Lucknow. She has about 18 years of experience across renewable energy, oil and gas, and infrastructure. She was CFO of Serentica Renewables, where she handled capital structuring and debt and equity fund-raising for large clean-energy projects, and earlier held leadership roles at Azure Power and Bharat Petroleum (BPCL). She joined Bhilwara Energy in April 2026 as Senior Vice President – Finance, was made President – Finance, and moved to this company as CFO when Bhilwara Energy merged in.

people.name: Ankur Khaitan
people.role: Managing Director & CEO, TACC (the anode subsidiary)
people.since: Named in the company's leadership team, Sep 2026
people.bio: Has more than 17 years in graphite and carbon materials. At HEG he led marketing for the graphite specialties business and international business development across Europe and the CIS region. He now runs TACC, the subsidiary building the synthetic graphite anode plant that is this company's main growth bet. He studied at IIM Ahmedabad, the University of Texas at Austin and Annamalai University.

people.name: Hiren Pravin Shah
people.role: Managing Director & CEO, Replus (battery packs and energy storage)
people.since: Named in the company's leadership team, Sep 2026
people.bio: Founder of Replus, the lithium-ion battery-pack and energy-storage business that is now part of this company. He has more than 25 years in lithium-ion battery technology and renewable energy and earlier held leadership roles at Panasonic and Delta Electronics. The company says he developed Replus's patented battery designs.

people.name: Ravi Gupta
people.since: 1 Sep 2026 (Company Secretary of Bhilwara Energy since July 2009)
people.bio: A commerce graduate and law graduate of Delhi University and a fellow member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. He has more than 25 years in banking, finance, accounts, legal and secretarial work, including fund-raising, debt financing, acquisitions and divestments. He was Company Secretary of Bhilwara Energy from July 2009 and moved here when it merged in.

companies.changes: The split took effect on 1 Sep 2026. Ravi Jhunjhunwala gave up the CMD & CEO post here to lead HEG Graphite and stays as a non-executive director. Executive Director Manish Gulati, CFO Ravi Kant Tripathi and Company Secretary Vivek Chaudhary moved to HEG Graphite; Neha Rajvanshi and Ravi Gupta replaced them. Strategy head Puneet Anand ceased to be key managerial personnel on 1 Sep 2026, and President – Investor Relations Salil Bawa resigned on 14 Sep 2026. Riju Jhunjhunwala's appointment still needs shareholder approval.

companies.styleNote: The Austrian-listed RHI Magnesita group owns 56.07% through three Dutch holding companies (Dutch US Holding 40.03%, Dutch Brasil Holding 9.99%, VRD Americas 6.06%). No family is involved; the parent appoints hired managers. Parmod Sagar, MD & CEO for 13 years, became non-executive Chairman on 1 July 2026, and Pankaj Malhan, hired from Jindal Steel, took over as MD & CEO.

people.name: Pankaj Malhan
people.role: Managing Director & CEO; President – India Region
people.since: 1 Jul 2026 (five-year term, subject to shareholder approval)
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in instrumentation and control from Dr B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar, and a postgraduate qualification in business management from XLRI Jamshedpur. He has about three decades in steel, manufacturing, industrial materials and infrastructure. Just before joining he was Executive Director – Odisha at Jindal Steel and also led its sales and marketing; earlier he held leadership roles at JSW Steel, Vedanta Resources, Tata Steel and Tata BlueScope. He has sat on the boards of JSW Steel Coated Products, ESL Steel and Ferro Alloys Corporation. He won ASSOCHAM's CEO of the Year award (2019) and ET Now's Business Leader of the Year – Manufacturing (2020). As a steel-industry insider he knows the company's customers from the buying side.

people.name: Azim Syed
people.since: Head of finance for India since April 2024 (CFO from 1 May 2024); whole-time director until 30 Jun 2026
people.bio: Joined the RHI Magnesita group in 2019, where he was responsible for global supply chain and integrated business planning before moving to India as head of finance in 2024. His earlier career was in supply-chain roles across hi-tech, telecom, consumer goods, retail and manufacturing, focused on supply-chain transformation. He led the transport-management and 'Everest' digital systems roll-outs at the group. He stepped off the board on 30 June 2026 for personal reasons but continues as CFO.

people.name: Sanjay Kumar
people.since: Company Secretary at least since FY25
people.bio: An associate member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. He is one of the company's three key managerial personnel, with the MD & CEO and the CFO, and signs its stock-exchange filings.

people.name: Jyotirmoy Bhattacharjee
people.role: Head of Steel Sales – India Region
people.bio: Has 29 years in the Indian refractory industry across sales and marketing, field operations and business excellence. He joined the group in 2005 as a sales manager and headed its technical marketing department for 12 years before becoming head of steel sales for India. The company says its India steel sales grew from about €20 million in 2005 to about €400 million under the steel team, as Indian steel output rose from 35 to 135 million tonnes.

people.name: Sanat Ganguli
people.role: Head of Industrial & Iron Making – India Region
people.since: Joined with the Dalmia refractory business
people.bio: Has 19 years in refractories and metals, in operations and technology, strategy, and sales and marketing. Before Dalmia's refractory business merged into RHI Magnesita India he was business head of the Dalmia–Seven Refractories joint venture, which the company calls the fastest-growing monolithics business, and chief strategy officer for international business at Dalmia OCL. He has an engineering degree in ceramic technology and executive courses from Wharton, MIT and TMTC.

people.name: Abhishek Sharma
people.bio: Has about 26 years in manufacturing in chemicals, polymers, pulp and fibre. He worked at Reliance Industries, Indorama Synthetics and SRF before joining the company in 2023, and now runs its Indian plants.

companies.changes: Parmod Sagar resigned as MD & CEO on 30 Jun 2026 for personal reasons and stayed as non-executive Chairman; Pankaj Malhan became MD & CEO on 1 Jul 2026. CFO Azim Syed resigned as a whole-time director the same day but continues as CFO. The FY26 annual report was not yet filed when this was written.

companies.styleNote: Run by the Kolkata-based S.K. Bajoria group. Executive Chairman Shishir Bajoria is the promoter, and his son Mihir Bajoria became MD on 1 March 2026, replacing the hired MD James McIntosh. A hired Director & CEO India, Mukesh Rawal, runs the Indian plants from 16 August 2026. Promoters own 72.43%, almost all through Bajoria Financial Services (67.32%).

people.name: Shishir Kumar Bajoria
people.since: Board since Sep 2007; re-appointed Executive Chairman Apr 2026 to Mar 2029
people.relation: Promoter; father of MD Mihir Bajoria
people.stake: 4.11% in his own name, 4.23% with spouse and dependent children (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); his HUF holds another 0.87%; promoter group together 72.43%, mostly via Bajoria Financial Services
people.bio: A B.Com (Hons) graduate with about 50 years in business; he is 69. He is the promoter of the S.K. Bajoria group, which besides refractories runs insurance broking and health-insurance claims administration businesses. He has been the key decision-maker at IFGL and its predecessor companies. He is a former President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and a former director of West Bengal's and Odisha's state industrial development corporations, and has been knighted by Denmark and Italy. He was paid ₹331 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Mihir Prakash Bajoria
people.since: Board since May 2025; MD since 1 Mar 2026 (to Feb 2029)
people.relation: Son of Executive Chairman Shishir Bajoria
people.bio: Holds a diploma in international relations, politics and economy from Oxford Brookes University and completed the International Baccalaureate at Sevenoaks School. He has about 16 years in the refractory business. He was on the board of the UK subsidiary Monocon International Refractories from 2010 and its Chairman from 2015 to August 2025, overseeing the overseas subsidiaries from the UK before moving to Kolkata. He joined the IFGL board in May 2025 and took over as MD from the hired MD James McIntosh. About 3.8% of votes cast opposed his appointment. He is 41.

people.name: Mukesh Harshadrai Rawal
people.since: Board since Apr 2026; Director & CEO India from 16 Aug 2026 (three years, subject to shareholder and central government approval)
people.relation: Not related to any director
people.bio: A US citizen of Indian origin with a bachelor's degree in metallurgical engineering. He joined the IFGL group in 1983 and has long experience in refractories and in the iron and steel industry. Until 15 August 2026 he was President of the US subsidiary Mono Ceramics and head of the group's Americas business. He replaced Arasu Shanmugam, who resigned in April 2026, to run the Indian operations.

people.name: Rajesh Agarwal
people.since: Whole-time director since Nov 2022 (re-appointed to Nov 2028)
people.bio: A B.Sc graduate and fellow member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, with about 42 years of experience in corporate law, taxation and legal matters. He was Company Secretary of the erstwhile Indo Flogates, the erstwhile IFGL Refractories and this company before joining the board as Director – General Counsel. He is 63.

people.name: Amit Agarwal
people.bio: A B.Com (Hons) graduate of St. Xavier's College, Kolkata, and a chartered accountant. He joined IFGL in 2012 as a senior manager in accounts and finance and rose to CFO.

people.name: Hirdesh Sehgal
people.bio: An IIT graduate in mechanical engineering with about 38 years in refractories across projects, production, maintenance, engineering, product design and business development. He has done management programmes at IIM Ahmedabad, TMTC and ISB. The company says he led about ₹600cr of projects in the last six years, including robotics and automation, high-temperature furnaces, tap-hole clay and black refractories lines.

people.name: Mansi Damani
people.since: With the S.K. Bajoria group since 2002
people.bio: A fellow member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India with a postgraduate diploma in business administration (finance) from Symbiosis, Pune. She joined the S.K. Bajoria group in 2002 and has more than 20 years in the refractory business, handling legal, tax and secretarial compliance.

companies.changes: Director & CEO India Arasu Shanmugam resigned on 6 Apr 2026; Mukesh Rawal took over on 16 Aug 2026 (postal ballot for his appointment issued 8 Sep 2026). Hired MD James McIntosh left on 28 Feb 2026 and Mihir Bajoria succeeded him. Director Wayne Vardy resigned on 31 May 2026. Chief Research Officer N.K. Mishra and Chief Procurement Officer Sanjoy Gangopadhyay resigned in May and April 2026. Akshay Bajoria was promoted to President – Business Development & Strategy on 15 Jul 2026. Ashok Kumar Kedia and Frank Mitchell became Co-Presidents of the US subsidiary Mono Ceramics on 16 Aug 2026.

companies.styleNote: Promoter Prayasvin Patel is Chairman & Managing Director. His son-in-law Aayush Shah becomes an executive director from 1 October 2026, and his brother-in-law Pradip Patel sits on the board as a non-executive director. Hired professionals run finance and the two divisions. Promoters own about 59%.

people.name: Prayasvin B. Patel
people.since: Board since 1983; MD from 1993, CMD from 2006; re-appointed for 3 years from 1 July 2026
people.relation: Promoter; father-in-law of Aayush Shah; brother-in-law of director Pradip Patel
people.stake: 1.75% (39,25,864 shares, FY26 annual report); promoters together about 59%
people.bio: Prayasvin Patel has a mechanical engineering degree from Sardar Patel University and an MBA from Loyola University Chicago. He began as sales director of Prayas Casting, joined Elecon as joint managing director, became managing director in 1993 and chairman & managing director in 2006. He built the gear division into what the company calls Asia's largest industrial gear maker and led its first overseas acquisition, Benzlers-Radicon, bought from David Brown Gear Systems. He is also an executive director of the listed Eimco Elecon (India) and a director of several Elecon group companies. His FY26 pay included a ₹15cr commission.

people.name: Aayush A. Shah
people.since: Board since April 2023 (non-executive); executive director from 1 October 2026
people.relation: Son-in-law of the Chairman & MD, Prayasvin Patel
people.bio: Aayush Shah has a mechanical engineering degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in the US. He is chief executive and executive director of Power Build Private Limited, an Elecon group company. He joined Elecon's board as a non-executive director in April 2023. The board made him an executive director from 1 October 2026 so he can take on more day-to-day operating work, which the company describes as part of its leadership continuity plan. He was born in 1994.

people.name: Chintan J. Shah
people.bio: Chintan Shah became CFO on 15 April 2026, replacing Narasimhan Raghunathan, who left on 31 January 2026. He has about 19 years in finance and accounts, with experience in Big Four consulting, IT services, engineering, medical devices and chemicals. His work has covered financial strategy, risk management, project monitoring, listing compliance and investor relations.

people.name: Dipak S. Dalwadi
people.bio: Dipak Dalwadi took charge of the gear division, Elecon's main business, on 1 August 2025, replacing Man Mohan Nanda at the end of his tenure. He is named as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his education or earlier career.

people.name: Kaushik M. Patel
people.bio: Kaushik Patel has run the material handling equipment division since 27 May 2025, replacing Pranav Kumar Bhasin. In FY26 the division's revenue grew about 44% to ₹667cr as it shifted towards product supply and after-sales service. The company has not published his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: CFO Narasimhan Raghunathan resigned on 31 January 2026; Chintan Shah took over on 15 April 2026. Both division heads changed in 2025. Aayush Shah moves from non-executive to executive director on 1 October 2026.

companies.styleNote: Co-founder Nikhil Kumar is Managing Director. The other co-founder, Mohib Khericha, is non-executive Chairman. A hired CEO, Deepak Kumar Sinha, joined in April 2026 to run operations. Promoters owned about 27% in March 2026 and were issued ₹75cr of new shares in September 2026.

people.name: Nikhil Kumar
people.since: Promoter since 1999; MD since 2012; re-appointed from 17 January 2026
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter
people.stake: 8.30% (31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoters together about 27%
people.bio: Nikhil Kumar is an engineering graduate of Karnataka Regional Engineering College, Surathkal, and did the General Management Programme at Harvard Business School. Before TD Power he worked at Kirloskar Electric. He co-founded the company in April 1999 and has been managing director since 2012, covering strategy, technology tie-ups and sales. He has more than 30 years in electric rotating machines. He is also managing director of the German subsidiary TD Power Systems Europe and draws part of his pay from it. He sold some shares in FY26, cutting his stake from 11.2% to 8.3%.

people.name: Deepak Kumar Sinha
people.bio: Deepak Kumar Sinha has an electrical engineering degree from Bhagalpur Engineering College and a postgraduate diploma in business administration from IIM Kozhikode. He has more than 30 years in the power sector. He was previously chief executive and whole-time director of L&T-MHI Power Turbine Generators, which makes large turbines and generators for thermal power plants. Before that he held senior management, technology and operations roles at GE Power and other companies. He joined TD Power as CEO on 3 April 2026.

people.name: M. N. Varalakshmi
people.bio: M. N. Varalakshmi has been CFO since 2018, when she replaced K. G. Prabhakar on his retirement. She was earlier Manager, Finance & Accounts at the company, so she rose from within. She studied at the University of Pune.

people.name: Ramakrishna Varna
people.bio: Ramakrishna Varna was made Chief Technical Officer on 15 October 2025 and is listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his education or earlier career.

people.name: Vinay Hegde
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Vinay Hegde leads global sales and marketing and is named as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: Deepak Kumar Sinha joined as CEO on 3 April 2026. Head of Operations Sanju Davis, appointed in October 2025, left on 12 March 2026. A September 2026 EGM approved a ₹75cr preferential issue to promoters and a QIP.

companies.styleNote: The Sawhney family runs it. Dhruv Sawhney is Chairman & Managing Director and his son Nikhil is Vice Chairman & Managing Director. His other son Tarun, who runs sister company Triveni Engineering, is a non-executive director. Day-to-day operations are run by a hired CEO and COO. Promoters own 55.8%.

people.name: Dhruv M. Sawhney
people.since: Board since 2011 (demerger); current term 10 May 2024 to 9 May 2029
people.relation: Promoter; father of Nikhil Sawhney (VCMD) and Tarun Sawhney (non-executive director)
people.stake: 8.22% in his own name; 28.4% including shares he owns beneficially (FY26 annual report); promoters together 55.8%
people.bio: Dhruv Sawhney has a master's in mechanical sciences from Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and an MBA with distinction from Wharton. He chairs the Triveni group, which includes Triveni Turbine and the sugar and engineering company Triveni Engineering & Industries. He was president of the Confederation of Indian Industry in 1991-92 and co-chaired the Indo-French CEOs' Forum for ten years. He was the founding chairman of IIM Kashipur for nine years. France gave him the Legion d'Honneur and the UK made him an honorary LVO. He is 82 and drew ₹7.4cr from the company in FY26.

people.name: Nikhil Sawhney
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Dhruv Sawhney; brother of Tarun Sawhney
people.bio: Nikhil Sawhney has a BA and MA from Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and an MBA from Wharton. He is also a director of Triveni Engineering & Industries. Under him the company made Forbes Asia's 'Best Under A Billion' list in 2024 and 2025. He co-founded the CII-Triveni Water Institute and is a former chairman of CII's Northern Region. He was the best-paid executive in FY26, at ₹11.5cr including ₹6cr of commission.

people.name: S. N. Prasad
people.bio: S. Narayana Prasad graduated in mechanical engineering from Nagarjuna University in 1991 and has a postgraduate diploma in computer applications. He has more than 30 years of experience across marketing, global sales, project execution, engineering, supply chain and service. Before becoming CEO on 1 April 2024 he was President and Global Business Head of the product business, which he grew across more than 100 countries.

people.name: Sachin Parab
people.bio: Sachin Parab graduated in mechanical engineering from Walchand College of Engineering in 1991 and has a postgraduate diploma from the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (1994). Before becoming COO on 1 April 2024 he was President and Business Head of the aftermarket business, which the company is pushing hard. He has attended management programmes at IIM Ahmedabad and Harvard Business School.

people.name: Lalit Kumar Agarwal
people.bio: Lalit Agarwal is a commerce graduate of H.L. College of Commerce, has an MBA and is a cost accountant. He was finance general manager at Cadila Pharmaceuticals (1998–2008), senior finance manager at Asian Paints (2008–2016) and finance general manager at Schneider Electric (2016–2019). He briefly worked at Riau Andalan Pulp & Paper before joining Triveni as Vice President Finance in October 2019. The company credits him with the due diligence for its first overseas acquisition and with its credit rating upgrade to AA+.

people.name: P. U. Gopi
people.role: Executive Vice President & Chief Technology Officer
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: P. U. Gopi graduated in mechanical engineering from NIT Surathkal in 1988 and has an MBA in finance from Bangalore University (1994). He has more than 35 years in industrial turbomachinery and previously worked at Alstom Power and CICB-Elliott compressors. As CTO he runs project engineering, product development and validation, including the turbines that use CO₂ as the working fluid.

companies.changes: Nikhil Sawhney was re-appointed for five years from 10 May 2026. Head of Investor Relations Surabhi Chandna resigned in November 2025.

companies.styleNote: A subsidiary of GE Vernova: GE Steam Power International BV owns 68.58%. GE Vernova executives run it. The non-executive chairman, Craig Richards, is a GE Vernova regional manager. In July 2024 the parent dropped its plan to exit and stop being promoter. No family involvement.

people.name: Puneet Bhatla
people.bio: Puneet Bhatla has a mechanical engineering degree and more than 36 years in the power sector. He worked at NTPC, BHEL and Siemens India in engineering, product management, project execution, business development, JV negotiations and technology licensing for steam, nuclear and gas turbines. At GE Steam Power he led India services operations. He now also leads GE's Steam Power India growth areas: core and upgrade services, air-quality control equipment and the Durgapur factory. He has been a co-opted member of Aligarh Muslim University's mechanical engineering board of studies since 2020.

people.name: Shrikar Thakur
people.bio: Shrikar Thakur has a mechanical engineering degree from BIT Mesra and an MBA in international business from IIFT New Delhi, and is a graduate of GE's Accelerated Leadership Program. He has more than 17 years in power, infrastructure, manufacturing and EPC, with roles in India, France and the US. Before GE he worked at the Alstom Bharat Forge joint venture and the Kalyani Group. At GE he set up and led the project management office for Steam Power India and is now India New Build Leader, in charge of large power and EPC projects. He was named senior management in May 2025 and joined the board on 1 July 2026, aged 39.

people.name: Rahul Rojal
people.bio: Rahul Rojal is a chartered accountant with more than 16 years in financial reporting, controllership, audit and governance. He started at PwC, where he spent six years in audit, then spent seven years in finance at another listed company. At GE Power India he rose to Senior Financial Reporting Manager and worked on demergers, slump sales, carve-outs and valuations. He became CFO on 19 June 2026.

companies.changes: Whole-time director and CFO Aashish Ghai resigned with effect from 13 May 2026. Company secretary Kamna Tiwari resigned on 2 April 2026; Vipul Sharma replaced her from 19 June 2026. The NSE/BSE ticker changed from GEPIL to GVPIL in August 2025.

companies.styleNote: The Desai family runs it. Brothers Kushal Desai (Chairman, MD & CEO) and Chaitanya Desai (MD) each own 22.7%. Kushal's son Rishabh became a whole-time director in September 2025. Kushal's daughter and son-in-law also work in the company. Hired CEOs run the cables and conductor businesses. Promoters owned about 58% before the August 2026 QIP and about 55% after it.

people.name: Kushal N. Desai
people.since: Chairman & Managing Director; family has run Apar for three generations
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Chaitanya Desai; father of Rishabh Desai and of Gaurangi Mehra (Director, Marketing & Communications)
people.stake: 22.70% (FY26 annual report); promoters together about 58% in March 2026, about 55% after the August 2026 QIP
people.bio: Kushal Desai has two bachelor's degrees from the University of Pennsylvania: electrical engineering (Moore School) and economics (Wharton). In 1997 he co-founded APAR Infotech, a systems integration software company, and worked there until 2004, when it listed on NASDAQ. He runs Apar jointly with his brother and is also its CEO. He sits on the boards of Dharmsinh Desai University and the DDMM heart hospital in Nadiad. His FY26 pay was ₹15.3cr, mostly commission.

people.name: Chaitanya N. Desai
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Kushal Desai; uncle of Rishabh Desai
people.bio: Chaitanya Desai has two bachelor's degrees from the University of Pennsylvania: chemical engineering and economics (Wharton). He joined Apar in 1993 in the polymer division, which had a technical tie-up with Goodyear. He turned that business around and ran it for 15 years until it was sold to a European multinational. He then took charge of the conductor business and also has a strategic role in cables. He sits on IEEMA's executive council. He was up for re-appointment by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Rishabh K. Desai
people.since: Whole-time director from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2030 (earlier a non-executive director)
people.relation: Son of Kushal Desai; nephew of Chaitanya Desai
people.bio: Rishabh Desai has a bachelor's in business management and entrepreneurship from Babson College in the US (2014). He worked for a year at Ergon, a US oil refiner, then led the construction of a factory in 2015 and operations in the Middle East and North Africa. He now runs the speciality oils business and is the only executive director paid partly by a subsidiary. He moved from non-executive to whole-time director in September 2025.

people.name: Ramesh S. Iyer
people.bio: Ramesh Iyer is a chartered accountant, cost accountant and company secretary. He had about 22 years in finance when he joined Apar as CFO on 3 February 2022. Before that he was CFO of Nitco from 2020 to 2021.

people.name: Chandrashekhar Shrotri
people.bio: Chandrashekhar Shrotri has more than 35 years in sales, marketing, business development, product management and general management across India, Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East. Before Apar he was at Siemens, most recently as Segment CEO for a region covering South Asia, Southeast Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and Australia (22 countries). He replaced Shashi Amin, who resigned in December 2025.

people.name: Manish Agrawal
people.role: CEO, Conductors & Telecommunications; MD, APAR T&D
people.since: Listed on the company's management page
people.bio: Manish Agrawal runs the conductor and telecom cable businesses and is managing director of APAR T&D. He has more than 27 years in the power and telecom sectors and specialises in transmission and distribution. The company describes him as a Harvard alumnus but does not name the programme.

companies.changes: Cables CEO Shashi Amin resigned in December 2025; Chandrashekhar Shrotri replaced him from 4 December 2025. Rishabh Desai became a whole-time director on 1 September 2025. A ₹2,500cr QIP in August 2026 diluted the promoters.

companies.styleNote: Genus is part of the Kailash Group of the Agarwal family. Ishwar Chand Agarwal is Executive Chairman. Two of his sons are executives: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal (MD & CEO) and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal (Joint MD). A third son, Kailash Chandra Agarwal, is non-executive Vice-Chairman. Each of the three executives was paid about ₹21cr in FY26. Promoters own about 39%, mostly through group companies.

people.name: Ishwar Chand Agarwal
people.since: Board since 1994; current term 24 January 2024 to 23 January 2029
people.relation: Promoter; father of Kailash Chandra, Rajendra Kumar and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.stake: 0.89% in his own name (27,02,491 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 39%
people.bio: Ishwar Chand Agarwal is a commerce graduate with more than five decades in business. The family group spans power infrastructure, paper, coal and coke, apparel and agricultural commodities. He is described as focused on strategy, expansion and succession planning. He is 76, has been on the board since May 1994, and was paid ₹21.2cr in FY26. He is also a director of other group companies, including Kailash Industries and Genus Paper & Boards.

people.name: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal
people.since: Board since 2001; current term 29 May 2024 to 28 May 2029
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Ishwar Chand Agarwal; brother of Kailash Chandra and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.bio: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal has a B.E. in electronics. He has spent his career in power distribution, covering smart metering, smart grid, solar panels and batteries. He sets the company's strategy and product direction and oversees technology, R&D, alliances and partnerships. He joined the board in January 2001, is 50, and was paid ₹20.6cr in FY26.

people.name: Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.since: Board since 2004; current term 20 September 2024 to 19 September 2029
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Ishwar Chand Agarwal; brother of Kailash Chandra and Rajendra Kumar Agarwal
people.bio: Jitendra Kumar Agarwal has an MBA in marketing. He leads marketing, branding and sales in power distribution and power backup, including finding new business, trade shows and digital marketing. He also has experience with operating-expenditure (Opex) business models such as the smart-meter contracts. He joined the board in May 2004, is 49, and was paid ₹20.6cr in FY26.

people.name: Nathu Lal Nama
people.since: Whole-time director from 9 February 2026 (2-year term); CFO until 18 May 2026
people.bio: Nathu Lal Nama is a chartered accountant with more than 36 years in finance and accounts, covering planning, budgeting, audits, working capital, costing and internal controls. He was Genus's chief finance officer and joined the board as a whole-time director in February 2026. When a new CFO was hired in May 2026 he gave up the CFO role but stayed on the board as an executive director. He is 61.

people.name: Vinod Raheja
people.bio: Vinod Raheja is a chartered accountant with more than 33 years in senior finance roles, including as CFO in several industries. His experience covers M&A, restructuring, fundraising, working capital, taxation, risk management and ERP/SAP systems. The company did not name his earlier employers. He is 57 and joined as CFO on 18 May 2026.

companies.changes: Vinod Raheja became CFO on 18 May 2026, and Nathu Lal Nama moved out of the CFO role but stayed as a whole-time director. Two chief human resources officers left in FY26 (June 2025 and March 2026); a third joined in May 2026.

companies.styleNote: A founder-family company. Founder R. Doraiswamy, 83, is Managing Director and his elder son D. Rajesh Kumar is Joint MD. His younger son Vishnu Rangaswamy is a non-executive director. A CFO was hired from outside in April 2026; before that the Joint MD also acted as CFO. Promoters own 37.5%, much of it through group companies.

people.name: R. Doraiswamy
people.relation: Founder; father of D. Rajesh Kumar (Joint MD) and Vishnu Rangaswamy (director)
people.bio: R. Doraiswamy is an electrical engineering graduate who has run Salzer since it started in 1985. The company credits him with bringing the Salzer group's electrical installation products up to international quality standards. Shareholders re-appointed him for three years from 1 May 2026 by postal ballot, at 83. The terms are a monthly salary of ₹6.5 lakh plus 2.5% of net profit as commission. He was paid about ₹1.1cr in FY25.

people.name: D. Rajesh Kumar
people.since: More than three decades at Salzer; Joint MD (and CFO until 31 March 2026); re-appointment for 5 years from 1 October 2026 put to the September 2026 AGM
people.relation: Son of the founder-MD, R. Doraiswamy; elder brother of director Vishnu Rangaswamy
people.bio: Rajesh Kumar has worked at Salzer for more than 30 years in finance, planning, treasury and operations. He was Joint MD and CFO (latest term from October 2021) until April 2026, when a separate CFO was hired, and he stayed on as Joint MD. The board credits him with capacity expansion, product diversification and about 23% sales growth a year over the last five years. He is also a director of group companies including Kaycee Industries (a listed subsidiary), Salzer Exports and Salzer EV Infra, and a nominee director on Ultrafast Chargers, its EV-charger partner.

people.name: Raman Krishnamoorthy (K. Raman)
people.bio: K. Raman joined as CFO on 1 April 2026, taking the CFO role from Joint MD Rajesh Kumar. Management said he was hired to strengthen financial governance and planning for the next phase of growth. The company has not published his education or earlier employers.

people.name: M. Lakshminarayana
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: M. Lakshminarayana heads operations and is first on the list of senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his background.

companies.changes: K. Raman became CFO on 1 April 2026; Rajesh Kumar gave up the CFO title and stayed Joint MD. In FY26 some designated insiders made contra trades and traded during the closed window. They paid back ₹4.8 lakh of profit and ₹3.25 lakh of penalties, and the company reported this to SEBI in March 2026.

companies.styleNote: A single family runs it. Founder Ashok Kumar Agarwal is Chairman & MD, his son Ankit Agrawal is CEO, and Ankit's wife Neha Agarwal is a whole-time director and also acting CFO. There has been no dedicated CFO since April 2025. The three executives have personally guaranteed bank loans and lent money to the company. Promoters own about 52%.

people.name: Ashok Kumar Agarwal
people.relation: Founder; father of Ankit Agrawal; father-in-law of Neha Agarwal
people.stake: 22.64% (FY26 annual report); promoter family together about 52%
people.bio: Ashok Kumar Agarwal founded the company in 1994 in a small workshop in Jaipur's Malviya Nagar. It began as a metal-castings business and grew into switchgear panels, meter boxes and enclosures for power utilities. He has more than four decades in the electrical industry. He sets strategy and chairs the board, and the company says his recent focus has been certified 'intelligent' products such as PulseBox and how capital is spent. The company has not published his education.

people.name: Ankit Agrawal
people.relation: Son of the founder, Ashok Kumar Agarwal; husband of Neha Agarwal
people.bio: Ankit Agrawal has 23 years in the industry. He runs growth, diversification and the technology programme, and is responsible for sales, marketing and quality. He is the company's main contact for investors and analysts. The company's Jaipur premises include plots he owns personally. He raised his stake from 9.7% to 17.7% during FY26. The company has not published his education.

people.name: Neha Agarwal
people.role: Whole-time Director & Chief Financial Officer (additional charge)
people.since: Board since June 2016; acting CFO since 4 July 2025
people.relation: Wife of CEO Ankit Agrawal; daughter-in-law of the Chairman & MD
people.bio: Neha Agarwal has about 14–16 years in management, administration and operations at the company, and oversees daily operations. She took the extra charge of CFO on 4 July 2025 after CFO Anand Chaturvedi left in April 2025. She is steering the move to Main Board reporting. She also leads the company's CSR work and is a director of the solar subsidiaries RMC Green Energy and RMC Solar One, Two, Three and Five. She was born in 1982.

people.name: Manish Mantri
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Manish Mantri is a chemical engineering graduate of MREC (now MNIT) Jaipur with about 30 years in manufacturing and services. He set up new plants at the Aditya Birla Group and RR Kabel, led high-voltage and extra-high-voltage projects at Sterlite Technologies, and managed large EPC and EHV projects at KEI Industries.

people.name: Vikash Verma
people.bio: Vikash Verma has been a chartered accountant since 2005 and has more than 22 years of experience. He previously worked at South Asia LPG Company, the joint venture between Hindustan Petroleum and TotalEnergies. He is one of two chartered accountants hired in the second quarter of FY26 to rebuild the finance team, and was later named senior management.

people.name: Sajal Kumar Ghosh
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Sajal Kumar Ghosh has 33 years in Indian manufacturing and specialises in polymers and composites. His work covers materials science, product development, technical services and R&D. It supports the SMC and FRP moulding capability that the PulseBox smart box relies on.

companies.changes: CFO Anand Chaturvedi left on 16 April 2025, and Neha Agarwal has held the CFO role as an additional charge since July 2025. Shivani Bairathi became company secretary in June 2025. The company moved to BSE's Main Board and listed on NSE on 1 April 2026.

companies.styleNote: Part of the INOXGFL group controlled by Vivek Jain's family. His son Devansh Jain, who started the company, is a whole-time director and leads the group's renewables businesses. A hired CEO runs day-to-day operations, and the group's renewables CEO sits above him. Promoters own about 44%, mainly through Inox Leasing & Finance (27.7%) and two LLPs. The 2026 AGM notice seeks approval for loans of up to ₹600cr from Devansh Jain.

people.name: Devansh Jain
people.since: Started Inox Wind in 2009; whole-time director
people.relation: Promoter; son of INOXGFL group chairman Vivek Jain
people.stake: 0.004% in his own name (63,200 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 44%
people.bio: Devansh Jain has a double major in economics and business administration from Carnegie Mellon University in the US. He set up Inox Wind as the group's move into renewables, took it public in 2015 and listed Inox Green, a wind-farm maintenance company, in 2022. He is also building INOX Solar (solar cells and modules), GFCL EV (battery chemicals) and INOX Clean Energy, an IPP with about 3,000 MW of wind and solar capacity. He has held roles at PHDCCI, FICCI, IWPA and YPO, and was on Fortune's '40 Under 40' list in 2023–2025.

people.name: Manoj Dixit
people.since: Re-appointed for 2 years from 3 December 2025; with the INOXGFL group since 2008
people.bio: Manoj Dixit has a master's in mechanical engineering and more than 27 years in power project development, power scheduling, land acquisition and regulatory approvals. Before joining the INOXGFL group in 2008 he worked at Perfect Refractories and Gujarat Fluorochemicals.

people.name: Sanjeev Agarwal
people.bio: Sanjeev Agarwal has a mechanical engineering degree from IIT Roorkee and an MBA from Pune University. He has more than 34 years in project execution, sales, supply chain and change management across T&D, fossil power and nuclear steam turbines, in Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Europe. He previously worked at TBW, Alstom, GE and KEC International. He became CEO on 1 June 2025, replacing Kailash Lal Tarachandani, who moved up to group CEO for renewables.

people.name: Kailash Lal Tarachandani
people.role: Group Chief Executive Officer, Renewables Business
people.since: Joined as CEO in May 2013; group renewables CEO from June 2025
people.bio: Kailash Tarachandani has a B.Tech in electrical engineering from IIT Kanpur and an MBA from INSEAD. He has more than 30 years in strategy, global project execution, product management and business development, including setting up plants and acquiring technologies. Before joining Inox Wind as CEO in May 2013 he worked at Kenersys (Pune), Vestas Wind Systems, Alstom Power in Switzerland and Larsen & Toubro. In June 2025 he became group CEO of the renewables business.

people.name: Shivam Tandon
people.since: CFO (earlier CFO of Inox Wind Energy)
people.bio: Shivam Tandon is a chartered accountant with more than 17 years in manufacturing finance: reporting, budgeting, cost control, banking, tax and audit. Before the INOXGFL group he worked at the BC Jindal Group, Samvardhana Motherson and Tata Steel. His previous role was CFO of Inox Wind Energy.

companies.changes: Sanjeev Agarwal replaced Kailash Tarachandani as CEO on 1 June 2025. Non-executive director Urvashi Saxena left on 30 June 2025. Manoj Dixit was re-appointed as whole-time director from December 2025.

companies.styleNote: The Nahata family controls it. Anant Nahata, son of HFCL founder Mahendra Nahata, is MD & CEO. The promoter stake of about 66% is held through NextWave Communications (54.7%), Satellite Finance and HFCL; Anant holds no shares personally. The non-executive chairman, Himanshu Baid, is MD of Poly Medicure. Hired CEOs run the EV-charger and critical-power businesses.

people.name: Anant Nahata
people.since: Board since June 2008; employed since July 2017
people.relation: Promoter; son of Mahendra Nahata, founder and MD of HFCL (a promoter shareholder)
people.stake: nil personally (FY26 annual report); promoter group about 66%, mainly through NextWave Communications
people.bio: Anant Nahata has a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Pennsylvania. He worked in investment banking at Credit Suisse in New York and later founded the online fashion retailer Koovs. In the late 2000s he promoted Infotel Broadband, which won all-India spectrum and was sold to Reliance. He has been on Exicom's board since 2008 and full-time since 2017. Under him the company expanded from telecom power systems into EV chargers, listed in March 2024 and bought the Australian fast-charger maker Tritium. He is 42 and was paid ₹2.1cr in FY26.

people.name: Vivekanand Kumar
people.since: With Exicom since 2021; re-appointed at the 2025 AGM
people.bio: Vivekanand Kumar is an engineer with a postgraduate business degree and more than 20 years in manufacturing, operations and supply chain. Before Exicom he held leadership roles at Autoliv India, Gates India, GKN Driveline India, Caparo Engineering India and Roop Automotives. The company credits him with strengthening its manufacturing and operations.

people.name: Shiraz Khanna
people.bio: Shiraz Khanna is a chartered accountant with more than 30 years of experience. He has been CFO since 2021 and also oversees accounts, treasury, tax, compliance and legal. Before Exicom he held senior finance roles at PwC India, Aircel, Bharti Airtel and American Express.

people.name: Anshuman Divyanshu
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Anshuman Divyanshu has nearly 20 years in energy, mobility and infrastructure. He held leadership roles at BPCL, Reliance Industries and Reliance BP Mobility, where he helped build Jio-bp's EV charging network into one of India's largest charge-point operators. He runs Exicom's EV-charger division.

people.name: Sanjeev Kumar Narula
people.bio: Sanjeev Narula has a B.Tech and runs the critical power business, which grew out of Exicom's original telecom power business. Before Exicom he held leadership roles at Mahindra & Mahindra, Honda Siel Power Products and TAFE, and grew businesses in India, the SAARC region, Africa and the Middle East. He joined in September 2022.

people.name: Puran Mal Singh
people.bio: Puran Mal Singh has led Exicom's research and development since joining in 2011, with a focus on power electronics and product development. He previously worked at Delta Power Solutions.

companies.changes: No KMP or senior management changes in FY26. Vice President (Manufacturing) Aman Sharma resigned with effect from 30 June 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Raman Bhatia is Managing Director and his wife Sarika Bhatia is a whole-time director. Other Bhatia relatives are in the promoter group, including former CFO Vikas Bhatia, who now heads field execution. Promoters own about 59%. The board elects a chairman at each meeting rather than having a standing one.

people.name: Raman Bhatia
people.relation: Founder and promoter; husband of Sarika Bhatia
people.stake: 29.91% (FY26 annual report); his HUF holds another 13.40%; promoter family together about 59%
people.bio: Raman Bhatia founded Servotech and has run it as MD since it began. He started in business in 1991, first with a TV repair business, before moving into power products. He took the company from traditional power backup products into solar, EV chargers, power electronics and batteries, and listed it on NSE. The company has not published his education. The 2026 AGM notice proposed pay of up to ₹1.8cr a year for him.

people.name: Sarika Bhatia
people.since: Whole-time director; re-appointment proposed at the 2026 AGM
people.relation: Wife of the founder-MD, Raman Bhatia
people.bio: Sarika Bhatia runs sales and marketing and has more than 17 years in leadership roles at the company. The company says she handles client relationships and winning large tenders and projects. The company has not published her education.

people.name: Mrityunjay Kumar Jha
people.since: 24 July 2026 (3-year term, subject to shareholder approval)
people.bio: Mrityunjay Kumar Jha has worked at Servotech for 17 years in human resources, administration, employee relations and organisational development. He joined the board as a whole-time director on 24 July 2026, the day after Executive Director (HR) Digvijay Kapoor left. His proposed pay is up to ₹24 lakh a year.

people.name: Vipin Kaushik
people.bio: Vipin Kaushik is a chartered accountant with a postgraduate degree from Gujarat University, and holds diplomas in international financial reporting (ACCA) and management and business finance (ICAI). He has more than 20 years in corporate finance, strategy, accounts, tax and compliance. He has worked in senior roles, including as CFO, at ICICI Bank, Delhivery, V2 Retail and Franchise India Group. He was already at Servotech and was promoted to CFO on 1 April 2026, replacing Vikas Bhatia.

people.name: Arun Handa
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Arun Handa is Servotech's Chief Technical Officer and is named as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his background.

companies.changes: CFO Vikas Bhatia (promoter group) stepped down on 31 March 2026 and is now Head of Field Execution; Vipin Kaushik became CFO on 1 April 2026. Executive Director (HR) Digvijay Kapoor, appointed in June 2025, left on 23 July 2026, and Mrityunjay Kumar Jha joined the board as a whole-time director on 24 July 2026. NSE fined the company twice in FY26 (August and November 2025) for late compliance with Regulation 17(1A), the rule on non-executive directors over 75.

companies.styleNote: The Mehta family controls it. Bhavna Mehta owns 56.3% and the promoter group 58.6%. In February 2026 she stepped down as MD but stayed on the board as a non-executive director. Her husband Dr. Harshad Mehta is non-executive Chairman and their daughter Sonali Mehta is a non-executive director. A hired MD & CEO, N. Ramesh Kumar, now runs the company. The ₹42cr silicon-carbide know-how was bought from Sicamore Semiconductor (US), which the accounts list as an entity in which a director or relative is interested.

people.name: N. Ramesh Kumar (Ramesh Kumar Narasinghbhan)
people.bio: Ramesh Kumar has a B.E. in electrical engineering from MNNIT Allahabad and more than 42 years in electrical equipment. He started in 1984 as a graduate engineer trainee at GEC of India and joined Crompton Greaves in 1990, where he spent nearly three decades. There he ran motors, pumps, lighting, fans, appliances, transformers and switchgear, and rose to President of CG's India businesses and then President of the industrial business at CG Power. Most recently he was CEO of Diffusion Engineers. He has attended leadership programmes at IIM Ahmedabad, ISB-Kellogg and Management Centre Europe, and was vice-president of IFMA and an elected member of ELCOMA. He is 63. His fixed pay is ₹1.9cr a year plus up to ₹40 lakh variable pay and a ₹30 lakh joining bonus.

people.name: Ramesh Gopal Trasi
people.since: CEO for more than 22 years until February 2026; CTO since then
people.bio: R. G. Trasi ran RIR as CEO for more than 22 years and also acted as CFO. When the new MD & CEO joined in February 2026 he moved to Chief Technology Officer, to lead its technology and innovation plan. He resigned as CFO on 2 June 2026, citing his other responsibilities.

companies.changes: Bhavna Mehta stepped down as MD and R. G. Trasi as CEO in February 2026; N. Ramesh Kumar became MD & CEO on 11 February 2026. Trasi also resigned as CFO on 2 June 2026, and we found no announcement of a replacement. Independent director Kaushal Mehta resigned in July 2025.

companies.styleNote: Part of the KP Group. Its founder, Dr. Faruk G. Patel, is non-executive Chairman and personally owns 57.9%. His son Hassan Patel is a whole-time director, and the long-serving engineer Muinulhaque Kadva runs the factories. The company pays the promoter a 2% brand royalty (₹19.2cr in FY26), and ₹32.9cr of 'advance for property' was outstanding to Faruk Patel in March 2026. A large part of its revenue comes from other KP Group companies.

people.name: Muinulhaque Kadva
people.since: With the company for over a decade; whole-time director
people.bio: Muinulhaque Iqbalhusen Kadva has a mechanical engineering degree from Gujarat Technological University and has been with the company for more than ten years. He heads manufacturing, running the factories and project execution. His expertise covers galvanising, fabrication, telecom towers and support structures for renewable projects. He is involved in day-to-day management and strategic decisions, and is one of the company's designated officials for disclosure.

people.name: Hassan Faruk Patel
people.relation: Promoter; son of the founder and Chairman, Dr. Faruk G. Patel
people.stake: 0.01% (6,117 shares, FY26 annual report); his father holds 57.87%
people.bio: Hassan Patel has a BBA from AURO University, Surat. He leads human resources for the KP Group and is also involved in overall management, finance, strategic planning and decisions at KP Green. He became a whole-time director in September 2025 and was paid ₹32.6 lakh in FY26. He is also a director of several group companies, including green hydrogen and ammonia, energy storage and O&M units. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the September 2026 AGM.

people.name: Pravinkumar Singh
people.bio: Pravinkumar Singh has a commerce degree from South Gujarat University. He has experience in financial management, planning, risk assessment, corporate finance and compliance, according to the company's website. The company has not published his earlier employers.

companies.changes: Hassan Patel became a whole-time director on 29 September 2025. On 3 July 2026 non-executive director Amit Khandelwal resigned, and Prof. Sunil Kumar Maheshwari (formerly of IIM Ahmedabad) joined as non-executive Vice-Chairman, subject to approval at the September 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: A Patel family business from Anand, Gujarat. Brothers Niral Patel (Chairman & MD) and Amish Patel run it with their first cousin Tanmay Patel as whole-time directors. The long-time director Krupeshbhai Patel died in August 2025. A hired CEO, Akshaykumar Mathur, runs day-to-day operations. Promoters and the family trust own about 87%.

people.name: Niral K. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Amish Patel and first cousin of Tanmay Patel
people.stake: 8.29% (63,75,000 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 87%
people.bio: Niral Patel, 44, has a computer engineering degree from the University of Pune, a diploma in electrical engineering from the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education and an MBA from Hult International Business School. He has more than 22 years in transformer making. At Atlanta he handles customer and supplier relationships, strategy and budgets. He is also linked to several family companies, including Amod Stampings, Auro Stampings, Venus Laminations and the Neptune realty firms. Amod Stampings is a large parts supplier to Atlanta, so related-party purchases are worth watching.

people.name: Tanmay S. Patel
people.since: With the company since 2002; director since July 2002
people.relation: Promoter; first cousin of Niral and Amish Patel
people.bio: Tanmay Patel, 48, has a diploma in electrical engineering from the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education. He has more than 22 years in the transformer, electrical and manufacturing industries, all of it at Atlanta, which he joined in 2002. He is responsible for buying raw materials and components and for supply-chain logistics.

people.name: Amish K. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Niral Patel and first cousin of Tanmay Patel
people.bio: Amish Patel, 42, has a bachelor's degree in business administration from Sardar Patel University. He has about 17 years of experience in real estate, investment and acquisitions, and is also associated with the family's Neptune Realty. He joined Atlanta's board in 2022. His job is to find suitable land for new plants and to work with project managers and contractors on building them.

people.name: Akshaykumar B. Mathur
people.bio: Akshaykumar Mathur has a B.Tech in electronics and communication from Kakatiya University and an MBA from the University of Jodhpur. He has about 44 years of work experience, 32 of them in the transformer industry, and previously worked at Voltamp Transformers. He joined Atlanta in August 2015 and signs the CEO certificate on the accounts. He is the senior hired manager in a family-led company.

people.name: Mehul S. Mehta
people.bio: Mehul Mehta has a commerce degree and a postgraduate diploma in business administration from Sardar Patel University, plus a diploma in business management, an advanced diploma in management and an MBA from ICFAI University, Dehradun. He previously worked at ABG Cement. He joined Atlanta in March 2005 and has about 19 years of experience in finance.

people.name: Anand Sharma
people.bio: Anand Sharma has an engineering diploma from Dayalbagh Educational Institute and a postgraduate diploma in business administration (operations) from the Symbiosis Centre for Distance Learning. Before joining Atlanta in March 2022 he worked at Crompton Greaves, EMCO, Caparo Fasteners, NLMK India Service Center, Hotline Glass and BTA Cellcom. He is listed as senior management.

people.name: Minesh Bhatt
people.bio: Minesh Bhatt has a diploma in electrical engineering from Government Polytechnic, Chhotaudaipur. He previously worked at Voltamp Transformers and joined Atlanta in April 2004. He has 23 years of engineering experience and heads transformer design, which matters as the company moves up to 400 kV and 765 kV units.

companies.changes: Whole-time director Krupeshbhai Patel died on 7 August 2025; his shares are being transferred. No executive changes filed since the annual report (27 August 2026).

companies.styleNote: Two managing directors share the top job. The promoter Kunjal Patel, who owns 30%, is Vice Chairman & MD. The Chairman & MD, Kanubhai Patel, is a chartered accountant who has worked for the group since 1982 and is not related to the promoter. Kunjal Patel's relative Taral Patel is a non-executive director. Promoter holding fell from 38% to 30% after a 7.8% block sale in September 2025.

people.name: Kanubhai S. Patel
people.since: Joined 1992 as CEO; executive director 1995; joint MD 2002; Chairman & MD since 2013
people.relation: Not related to the promoter or any director
people.bio: Kanubhai Patel, 69, is a commerce graduate, a fellow chartered accountant and a fellow company secretary, and attended an advanced management programme at Kellogg in the US. He worked for the group as a professional from 1982 and moved to Voltamp in 1992 as CEO. He became executive director in 1995, joint managing director in 2002 and chairman & managing director in 2013. The company credits him with shifting it from utility tenders to private industrial customers, keeping it debt-free since 2005-06 and taking it public in 2006. He is also an independent director of Epigral and Paramount.

people.name: Kunjal L. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; related to non-executive director Taral K. Patel
people.stake: 30.00% (30,35,176 shares, FY26 annual report); down from 37.80% a year earlier
people.bio: Kunjal Patel has an electrical engineering degree from M. S. University of Vadodara and attended INSEAD. He joined Voltamp in 1994 and has worked across production, marketing, after-sales service and general management. He now oversees purchasing and planning, quality control, manufacturing, transformer design and the service business. He is the company's only promoter shareholder of size, and sold 7.8% of the company in a block deal in September 2025.

people.name: Vijay Gupta
people.since: COO from November 2025; with the company about 18 years
people.bio: Vijay Gupta has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering and an MBA. He has about 33 years in the transformer industry, including 15 years in the transformer business of Crompton Greaves. He joined Voltamp about 18 years ago and ran its power-transformer business unit before being promoted to COO in November 2025.

people.name: Shailesh Prajapati
people.bio: Shailesh Prajapati is a chartered accountant. He joined Voltamp in 2018 and was General Manager – Accounts & Finance before becoming CFO in May 2022, when the long-serving CFO Vallabh Madhani retired. At his appointment he had about 14 years of experience in accounts, banking and finance, direct and indirect tax and statutory compliance.

companies.changes: Vijay Gupta promoted to COO on 8 November 2025. No executive changes filed since the annual report (7 July 2026).

companies.styleNote: Founded in 1981 by Jitendra Mamtora, who is Chairman and a whole-time director. His son Satyen Mamtora is MD & CEO, and his wife Karuna Mamtora is an executive director. A hired CEO lasted only six months (July 2025 to January 2026), after which Satyen took the CEO title too. Promoters own about 64%; lenders hold a pledge over about 14% of the company's shares owned by a director.

people.name: Jitendra U. Mamtora
people.since: Founder (1981); Chairman since incorporation in 1994; re-appointed from 1 January 2026
people.relation: Founder; husband of Karuna Mamtora and father of Satyen Mamtora
people.stake: 31.30% (9,39,63,368 shares, FY26 annual report); family together about 50%, promoter group about 64%
people.bio: Jitendra Mamtora has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College. He started in 1969 as an engineer at Electrical Equipment Manufacturing Company and set up Transformers and Rectifiers in Gujarat in 1981, first making distribution transformers and then furnace transformers. He has more than 40 years in the industry and has built the company into a maker of units up to 1,200 kV. He sits on the executive council of IEEMA, the electrical equipment makers' association, has chaired its transformer division since 2007, and is active in CII and FICCI.

people.name: Satyen J. Mamtora
people.since: Director since July 1994; CEO title added 8 January 2026
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Jitendra Mamtora, and of Karuna Mamtora
people.bio: Satyen Mamtora, born in 1974, has a diploma in electrical engineering from Uxbridge College in London. He has been with the company since its early years and was trained in rotation across all key functions. He runs production and marketing, built the company's position with state and central power utilities, and set up its global marketing plan. Under him sales crossed ₹2,000cr in FY25. He took over the CEO role in January 2026 after the hired CEO, Mukul Srivastava, resigned.

people.name: Karuna J. Mamtora
people.since: Executive director since April 2005; re-appointed from 1 April 2026
people.relation: Wife of the Chairman, Jitendra Mamtora; mother of Satyen Mamtora
people.bio: Karuna Mamtora has a bachelor's degree in arts from Gujarat University. She has been involved with the company since its early days and became an executive director in April 2005. She handles general administration and human resources and leads the company's CSR programmes as chairperson of the CSR committee.

people.name: Mehul Shah
people.bio: Mehul Shah is a chartered accountant with more than 26 years of experience in accounting, financial operations, fund management, budgeting, tax and corporate governance. Before joining TARIL he worked at Nirma, Adani Enterprises, Reliance Logistics, Arvind SmartSpaces, Gujarat Ambuja Exports and Asian Granito India. He replaced Chanchal Rajora as CFO in March 2026, as the company spends heavily on backward integration.

people.name: Chanchal S. S. Rajora
people.since: Director Finance from November 2025; CFO until 5 March 2026
people.bio: Dr. Chanchal Rajora is a chartered accountant with about 25 years of experience in corporate finance, fund raising, financial planning, mergers and acquisitions, and credit and risk management. He was the company's CFO and adviser to the board, and was made Director – Finance in November 2025. He stepped down as CFO in March 2026 in what the company called a strategic restructuring, and stays on as senior management.

companies.changes: Hired CEO Mukul Srivastava (joined July 2025) resigned on 7 January 2026 for personal reasons; Satyen Mamtora became MD & CEO. CFO Chanchal Rajora handed over to Mehul Shah on 5 March 2026 and stays as Director – Finance. The company website now lists Bhavin Vahia as HR head in place of Ajay Bamzai named in the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Run by its two co-founders, who are not related to each other: Vee Rajmohan (Chairman & MD) and K. V. Pradeep Kumar (whole-time director). Both were re-appointed for three years from 31 August 2026. Both are also partners in Danya Electric Company, a transformer firm in which Supreme holds a 90% profit share, trades with it and guarantees its loans. The two founders own 52% between them; the promoter group about 57%.

people.name: Vee Rajmohan
people.since: Founder (partnership firm 2001); director since June 2005; re-appointed to August 2029
people.relation: Co-founder; not related to any director
people.stake: 31.51% (78,75,430 shares, FY26 annual report); founders together 52%
people.bio: Vee Rajmohan, 55, started in 1990 as works manager at Venuss Herbo Aromatics in Rajapalayam, Tamil Nadu, where he set up and commissioned the plant; he stayed until 2001. That year he and Pradeep Kumar founded the partnership Supreme Power Equipments to make distribution transformers for the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board, and in 2005 turned it into a private company. The FY26 annual report lists a bachelor's degree in engineering, while the 2023 IPO prospectus said he had enrolled for one; he also holds an honorary doctorate in business. He leads strategy, business development and expansion, including the new 220 kV Kannur plant. He holds a 7.5% profit share in Danya Electric Company, a related party.

people.name: K. V. Pradeep Kumar (Vishwambran Nair Pradeep Kumar)
people.since: Co-founder (2001); whole-time director since June 2023; re-appointed to August 2029
people.relation: Co-founder; not related to any director
people.bio: Pradeep Kumar, 55, has a bachelor's degree in engineering. He joined Indotech Transformers (now Prolec GE) in Chennai as a quality-assurance trainee engineer in 1991 and by 1997 headed quality assurance for transformers up to 100 MVA and 230 kV. He co-founded Supreme with Vee Rajmohan and is its technical lead, overseeing manufacturing, quality, procurement and design. He developed the company's wind-turbine and inverter-duty transformer designs, sold to many wind and solar plants. He holds a 2.5% profit share in Danya Electric Company.

people.name: Thulasiraman Boologa Nathan
people.bio: Thulasiraman Boologa Nathan has a B.Com and has passed the intermediate level of the cost accountancy (ICWA) course.
