He has more than 30 years of experience in finance, accounts, costing and budgeting. Before joining Supreme he was senior manager, finance and accounts, at Vetrivel Forgings. He became CFO in September 2023, just before the company's December 2023 SME IPO.

companies.changes: Non-executive director Devaraja Iyer Krishna Iyer resigned on 13 August 2026; Ramesh C. Behera joined as an independent director the same day. MD and whole-time director re-appointed from 31 August 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Pandyan family company from Sangli. The founder Thalavaidurai Pandyan is Chairman & MD, his son Bharanidharan Pandyan is Joint MD, and his wife Chitra Pandyan is a whole-time director. A hired CEO, Sanjog Mhatre, has run operations since February 2026. The three are proposed for re-appointment for five years from March 2027. Promoters own about 74%, most of it held by Bharanidharan.

people.name: Thalavaidurai Pandyan
people.relation: Founder; father of Joint MD Bharanidharan Pandyan and husband of whole-time director Chitra Pandyan
people.stake: 12.73% (98,60,480 shares, FY26 annual report); family together about 50%, promoter group about 74%
people.bio: Thalavaidurai Pandyan, 71, has a diploma in electrical engineering (industrial electronics) from Tamil Nadu's State Board of Technical Education. He has more than four decades of experience in high-voltage electrical equipment, power systems and power-quality products. He has been a promoter and director since the company was set up in 2001 and handles its day-to-day affairs. He is proposed for re-appointment as Chairman & MD for five years from March 2027, which needs a special resolution because he is over 70. His FY26 pay was ₹2.07cr.

people.name: Bharanidharan Pandyan
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD, Thalavaidurai Pandyan, and of Chitra Pandyan
people.bio: Bharanidharan Pandyan, 42, has an electrical and electronics engineering degree from B.M.S. College of Engineering and an MBA from S.P. Jain Institute of Management & Research, and is pursuing a PhD in strategy at S.P. Jain School of Global Management. He has more than two decades of experience in high-voltage equipment, reactors and reactive-power products, and has done business in over 95 countries. His listed expertise includes corporate strategy and mergers and acquisitions; the group has bought Endoks in Turkey, Mehru Electrical and Sukrut Electric, and plans to buy the insulator maker Win-Win. He is the largest shareholder, and his FY26 pay was ₹2.12cr.

people.name: Chitra Pandyan
people.relation: Wife of the Chairman & MD; mother of Joint MD Bharanidharan Pandyan
people.bio: Chitra Pandyan, 70, has been with the company since it was set up and oversees its administrative functions. Her listed qualification is matriculation. Her FY26 pay was ₹49.5 lakh, and she is proposed for re-appointment for five years from March 2027.

people.name: Mahesh V. Saralaya
people.since: Joined October 2006; whole-time director since February 2024
people.bio: Mahesh Saralaya, 67, has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology and is a chartered engineer registered with the Institution of Engineers (India). He joined Quality Power as a marketing manager in October 2006 and joined the board as a whole-time director in February 2024, before the IPO. He is the only non-family executive on the board.

people.name: Sanjog S. Mhatre
people.bio: Sanjog Mhatre was the company's Chief Business Officer before being made CEO in February 2026. He has more than 30 years of experience in profit-and-loss management, business turnaround and global operations, with senior roles at L&T, CTR Ltd., Arcteq and BSC GmbH. He took over the India operations when the president of India operations, Vivek Moroney, resigned at the end of December 2025.

people.name: Rajesh Jayaraman
people.bio: Rajesh Jayaraman became CFO in 2024, before the February 2025 IPO. The company describes him as experienced in finance, strategic planning, risk management and governance. Business-data profiles list earlier roles as operations director at Prager Metis Global Services, general manager for finance and investor relations at Sicagen India, general manager finance at Kare Labs, and CFO of ICE Steel 1.

companies.changes: Vivek Moroney, President & Head of India Operations, resigned on 31 December 2025. Sanjog Mhatre promoted from Chief Business Officer to CEO on 4 February 2026. No executive changes filed since the annual report (5 September 2026).

companies.styleNote: The promoter Narendra Goliya stepped back from MD to Executive Chairman in August 2024 and a hired manager, Dineshkumar Musalekar, runs the group; he was made Managing Director in May 2026. No other family member is on the board. The Goliya family and trusts own about 70%; in August 2026 a press report said they were talking to buyers, which the company did not deny.

people.name: Narendra J. Goliya
people.since: Promoter; MD until August 2024, Executive Chairman since
people.relation: Promoter; the promoter group also includes Asha, Rishabh and Anushree Goliya and two family trusts
people.stake: 42.18% (1,62,57,098 shares, held jointly with Asha Goliya, FY26 annual report); promoter group 69.55%
people.bio: Narendra Goliya has an electrical engineering degree from IIT Bombay and a master's degree in microelectronics from Stanford University. He has more than 40 years in manufacturing and the electrical industry. He built Rishabh in Nashik, bought Lumel and Lumel Alucast in Poland in July 2011, bought Sifam Tinsley in the UK and set up its US sales arm. He also runs Shanti Instruments, a company his father started in Mumbai, and chairs the Nashik Engineering Cluster. He is founder chief patron of the Jain International Trade Organisation (JITO).

people.name: Dineshkumar Musalekar
people.since: Whole-time director & Group CEO from August 2024; MD from 18 May 2026 (5 years)
people.stake: 0.52% (2,00,749 shares, FY26 annual report); also granted ESOPs
people.bio: Dineshkumar Musalekar, born in 1971, has an electronics and communications engineering degree from Karnataka University, a master's degree from the Somaiya Institute (an MBA in human resource management) and an executive programme from Henley in the UK. He spent about a decade at Otis Elevator in India, rising from graduate trainee to manager of its modernisation department, and another decade at Avire (Halma group) as India resident director and general manager for India, the Middle East and Africa. Since 2013 he has been president and CEO of the group's Polish units Lumel and Lumel Alucast, and was honoured by the mayor of Zielona Góra for turning Lumel around. He is paid ₹1.4cr in India plus salaries from both Polish units.

people.name: Vishal Kulkarni
people.bio: Vishal Kulkarni has an M.Com from Pune University and is an associate member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. Before joining Rishabh in July 2014 he worked at Techno Force (India) and ThyssenKrupp India. He co-signs the CEO/CFO certificate on the accounts.

people.name: Mahesh Naval
people.bio: Mahesh Naval has a degree in electronics and telecommunication engineering and more than 25 years of operations experience. He previously worked at Radiant Appliances, LG, Celetronix, Globatronix and MIRC. He is listed in the annual report's management team.

people.name: Nitinkumar Deshpande
people.role: AVP – Global Head, Marketing and Strategic Business Development
people.bio: Nitinkumar Deshpande has an electrical engineering degree from Mumbai University and an MBA from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, Pune. He has more than 24 years in the electrical and electronics industry, including roles at ABB, Siemens and Schneider Electric. He leads global marketing and strategic business development.

companies.changes: Dineshkumar Musalekar re-designated from whole-time director to Managing Director on 18 May 2026 (shareholder approval at the AGM). The company disclosed Anand Laddha's resignation at a material subsidiary in July 2025. No other executive changes filed since the annual report (9 July 2026).

companies.styleNote: A subsidiary of France's Schneider Electric, which holds about 75% through Indian and Singapore holding companies. There is no family promoter; the group appoints career managers, several of them from the L&T electrical business Schneider bought in 2020. The board is chaired by an independent director, Pravin Kumar Purang, and Schneider executives sit as non-executive directors.

people.name: Udai Singh
people.since: September 2023; re-appointed for 3 years from 15 September 2026
people.stake: 500 shares (FY26 annual report); also eligible for Schneider Electric SE stock plans
people.bio: Udai Singh has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from IIT Varanasi and has attended leadership programmes at the Ross School of Business and INSEAD. He joined L&T's electrical and automation business as a graduate engineer trainee in 1992 and spent more than 33 years there and in its successor under Schneider, in sales, marketing, projects and contract management and manufacturing. His last role before this job was business head of the equipment business. He became MD & CEO in September 2023. His fixed pay plus target bonus and long-term incentive is about ₹3.8cr a year under the new term.

people.name: Soumya Bagchi
people.since: Board from 30 June 2026; whole-time director from 14 August 2026 (3 years)
people.bio: Soumya Bagchi has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Jadavpur University, Kolkata, and has attended leadership programmes at the Ross School of Business and INSEAD. He joined L&T's electrical and automation business as a graduate engineer trainee in 1994 and moved to Schneider when it bought that business in 2020. Over more than 30 years he has handled profit-and-loss ownership, product development, business development, projects and manufacturing. He was business unit head for medium-voltage equipment and earlier headed project and contract management for low- and medium-voltage equipment in India, the Middle East and Africa. He joined the board as whole-time director Chinmoy Das was leaving.

people.name: Omkar Prasad
people.bio: Omkar Prasad is a fellow chartered accountant with a master's degree in economics, is an alumnus of IIM Bangalore and holds certifications in business responsibility and sustainability reporting. Before becoming CFO he was Schneider Electric's chief accounting officer for Greater India, covering India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. He has more than two decades in financial control, tax compliance, risk management and digital finance projects, and earlier worked as plant controller, internal auditor and corporate finance manager. He replaced Suparna Banerjee Bhattacharyya, who left to pursue a career outside the group.

companies.changes: CFO Suparna Banerjee Bhattacharyya left on 15 September 2025; Omkar Prasad took over the next day. Whole-time director Chinmoy Das resigned for personal reasons with effect from 30 June 2026; Soumya Bagchi joined the board on 30 June and became whole-time director on 14 August 2026. Udai Singh re-appointed MD & CEO from 15 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Keyur Shah took over the company as managing director in 2008 and is Chairman & MD; his wife Twinkle Shah is a non-executive director. Day-to-day functions are run by hired executive directors for finance, global business and operations, who are not board members. A German bushing expert, Hartmuth Fethke, sits as a non-executive director. The couple own about 55% (53.4% and 1.9% at March 2026).

people.name: Keyur G. Shah
people.relation: Promoter; husband of non-executive director Twinkle Shah
people.stake: 53.36% (1,52,34,595 shares, FY26 annual report); with his wife about 55%
people.bio: Keyur Shah has a diploma in civil engineering from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. He joined Yash Highvoltage in March 2008, when he took it over as managing director, and has about 25 years of industry experience. He built it into what the company calls India's leading maker of high-voltage and high-current transformer bushings, and chairs its technical advisory board. At the 2024 IPO he oversaw administration and finance. His other ventures include Yash Swisstech, Desar Estate and Upscale Developers. Shareholders are being asked to approve pay above the statutory limit for him from March 2026.

people.name: Darshan Thakkar
people.bio: Darshan Thakkar has more than 25 years in finance, mostly at banks including Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, ABN AMRO and The Royal Bank of Scotland, before moving into corporate finance at manufacturers. He heads finance and accounts and also oversees investor relations, risk management, legal and compliance, HR and IT. He is not a board director; 'executive director' is his job title.

people.name: Sumit Poddar
people.bio: Sumit Poddar has cleared the final examination of the Institute of Cost and Works Accountants of India. He has about 25 years of experience across pharma and life sciences, oil and rubber, metals and mining, procurement, project finance and investment banking. He joined Yash in September 2022 and became CFO in August 2024, before the IPO. He advises the MD on finance, planning and investment decisions.

people.name: Nirav P. Patel
people.bio: Nirav Patel is an electrical engineer and has completed a HarvardX online course in entrepreneurship in emerging economies. He has more than 18 years in operations, marketing and business leadership in the power and manufacturing sectors, rising at Yash through roles as assistant manager for sales and marketing, general manager for business operations and chief marketing officer. people.name: Maneesh Tiwari

people.name: Jasbir Singh

people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in industrial production and an MBA, with over 25 years in consumer durables and electronics manufacturing. people.name: Daljit Singh
people.since: On the board since January 2008; MD, current term August 2022 to August 2027
people.relation: Promoter; brother of the Executive Chairman Jasbir Singh
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering and a master's in information technology. people.name: Sachin Gupta
people.role: Whole-time Director; CEO, Consumer Durables Division
people.bio: An engineer with a PGDM in business administration, a Six Sigma Black Belt and Toyota Production System certification. people.name: Sudhir Goyal

people.name: Sanjay Kumar Arora
people.role: Whole-time Director, IL JIN Electronics (electronics subsidiary)
people.since: Named as senior leader on the company's leadership page

He set up the blueprint for Amber's electronics (EMS) business and led its move into new segments and circuit boards through the Ascent Circuits acquisition.

people.name: Udaiveer Singh
people.since: With Sidwal for more than three decades

people.name: Vishal Gupta

people.name: Vikas Gupta
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Anurag Gupta and Vishal Gupta
people.bio: Holds an MBA from the University of Pune and has 31 years in electronics manufacturing. He looks after new business development, customer relations and internal support services, with a focus on the washing machine and LED TV businesses.

people.name: Pramod Chimmanlal Gupta

people.name: Sajid Shaikh

people.name: Hardeep Singh
people.since: Founder; on the board since March 2016

people.bio: Has more than two decades of experience making TV kits, electronic components and LED lighting. people.name: Surmeet Kaur
people.relation: Promoter; wife of the Chairman & MD; mother of Ishween Kaur; mother-in-law of Sanjeet Singh

people.name: Sanjeet Singh

people.since: With the company since February 2019; CEO from May 2025; also CFO from August 2025

companies.styleNote: ICICI Bank has no promoter; it is widely held by institutions. It is run by career ICICI managers: all four board executives and the CFO have spent 28 to 40 years inside the group. The non-executive chairman is Pradeep Kumar Sinha, a former Cabinet Secretary. No director is related to another. Directors and officers together own only 0.04% of the shares.

people.name: Sandeep Bakhshi
people.since: Joined ICICI 1986; MD & CEO since 15 October 2018 (re-appointed to 3 October 2028)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh, with a management degree from XLRI Jamshedpur. He joined ICICI in 1986 and has worked across ICICI Limited, ICICI Lombard General Insurance, ICICI Bank and ICICI Prudential Life, which he ran as MD & CEO from August 2010. He came back to the bank in June 2018 as Chief Operating Officer (designate) and became MD & CEO on 15 October 2018, after the Chanda Kochhar episode. The RBI approved a further two-year term from 4 October 2026 to 3 October 2028, shorter than the usual three years. He is 66 and holds no other directorships, so succession is the thing to watch.

people.name: Sandeep Batra
people.since: Joined ICICI group 2000; Executive Director since 23 December 2020 (term to 22 December 2027)
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary. He joined ICICI Prudential Life as CFO in 2000, and later served as Group Compliance Officer of ICICI Bank, Executive Director of ICICI Prudential Life and President at ICICI Bank. He has run the bank's Corporate Centre since July 2018 and joined the board as Executive Director in December 2020. He chairs ICICI Prudential Life, ICICI Prudential AMC and ICICI Venture, sits on the ICICI Lombard board, and chaired ICICI Bank UK from 2018 to 2023.

people.name: Rakesh Jha
people.role: Executive Director (retail, small business and corporate banking)
people.since: Joined ICICI 1996; Executive Director since 2 September 2022 (term to 1 September 2027)
people.bio: An engineering graduate from IIT Delhi with a post-graduate management degree from IIM Lucknow. He joined ICICI in 1996 and worked in several areas before becoming the Group CFO. He joined the board as Executive Director in September 2022 and now runs the retail, small-enterprise and corporate banking businesses. He chairs ICICI Lombard General Insurance, ICICI Home Finance and ICICI Securities. At 54 he is the youngest of the executive directors.

people.name: Ajay Kumar Gupta
people.since: Joined ICICI November 1991; Executive Director since 15 March 2024 (re-appointed to 26 November 2028)
people.bio: A chartered accountant who joined the ICICI group in November 1991. He has worked in corporate banking, project finance, SME lending, debt-service management, credit policy and operations. He is responsible for credit policy and underwriting for retail and business banking, and for operations, technology and data analytics. He joined the board in March 2024, and the RBI approved a further two-year term from 27 November 2026 in July 2026. He chairs ICICI Securities Primary Dealership and I-Process Services.

people.name: Anindya Banerjee
people.since: Joined ICICI group 1998; Group CFO since 1 May 2022
people.bio: A chartered accountant who joined the ICICI group in 1998. He began in corporate banking and then moved to planning and strategy in the corporate office. He became Group CFO on 1 May 2022, succeeding Rakesh Jha, and is responsible for financial reporting, planning and strategy, and asset-liability management. He joined the board of ICICI Venture Funds Management in July 2026. He presents the bank's quarterly results to analysts.

companies.changes: No executive exits since the annual report. The RBI approved Sandeep Bakhshi's re-appointment for two years from 4 October 2026 (May 2026) and Ajay Kumar Gupta's for two years from 27 November 2026 (July 2026); shareholders voted at the 21 August 2026 AGM. Independent directors Neelam Dhawan and Radhakrishnan Nair retired in January and May 2026; Ashwani Bhatia joined in June 2026.

companies.styleNote: HDFC Bank has had no promoter since its 2023 merger with parent HDFC Limited; it is widely held by institutions. It is run by career bankers, most of whom joined in the 1990s. The top job is changing: CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan leaves on 26 October 2026, and the RBI has approved Anup Bagchi, an ICICI Group banker since 1992, to succeed him from 27 October for three years. The part-time chairman is former Finance Secretary Rajiv Kumar (since July 2026); former HDFC Ltd heads Keki Mistry and Renu Karnad sit as non-executive directors. No director or senior manager owns 1% or more, and none are related.

people.name: Sashidhar Jagdishan
people.role: Managing Director & CEO (term ends 26 October 2026; Anup Bagchi succeeds him)
people.bio: A physics graduate and chartered accountant with a master's in the economics of money, banking and finance from the University of Sheffield. He joined HDFC Bank in 1996 as a manager in finance, became Business Head – Finance in 1999 and CFO in 2008. In 2019 he was named the bank's 'Strategic Change Agent' and also ran HR, legal, communications and administration. He succeeded Aditya Puri as MD & CEO in October 2020 and led the bank through the 2023 merger with HDFC Limited. He told the board he would not seek a third term, which ends on 26 October 2026. A Supreme Court appeal in the Lilavati Trust case against him is pending.

people.name: Anup Bagchi
people.role: Managing Director & CEO from 27 October 2026 (additional director from 2 October 2026)
people.since: Appointed 1 October 2026 (RBI approval the same day) for three years from 27 October 2026
people.bio: Holds an engineering degree from IIT Kanpur and a management degree from IIM Bangalore. He joined the ICICI Group in 1992 and worked across treasury, retail, wholesale and investment banking. He was MD & CEO of ICICI Securities, then Executive Director of ICICI Bank from 2017 to 2023, overseeing retail, business and rural banking and later wholesale banking; the bank's retail mortgage book passed ₹2 lakh crore in that time. Since June 2023 he has been MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, where annualised premium crossed ₹10,000cr for the first time in FY25. He is not related to any director or key manager of HDFC Bank.

people.name: Kaizad Bharucha
people.role: Deputy Managing Director (leaving 31 December 2026, subject to RBI approval)
people.since: Joined October 1995; board since 2014; Deputy MD since 19 April 2023 (re-appointed to 18 April 2029)
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Sydenham College, Mumbai, and a banker for over 40 years. He joined HDFC Bank in October 1995 and built much of its credit and risk framework, joining the board in 2014. As Deputy MD he oversees the whole loan franchise: home, car, two-wheeler and personal loans, rural and small-business lending, and corporate and investment banking. He co-chaired the committee that integrated HDFC Limited into the bank and is a nominee director on HDFC Life. Press reports name him as one of the two candidates the board has sent to the RBI for the CEO post.

people.name: V. Srinivasa Rangan
people.role: Executive Director (HR, legal, secretarial, investment banking, information security, vigilance)
people.since: Executive Director since 23 November 2023 (board re-appointed him to 22 November 2027, pending RBI)
people.bio: A commerce graduate from the University of Delhi and a chartered accountant. He was Executive Director and CFO of HDFC Limited, the mortgage lender, until it merged into the bank in July 2023, and has long experience in housing finance and real estate. He has done housing-finance consulting work in Ghana and the Maldives and sat on RBI and National Housing Bank committees on securitisation and covered bonds. The ICAI named him Best CFO in the Financial Sector for 2010. At the bank he runs HR, corporate legal, secretarial and group oversight, investment banking, information security and fraud and vigilance.

people.name: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
people.role: Chief Financial Officer (retiring; hands over on 1 December 2026)
people.bio: A commerce graduate and fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and the Institute of Cost Accountants of India, with an MBA and US CMA and UK AIA qualifications. He has over 30 years in financial services and joined HDFC Bank from Citigroup in 2018. As CFO he presents the quarterly results and fielded questions on the post-merger margin and funding mix. He retires in November 2026, and Puneet Sharma takes over as CFO from 1 December 2026.

people.name: Puneet Sharma
people.role: Chief Financial Officer – Designate (CFO from 1 December 2026)
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a postgraduate diploma in management from the Indian School of Business, Hyderabad, and over 26 years in banking, financial services and strategy. He was most recently Group Executive and CFO of Axis Bank, and before that CFO of Tata Capital. HDFC Bank's board appointed him on 29 June 2026 as CFO-designate from 1 September 2026, to become CFO on 1 December 2026.

people.name: Jimmy Tata
people.since: Joined 1994; Chief Risk Officer from June 2013, now Chief Credit Officer
people.bio: Holds a master's in financial management from Jamnalal Bajaj Institute and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (India). He began in 1987 at Strategic Consultants and from 1989 worked at Apple Industries, rising to head its wholesale leasing and hire-purchase division. He joined HDFC Bank in 1994 as a corporate-banking relationship manager, later headed corporate banking, became Chief Risk Officer in June 2013 and is now Chief Credit Officer. He sits on the boards of HDB Financial Services and International Asset Reconstruction Co. On 12 September 2026 the board approved his appointment as a whole-time (executive) director for three years, subject to RBI approval.

people.name: Ashish Parthasarthy
people.role: Head – Branch Banking, Payments, Treasury, Liability Products, Marketing, Virtual Channels and Infrastructure
people.bio: An engineering graduate from the National Institute of Technology, Karnataka, with a postgraduate diploma in management from IIM Bangalore. He has over 37 years in banking, with particular expertise in interest-rate and currency markets. He now heads the branch network, deposits, payments, treasury, marketing and digital channels, which makes him central to the bank's push to rebuild its share of cheap current and savings deposits.

companies.changes: Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha, with the bank for over three decades and credited by the board as a principal architect of its credit framework, asked to leave from 31 Dec 2026; the board accepted on 17 Oct 2026 and sent it to the RBI. CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan will not seek a third term (ends 26 October 2026); the board sent two names to the RBI on 12 September 2026, and on 1 October the RBI approved Anup Bagchi (MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life) as MD & CEO for three years from 27 October 2026. Executive Director Bhavesh Zaveri left on 18 April 2026 at the end of his term. CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan retires in November 2026; Puneet Sharma (ex-Axis Bank CFO) joined as CFO-designate on 1 September. Jigar Shah (ex-KKR India) becomes General Counsel on 1 October 2026. Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March 2026; Rajiv Kumar became part-time chairman on 15 July 2026. On 12 September the board also approved Jimmy Tata as an executive director and a fourth whole-time director post, both pending RBI approval.

companies.styleNote: SBI is controlled by the Government of India, which owns 55.03% (March 2026). It has no family promoter: the government appoints the Chairman and four Managing Directors, all career SBI officers who joined as probationary officers around 1988–1991. Unlike private banks, the Chairman here is the top executive. The directors own only token amounts of shares, and none are related.

people.name: Challa Sreenivasulu Setty
people.since: Joined SBI 1988; MD from January 2020; Chairman since 28 August 2024
people.bio: A Bachelor of Science in Agriculture and a Certified Associate of the Indian Institute of Bankers. He joined SBI as a probationary officer in 1988 and has worked in stressed-asset management, corporate and mid-corporate banking, global markets, technology and syndication in India and abroad. He joined the board as Managing Director in January 2020, ran retail and digital banking until 2022 and then international banking, global markets and technology. He became Chairman on 28 August 2024 and has led several government task forces and committees.

people.name: Ashwini Kumar Tewari
people.since: Joined SBI 1991; MD since January 2021; current portfolio since 21 November 2023
people.bio: An electrical engineer who is a CAIIB and Certified Financial Planner, with a certificate course in management from XLRI. He joined SBI in 1991 as a probationary officer, headed its East Asia region from Hong Kong and ran its US operations from April 2017 to July 2020. He was then MD & CEO of SBI Cards, before joining SBI's board as MD in January 2021, first over international banking and technology and from June 2022 over risk, compliance and stressed assets. Since November 2023 he runs large-corporate and commercial lending and the subsidiaries (cards, mutual fund, insurance, capital markets), and sits on all their boards.

people.name: Rana Ashutosh Kumar Singh
people.role: Managing Director (International Banking, Global Markets & Technology)
people.since: Joined SBI 1 August 1991; MD since 7 August 2024; current portfolio since 15 December 2025
people.bio: A Certified Associate of the Indian Institute of Bankers with an executive MBA from S. P. Jain Institute of Management & Research, Mumbai; he has attended leadership programmes at Harvard, Stanford, ISB and INSEAD. He joined SBI in August 1991 and has worked in retail and digital banking, credit, HR, international and transaction banking. He was CEO of SBI's Frankfurt operations, headed the Chandigarh circle and served as Deputy MD for retail, transaction banking, strategy (as Chief Digital Officer) and HR. He became MD in August 2024 over risk, compliance and stressed assets, and since December 2025 runs international banking, treasury and technology. He has been a nominee director on NPCI and its subsidiaries.

people.name: Rama Mohan Rao Amara
people.since: MD since 18 December 2024; current portfolio since 1 December 2025
people.bio: An engineering graduate who is also a CFA and a certified Financial Risk Manager. He worked on key SBI assignments in Singapore and the US, and served as Group Chief Risk Officer. He then spent two and a half years as MD & CEO of SBI Card. He joined the board as MD in December 2024, first over international banking, global markets and technology, and since December 2025 runs the retail banking business, which serves more than 530 million customers.

people.name: Ravi Ranjan
people.bio: A career banker who joined SBI as a probationary officer in 1991 and has more than 34 years of experience. He worked abroad in Hong Kong (debt syndication) and Los Angeles, headed the retail network in Bengaluru, and was President and COO of SBI Capital Markets. He then headed the Chennai circle as Chief General Manager and served as Deputy MD for the Corporate Accounts Group and for Global Markets. Since December 2025 he is the MD for risk, compliance and stressed-asset recovery.

people.name: Sunil Ramgopal Agrawal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a bachelor's degree in computer-science engineering and over 27 years in financial services and strategy. He was CFO of Life Insurance Corporation of India, where he worked on its initial public offering, and resigned from LIC in June 2026. SBI hired him on contract after advertising the post publicly in January 2026. He replaced Kameshwar Rao Kodavanti, who retired on 31 July 2026.

companies.changes: CFO Kameshwar Rao Kodavanti retired on 31 July 2026; Sunil Agrawal (ex-LIC CFO) took over on 1 August. Deputy MD and Chief Credit Officer Ashok Kumar Sharma also retired on 31 July 2026; Satyendra Kumar Singh took over his role. MD Vinay Tonse completed his term on 30 November 2025. Four shareholder directors were elected from 26 June 2026.

companies.styleNote: Northern Arc has no promoter. Its biggest holders are private-equity investors: LeapFrog (16.2%) and Augusta/Affirma Capital (13.8% after a block sale on 31 August 2026), both with nominee directors. A hired banker, Ashish Mehrotra, has run it since April 2022. Founder-era CEO Kshama Fernandes stays on as a non-executive director. No director is related to another.

people.name: Ashish Mehrotra
people.bio: Holds an MBA and has over 25 years in retail and commercial banking, wealth management and insurance. He spent over 20 years at Citibank, where he became a Managing Director and head of Citibank India's retail bank. He then ran Max Bupa Health Insurance (now Niva Bupa) as MD & CEO. He joined Northern Arc as MD & CEO on 1 April 2022, took it public in September 2024, and has pushed it towards direct retail and digital lending. He is non-executive chairman of Pragati Finserv, its microfinance arm, and sits on the board of Northern Arc Investment Managers, its fund business. The board raised his pay from April 2026 to ₹6.05cr fixed plus ₹3.52cr variable.

people.name: Atul Tibrewal
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Calcutta University and a chartered accountant with about 25 years in financial services. He began at Birla Corporation's Durgapur Cement Works and Magma Leasing, and rose to Senior Vice President and Head of Treasury at Magma Fincorp. He joined Northern Arc as CFO in May 2021 and was CFO through its September 2024 IPO. His treasury background matters because a non-bank lender depends on bank loans and bonds for its funding.

companies.changes: No change in KMP during FY26 or since. Anuradha Rao moved from independent to non-executive non-independent director on 31 October 2025; Vidya Krishnan joined as an independent director the same day. Augusta sold 35.4 lakh shares on 31 August 2026, cutting its stake to 13.83%.

companies.styleNote: A founder-run fintech. The two co-founders, Ranvir Singh (Chairman & CEO) and Krishnan Vishwanathan (CFO), are the only executive directors and the only named promoters. They are not related to each other or to any other director. Together they own about 24.8% after the May 2026 IPO (35.2% before it); foreign and domestic funds own most of the rest.

people.name: Ranvir Singh
people.since: Co-founder (company set up 2016); Chairman since 8 July 2025; re-appointed Executive Director to 2 January 2031
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter
people.stake: 2,42,91,232 shares: 20.45% before the IPO (31 March 2026, FY26 annual report), about 14.4% of the post-IPO share count; the two founders together 24.8% (June 2026)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from IIT Bombay with a management diploma from IIM Bangalore, and over 20 years in consulting and financial services. He worked at McKinsey & Company India and at Shinka Technologies and Si Creva Consulting before co-founding OnEMI, which runs the Kissht lending app, in 2016. He became Chairman in July 2025 and took the company public in May 2026. He is a founding member of the Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment (FACE), the digital-lending industry body.

people.name: Krishnan Vishwanathan
people.since: Co-founder; CFO since 21 July 2025; re-appointed Executive Director to 26 June 2031
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter
people.stake: 1,74,93,894 shares: 14.73% before the IPO (31 March 2026, FY26 annual report), about 10.4% of the post-IPO share count
people.bio: An electrical engineer from IIT Delhi with an MBA from Yale University, and over 22 years in consulting, finance and technology. Before the company he worked at McKinsey & Company India, at the chip firms Silicon Access Networks, Analog Devices and Alliance Semiconductor, and at Shinka Technologies and Si Creva Consulting, the same two firms as Ranvir Singh. He co-founded OnEMI and has been an executive director; he took over as CFO in July 2025 after Amit Gupta resigned, shortly before the IPO.

people.name: Neha Shivran
people.since: Named in the FY26 management team
people.bio: Heads data and analytics at Si Creva Capital, the RBI-registered lending subsidiary, which matters because the business depends on scoring small digital loans. She has over 15 years of experience and previously worked at Lenddo, TransUnion Software Services, State Bank of India, the RBS India Development Centre and Asymmetrix Solutions.

people.name: Sandeep Kadam
people.since: Named in the FY26 management team
people.bio: Runs the technology behind the Kissht app. He has over 15 years of experience and previously worked at AlbaCo, Dhani Loans and Services, Jwala Technology Systems, Saavn (the music-streaming company) and Yahoo.

companies.changes: CFO Amit Gupta resigned on 17 July 2025; co-founder Krishnan Vishwanathan took over on 21 July 2025. Vertex Ventures' nominee director Piyush Kharbanda resigned on 17 August 2026; three other investor nominees left in July 2025 ahead of the IPO. The shares listed on 8 May 2026.

companies.styleNote: A family-run lender. Managing Director Manish Shah, his wife Nikita Shah and their son Monil Shah are all whole-time directors; the fourth executive, CFO Jay Mota, is a long-serving employee. The chairman is an independent director. The family and its companies own 74.99%; the September 2026 fund-raise gives the promoters warrants but still cuts them to about 69.5% on full conversion.

people.name: Manish Kiritkumar Shah
people.since: Director since incorporation (1996); MD, re-appointed to 31 March 2030
people.relation: Promoter; husband of Nikita Shah and father of Monil Shah
people.stake: 13.06% (31 March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoter family and group companies 74.99%
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Mumbai University with over 25 years in non-bank lending. He has been a director since the company was set up in 1996 and built it into a lender for two-wheelers, three-wheelers, electric vehicles, used cars and small personal loans, sold mainly through vehicle dealers. As MD he sets strategy, handles key relationships with lenders and dealers, and drives technology. He took the company public in 2024. On 22 September 2026 the board re-appointed him for three years from April 2027 and approved warrants for the promoters as part of a ₹99.99cr fund-raise.

people.name: Nikita Manish Shah
people.relation: Promoter; wife of Manish Shah and mother of Monil Shah
people.bio: Completed higher-secondary education in commerce and has about 28 years with the group's finance business. She has been a director since the company was incorporated in 1996. She leads business development, the dealer network, partnerships and customer acquisition, and also oversees marketing and the company's charity (CSR) work. She was re-appointed as whole-time director from 15 January 2027.

people.name: Monil Manish Shah
people.relation: Promoter; son of Manish and Nikita Shah
people.bio: Holds a master's degree in marketing from Queen Mary University of London. He joined the board in 2017 and, as Chief Business Officer, runs sales, business strategy, marketing and expansion into new branches and products. The 2024 prospectus credits him with a pivotal role in the company's growth strategy. He was re-appointed as whole-time director from 15 January 2027, and is the family's next generation in the business.

people.name: Jay Khushal Mota
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Mumbai University with over 18 years of experience, all of it at Manba, which he joined in 2006. He joined the board as a whole-time director and CFO in February 2023. He runs financial planning, treasury and borrowing, budgeting, audit and tax, and regulatory compliance. He was re-appointed as whole-time director from 15 January 2027.

companies.changes: No executive changes. In September 2026 the board re-appointed Manish Shah as MD from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030, and Nikita Shah, Monil Shah and Jay Mota as whole-time directors from 15 January 2027. On 22 September 2026 it approved a ₹99.99cr issue at ₹135 a share: ₹67.5cr of new shares to outside investors and ₹32.5cr of warrants to the promoters (shareholder vote on 19 October).

companies.styleNote: A second-generation family business: the four Arora brothers (sons of founder Raghunath Arora) hold the chairman, two managing director and one whole-time director seats, and younger family members run the India, US, Europe and Middle East businesses. A hired CFO and functional chiefs support them. Promoters own 51.0% (June 2026), with no pledge.

people.name: Vijay Kumar Arora
people.since: 1978 (joined the family business); on the board since 2004
people.relation: Promoter; son of founder Raghunath Arora; brother of Ashwani, Surinder and Ashok Kumar Arora
people.stake: 6.62% (2,29,86,920 shares, March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 51.0%
people.bio: He holds a B.Sc. from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut. He joined his father's rice-trading business in 1978 and led the export of basmati under the Daawat brand in the 1980s, then the acquisitions that built the group abroad, including the Royal brand in the US. He has led the company for over four decades. He was earlier chairman of the agro-processing committee of the PHD Chamber of Commerce. He is paid by the Dubai subsidiary LT Foods Middle East DMCC rather than by the listed company, and shareholders re-appointed him as managing director at the September 2025 AGM.

people.name: Ashwani Kumar Arora
people.since: About 1988 (37+ years at LT Foods); on the board since 2007
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Vijay, Surinder and Ashok Kumar Arora
people.stake: 6.95% (2,41,41,325 shares, March 2026, up from 6.62% after an inter-se transfer from Surinder Kumar Arora; FY26 annual report)
people.bio: He has spent more than 37 years at LT Foods. The company credits him with building Daawat into its flagship brand, bringing modern packaging and branding to Indian rice, and starting the backward integration from contract farming to packaged rice. As CEO he now leads global expansion across strategy, operations, finance and marketing. He is the only executive director paid by the listed company itself: about ₹2.8cr in FY26, including a ₹50 lakh fixed commission, a 15.9% rise on the year.

people.name: Surinder Kumar Arora
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Vijay, Ashwani and Ashok Kumar Arora
people.stake: 6.29% (2,18,32,515 shares, March 2026, down from 6.62% after transferring 11,54,405 shares to Ashwani Kumar Arora; FY26 annual report)
people.bio: He has over 30 years of experience running the group's manufacturing and operations. He leads automation, process efficiency and technology in the plants, which the company ties to its margin goals. He is paid by the subsidiary Daawat Foods Limited rather than by the listed company.

people.name: Ashok Kumar Arora
people.since: 8 April 2026 (whole-time director; earlier President, Punjab operations)
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Vijay, Ashwani and Surinder Kumar Arora
people.bio: He holds a B.A. from Guru Nanak University, Punjab. He has more than 40 years in the food business and built the group's sourcing and processing operations in Punjab, where he was President of Punjab operations until joining the board. Shareholders approved his appointment as whole-time director for three years by postal ballot in 2026. He is paid by the subsidiary Daawat Foods Limited.

people.name: Ritesh Arora
people.role: CEO, India and Far East Business
people.relation: Member of the Arora promoter group; his exact relation to the directors is not disclosed in the sources reviewed
people.bio: He began his career at Ernst & Young in 2013 and then ran his own almond-trading business. He joined LT Foods as a management trainee and rose through regional and national sales roles to become CEO of the India and Far East business in 2020. He launched the Daawat biryani kits and Daawat Cuppa Rice and led the Kameda Seika joint venture for rice snacks. Shareholders approved a rise in his pay at the September 2025 AGM.

people.name: Abhinav Arora
people.relation: Member of the Arora promoter group; exact relation not disclosed in the sources reviewed
people.bio: He leads the executive team of LT Foods Americas (the Royal and Golden Star brands), overseeing finance, sales, marketing, supply chain, production, R&D and quality. North America is about half of group revenue, which makes this the group's largest business.

people.name: Sachin Gupta
people.bio: He is an IIM alumnus with over 20 years in finance. The company lists his areas as financial strategy and planning, risk management, M&A and treasury. He is a key managerial person, and his pay rose 8% in FY26.

companies.changes: Ashok Kumar Arora joined the board as whole-time director on 8 April 2026. Ritesh Sud (ex-Tata Consumer, Perfetti) became Chief Marketing Officer for India and Far East in April 2026; K. Ganapathy Subramaniam, head of marketing, left on 31 July 2026. Two independent directors, Neeru Singh and Satish Chander Gupta, resigned on 6 May 2026; Rima Gupta and Raj Kumar Jain joined as independent directors.

companies.styleNote: The founding Challa family runs it: founder Challa Rajendra Prasad is Executive Chairman, his son Challa Srishant is Managing Director and his son-in-law B. Mohan Krishna is Executive Director. His wife Challa Shantha Prasad sits on the board as a non-executive director and is the largest single holder (24.0%). A hired CEO and CFO run day-to-day operations and finance. Promoters own 46.1% (June 2026), with no pledge.

people.name: Challa Rajendra Prasad
people.relation: Founder; husband of director Challa Shantha Prasad, father of MD Challa Srishant and father-in-law of Executive Director B. Mohan Krishna
people.stake: 10.02% (1,33,78,519 shares, March 2026, FY26 annual report); family together about 46.1%
people.bio: An engineer by training with over four decades in business, he founded CCL Products in 1995. Before that he led Asian Coffee Ltd., which the company calls India's first non-multinational instant coffee venture. He has served on the Coffee Board of India, and in 2019 the International Instant Coffee Organization gave him a lifetime achievement award. Shareholders re-appointed him Executive Chairman for five years from 1 April 2026. He was paid ₹4.2cr in FY26.

people.name: Challa Srishant
people.relation: Son of Executive Chairman Challa Rajendra Prasad and director Challa Shantha Prasad; brother-in-law of Executive Director B. Mohan Krishna
people.bio: A gold medallist in corporate law from NALSAR University, he also holds a diploma in IT law. He joined CCL in 2005 and became Managing Director in 2014. He has led its expansion abroad, with plants in Vietnam and Switzerland, and has been a member of the Coffee Board of India. He was paid ₹5.66cr in FY26, including ₹1.7cr of profit-linked commission, and can also earn a 3% profit commission from the Vietnam subsidiary.

people.name: B. Mohan Krishna
people.since: On the board since July 2013; current term to February 2029
people.relation: Son-in-law of Challa Rajendra Prasad and Challa Shantha Prasad; brother-in-law of MD Challa Srishant
people.bio: A civil engineer from JNTU Hyderabad, aged 45, he has more than 22 years of experience putting up civil, mechanical and electrical projects. At CCL he runs plant building and modernisation, and he led the recent capacity expansions in India and Vietnam, including the government approvals. He is also a director of the subsidiaries CCL Food and Beverages and Continental Coffee. He was paid ₹4.66cr in FY26 and can earn a 2.5% profit commission from the Vietnam subsidiary.

people.name: Praveen Jaipuriar
people.bio: He studied economics (honours) at Delhi University and took an MBA from K.J. Somaiya in 1997. He then worked in sales, marketing and business management at Balsara Home Products and Dabur India, across health care, foods, oral care and home care. He ran the Continental Coffee branded business as CEO before becoming CEO of the listed company in October 2021. His FY26 pay rose 8.2%.

people.name: Chaithanya Agasthyaraju
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a B.Com, he has about 19 years in finance: treasury, controllership, planning and analysis, audit and corporate finance. He began in internal audit at Hyundai Motor India and later worked at Ashok Leyland and Ola Electric. Before joining CCL he was CFO and director of finance at Griffith Foods. He replaced V. Lakshmi Narayana, who resigned in early 2025.

companies.changes: No change in directors or KMP since the FY26 annual report. In May 2026 the board regrouped its list of senior management to match the current reporting structure.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Nadir Godrej side of the Godrej group: Godrej Industries owns 65.05% and the promoter group 67.7% (June 2026), with no pledge. A hired CEO & MD, Sunil Kataria (ex-Godrej Consumer, Raymond Lifestyle), runs the business, with professional CEOs for each division. Nadir Godrej, non-executive chairman, handed over on 14 August 2026 to his son Burjis Godrej, who is an executive director focused on new businesses and capital allocation. Nisaba Godrej, Pirojsha Godrej and Tanya Dubash sit as non-executive directors.

people.name: Sunil Kataria
people.since: 5 May 2025 (CEO & MD-designate); CEO & MD from 1 September 2025, term to August 2030
people.bio: He holds an economics degree from Delhi University and an MBA in marketing from IMT Ghaziabad. He began his career at Marico, where he spent over a decade in sales and marketing, and has about 30 years across consumer goods, telecom and retail. He was CEO of India & SAARC at Godrej Consumer Products, then Managing Director of Raymond Lifestyle for about three years until April 2025. He succeeded Balram Singh Yadav, who retired as MD on 31 August 2025.

people.name: Burjis Godrej
people.since: Executive Director since 1 November 2022; Chairperson since 14 August 2026
people.relation: Promoter group; son of Nadir Godrej, the former non-executive chairman
people.stake: Individual holding not separately disclosed in the FY26 annual report; promoter group together 67.7%, mainly Godrej Industries (65.05%)
people.bio: He holds a BS and an MS in Earth Systems from Stanford University and an MBA from Harvard Business School, and attended Cornell's executive programme for agribusiness in 2018. He was COO of the company's crop-care business in 2023–2024 and Managing Director of its listed subsidiary Astec LifeSciences in 2025–2026. As executive director he works on new products, technologies, business models, geographies and capital allocation. He was paid ₹1.78cr in FY26, up from ₹0.84cr in FY24, and shareholders are being asked to approve his pay as executive chairperson.

people.name: Ravishankar A.
people.since: CFO-designate from 21 September 2026; CFO from 1 October 2026
people.bio: An electronics engineering graduate with an MBA from IIM Lucknow, he has over two decades in corporate finance, controllership, planning and investor relations. He comes from Hindustan Unilever, where he was most recently VP Finance for the Beauty & Wellbeing business and helped integrate the Minimalist and OZiva acquisitions. Before that he was HUL's Group Finance Controller and Head of Investor Relations. He has worked in India, the UK and Switzerland and sat on the boards of Unilever group companies, including the listed Unilever Nepal.

people.name: Capt. (Dr.) A.Y. Rajendra
people.bio: He served in the Remount & Veterinary Corps of the Indian Army and joined the company in 1999 in the integrated poultry business, heading breeding, hatcheries and broiler contract farming in South India. In 2019 he became CEO of ACI Godrej Agrovet, the Bangladesh joint venture. He then led special projects, including direct milk collection from farmers for Creamline Dairy, before taking over animal feed, the largest business. It now also includes aqua feed.

people.name: Sougata Niyogi
people.bio: He has a B.Sc. in agriculture from Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, West Bengal, and a postgraduate degree from the International Management Institute, New Delhi. He joined the company in 2003 as a sales officer and worked in crop protection and agri-retail across several states. In April 2017 he became national sales head of crop protection. He now runs oil palm plantations and milling, where about half of the company's capex goes.

people.name: Sivaram Yadavalli
people.role: Head – Strategy & Business Development; Interim CEO, Crop Care Business from 25 November 2026
people.bio: He holds gold medals in engineering from the College of Engineering, Guindy, and in business management from XLRI Jamshedpur. He was a management consultant at Accenture, Strategy& (PwC), A.T. Kearney and Tata Strategic Management Group. At Godrej Agrovet since 2021, he leads growth strategy, M&A, business transformation and the incubation of new businesses. He will also run the crop-care business on an interim basis after its CEO leaves.

companies.changes: CFO S. Varadaraj takes early retirement on 30 September 2026; Ravishankar A. (ex-HUL) is CFO from 1 October. N.K. Rajavelu, CEO of crop care, resigned on 21 September 2026 for an outside job (last day 24 November); Sivaram Yadavalli will be interim CEO. HR head Mallika Mutreja left in August 2026; Anushree Singh (ex-JSW Energy) became CHRO on 7 September. Nadir Godrej stepped down as chairman on 13 August 2026 and Burjis Godrej took over. Balram Singh Yadav retired as MD on 31 August 2025.

companies.styleNote: Bimal Thakkar is Chairman, Managing Director and CEO. His sons run the US business (Shivaan, President) and sales and strategy (Sumer). A hired whole-time director runs operations and a hired CFO runs finance. The Thakkar family owns only 36.1% (June 2026). Bimal Thakkar takes no salary but can earn a commission of up to 5% of group profit before tax.

people.name: Bimal Thakkar
people.since: On the board since May 2003; current term October 2023 to September 2028
people.relation: Promoter; father of Shivaan Thakkar (President, USA) and Sumer Thakkar (VP, Sales & Strategy)
people.stake: 13.08% (1,43,70,850 shares, March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 36.1%
people.bio: He is a commerce graduate, aged 60, with more than 40 years in the business. The company credits him with turning ADF into a global processed-foods company that exports to over 60 countries. Under him it listed, built three plants in India, set up subsidiaries in the US, UK and Australia, and made acquisitions abroad. He is paid only commission, in US dollars through the US subsidiary: ₹5.99cr in FY26.

people.name: Arjuun Guuha
people.since: 18 September 2023 (Director – Operations); whole-time director since 31 October 2023, five-year term
people.bio: A chemical engineer with an executive MBA from ISB, he has about three decades in food operations. He held head-of-operations and CEO roles at Hindustan Unilever, ICI Paints, Marico, Tasty Bite and Allanasons. Just before ADF he ran technical operations for the Annapurna atta and Captain Cook salt brands at MAV Holdings. At ADF he runs manufacturing, procurement and supply chain, including the new Surat plant. He was paid ₹1.2cr in FY26.

people.name: Shivaan Thakkar
people.since: February 2019 (joined as Manager – Business & Strategy Development)
people.relation: Son of Chairman & MD Bimal Thakkar
people.bio: He joined in 2019 as manager for business and strategy development. He was named President of the US business, which is nearly half of company revenue and includes the Ashoka and Truly Indian brands and the US distribution arm. In the FY26 report he describes managing the cost impact of US tariffs with retail partners. He is paid in US dollars by the US subsidiary: ₹2.38cr in FY26, more than any executive except his father.

people.name: Sumer Thakkar
people.relation: Son of Chairman & MD Bimal Thakkar
people.bio: He is listed as a senior manager in charge of sales and strategy. The annual report shows him working on brand refreshes, new products and distribution for Ashoka in North America. The company does not publish a fuller profile.

people.name: Srinivas Ayyagari
people.bio: A qualified cost accountant with a master's in business management, he has over two decades in business finance, controllership, treasury, tax and investor relations across India and South-East Asia. He has worked at L'Oréal, Vodafone, Ferrero and ITC. Just before ADF he was Vice President – Finance at Eureka Forbes, leading its finance function. He replaced Shardul Doshi, who resigned in December 2025.

companies.changes: Purvi Dwivedi, General Manager – Accounts (senior management), resigned on 21 August 2026. Jeetendra Joshi, General Manager – Supply Chain, left on 28 February 2026. CFO Shardul Doshi resigned in December 2025; Srinivas Ayyagari took over in February 2026.

companies.styleNote: Run by three brothers, Anil Kumar Mittal (Chairman & MD) and Arun and Anoop Kumar Gupta (Joint MDs), and their children. Anil's daughter Priyanka Mittal is a whole-time director running exports. Their sons run paddy procurement (Ashish Mittal), rice procurement and the Dhuri plant (Kunal Gupta), the India business (Ayush Gupta) and bulk exports (Akshay Gupta). Promoters own 60.2% (June 2026), mostly through three family trusts, with no pledge. The only hired executive of note is the CFO. The auditor qualified the FY26 accounts because the Enforcement Directorate is prosecuting the company, its Dubai subsidiary and one of the joint MDs (not named in the annual report) in a money-laundering case linked to AgustaWestland.

people.name: Anil Kumar Mittal
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Joint MDs Arun and Anoop Kumar Gupta; father of Whole-time Director Priyanka Mittal and of Ashish Mittal (Head, Paddy Procurement)
people.stake: 100 shares directly; Anil Mittal Family Trust 18.52% and his HUF 1.53% (March 2026, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 60.2%
people.bio: The company calls him the founder who built KRBL, and its India Gate brand, into the leading Indian basmati company. He has been president of the All India Rice Exporters Association and of the Basmati Rice Farmers and Exporters Development Forum. He received the Silver Jubilee Award of the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences. He guides overall strategy and was paid ₹4.45cr in FY26.

people.name: Arun Kumar Gupta
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Anil Kumar Mittal and Anoop Kumar Gupta; father of Kunal Gupta (Head, Rice Procurement & Dhuri Unit)
people.stake: 100 shares directly; Arun Kumar Gupta Family Trust 17.99% and his HUF 2.07% (March 2026, FY26 annual report)
people.bio: He has over 44 years in rice and paddy supply chains and milling technology. He runs procurement, making sure good-quality paddy is bought on time and at the right cost, and led the move to advanced milling technology. He was paid ₹4.45cr in FY26.

people.name: Anoop Kumar Gupta
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Anil Kumar Mittal and Arun Kumar Gupta; father of Ayush Gupta (Head, India Business) and Akshay Gupta (Head, Bulk Exports)
people.stake: 100 shares directly; Anoop Kumar Gupta Family Trust 16.56%, his HUF 3.11% and Binita Gupta Family Trust 0.39% (March 2026, FY26 annual report)
people.bio: He holds a science degree from the University of Delhi and has over 40 years in the rice industry, focused on strategy and finance. He has served on the executive committee of the All India Rice Exporters Association. The company credits him with its capital structure, liquidity and credit ratings. He chairs the board's CSR & ESG committee and was paid ₹4.45cr in FY26.

people.name: Priyanka Mittal
people.relation: Promoter group; daughter of Chairman Anil Kumar Mittal; sister of Ashish Mittal
people.stake: 100 shares directly (March 2026, FY26 annual report); she is also a trustee, with her parents, of the Priyanka Mittal Family Trust (June 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: She studied at the University of Southern California and completed Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management programme. She has more than two decades running international sales and marketing and leads the global push for the India Gate brand. She was the first woman to chair FIEO's northern region, co-chairs FICCI's Saudi-India Business Council, and was named Businesswoman of the Decade by the Women Economic Forum in 2018. She attended 3 of 7 board meetings in FY26 and was paid ₹3.55cr.

people.name: Ayush Gupta
people.since: Not disclosed (over a decade in the business)
people.relation: Son of Joint MD Anoop Kumar Gupta; brother of Akshay Gupta
people.bio: He has over a decade of experience in the business. The company credits him with building KRBL's lead in modern trade, strengthening its distributor network and leading its marketing campaigns and move into e-commerce. He runs the domestic branded business, where the company aims to become a multi-category, multi-brand food company.

people.name: Akshay Gupta
people.since: Not disclosed (over a decade in the business)
people.relation: Son of Joint MD Anoop Kumar Gupta; brother of Ayush Gupta
people.bio: He has over a decade in commodity sales and consumer-goods marketing. He handles large commodity deals and customer relationships in bulk exports, and aligns buying with sales to manage stock across the group's brands.

people.name: Ashish Jain
people.bio: He is the company's CFO and a key managerial person, and sits on the board's risk management committee. The company does not publish a profile of his education or earlier career. His pay rose 8% in FY26.

companies.changes: No change in directors or senior management since the FY26 annual report. Company Secretary Piyush Asija resigned in February 2026; Shubham Kandhway took over on 14 May 2026.

companies.styleNote: The Saraf family runs it: Ashish Saraf is Chairman & MD, Vinita Saraf is Vice-Chairperson and Shrey Saraf is a whole-time director. The annual report says the three are related. Two long-serving employees, plant head Gautam Kumar Pal and CFO Ashok Jain, are also whole-time directors. Promoters owned 54.3% at June 2026, 46.2% of it held by Ashish Saraf alone, before the ₹500cr share sale in July 2026 diluted them. No pledge was found.

people.name: Ashish Saraf
people.since: Since the company's start in 2005; Chairman & MD since 23 October 2024
people.relation: Promoter; related to Vinita Saraf and Shrey Saraf (annual report), who by their names are his wife and son
people.stake: 46.17% (2,75,68,720 shares, March 2026, up from about 42% after 23.8 lakh shares moved to him from his relatives Agastya and Shrey Saraf in FY26; FY26 annual report); promoter group together 54.3% before the July 2026 share sale
people.bio: He has about 33 years in specialty fats and butters and has led the business since it began. His experience covers procurement, supply chains, global business development and developing custom products for chocolate, confectionery and cosmetics brands. He became Chairman and Managing Director in October 2024.

people.name: Vinita Saraf
people.since: Executive director since March 2006; MD 2017–2022; Vice-Chairperson since 23 October 2024
people.relation: Promoter; related to Ashish Saraf and Shrey Saraf (annual report); by name, wife of Ashish Saraf and mother of Shrey Saraf
people.bio: She holds a B.Com from Mount Carmel College, Bangalore, and has about 21 years with the company. She joined the board as an executive director in 2006 and was Managing Director from 2017 to 2022. She then became a non-executive director in November 2022 (chairperson by 2024), returned as executive chairperson in July 2024, and moved to Vice-Chairperson when Ashish Saraf took over as Chairman in October 2024.

people.name: Shrey Saraf
people.since: Executive director since August 2019; whole-time director since April 2022
people.relation: Promoter; related to Ashish Saraf and Vinita Saraf (annual report); by name, their son
