Founder Mohan Agarwal is Chairman and MD and his sons Akshay and Raghav Agarwal are whole-time directors, each running a business unit. Promoters own 84% (June 2026 shareholding): Mohan Agarwal 40.58%, Pratibha Agarwal 20.25%, Akshay and Raghav 10% each, plus family HUFs. The nominee director of former investor Global Scrap Processors left the board in August 2026.

people.name: Mohan Agarwal
people.relation: Founder; father of Akshay and Raghav Agarwal
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Delhi University with more than 40 years in aluminium alloy recycling. He founded the company and has been with the CMR group since it started, becoming MD in its current form in August 2021. He sets strategy and the long-term plan, aiming for global leadership in aluminium recycling and green manufacturing. He is also a director of the Material Recycling Association of India. He is up for re-appointment as MD at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Akshay Agarwal
people.since: 12 August 2021 (re-appointed for five years from August 2026)
people.relation: Son of the Chairman Mohan Agarwal; brother of Raghav Agarwal
people.stake: 10.00% (June 2026 shareholding), plus the Akshay Agarwal Family Private Trust; promoters together 84%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering (Honours) from BITS Pilani (Goa campus) and has over 11 years in aluminium alloy recycling. He heads the used-beverage-can (UBC) recycling business at Sambalpur, Odisha, responsible for its performance and profitability. He also leads customer strategy and the push into domestic and export markets.

people.name: Raghav Agarwal
people.since: 12 August 2021 (re-appointed for five years from August 2026)
people.relation: Son of the Chairman Mohan Agarwal; brother of Akshay Agarwal
people.stake: 10.00% (June 2026 shareholding), plus the Raghav Agarwal Family Private Trust; promoters together 84%
people.bio: A chartered accountant (associate member of ICAI) with over nine years in aluminium alloy recycling. He heads the Tirupati plant and its green (low-carbon) aluminium billet business, and also prepares strategic and operating plans and budgets for the billets, IT and commodity sales businesses.

people.name: Yugal Kishor Garg
people.bio: A fellow chartered accountant with more than 22 years in accounting and finance. He earlier worked at Himalayan Crest Power, Spentex Industries, Jagat Agro Commodities, Shree Laxmi Flavours (Gopal Group) and Synergy Advanced Metals. He became CFO in August 2025, replacing Virender Kumar Shimar, who held the post for only three months.

people.name: Shreechandra Singh Rana
people.bio: Holds a diploma in electrical engineering from Uttar Pradesh Technical University and has more than 40 years in engineering. Before CMR he worked at Shriram Bearings, Shriram Honda Power Equipment, Omax Autos, Flex Industries, Escorts, Eicher Farm Machinery and AEY Key Tan and Vessels. He has been in an executive role at CMR since 2011 and is responsible for profitability, quality and project timelines.

people.name: Deepak Kumar
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Maharishi Dayanand University, Rohtak, with more than 19 years in procurement, all at CMR since 2006. He runs the buying of secondary aluminium scrap for all plants and decides trading terms with suppliers.

companies.changes: CFO Yugal Kishor Garg resigned on 3 October 2026 for personal reasons, effective 23 October 2026; the board will consider naming Satish Kumar Kaushik, recently appointed President – Finance, as CFO at its November 2026 meeting. CFO Virender Kumar Shimar joined in May 2025 and resigned in August 2025; Yugal Kishor Garg replaced him. Nominee director Peter Francis Amour (Global Scrap Processors) left on 10 August 2026 and Ankur Singh joined as an additional director. Independent director Satpal Arora resigned in May 2025.

companies.styleNote: Two promoter families run it together: Chairman & MD Paras Savla (the Shantilal Savla family) and MD Rupesh Savla. A 2017 SEBI order (on the group's earlier listed company, then also called Deep Industries) notes the two groups have no blood relationship, and the annual report says no directors are related. Paras Savla's relatives Dharen Savla and Shail Savla are both named Presidents. Promoters own 63.49% (June 2026): Rupesh Savla's family trust 31.49% and the Shantilal Savla family about 32%.

people.name: Paras Shantilal Savla
people.relation: Promoter; head of the Shantilal Savla family group; Shail Savla is a relative (AGM notice 2026)
people.stake: 200 shares personally (June 2026 shareholding pattern); his family group (Shantilal Savla Family Trust 12.7%, Dharen 6.43%, Priti Paras 6.43%, Mita Manoj 4.16%, Shail 2.27%) about 32%
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Gujarat University with more than 30 years in the business. The company credits him with turning Deep from a transport-services firm into a supplier of oil and gas field equipment and services and services. He chairs the board and signs the CEO certification. He drew ₹50.6 lakh in FY26. The group's related companies include Prabha Energy, a promoter-group oil and gas company to which Deep has lent money, which investors should watch.

people.name: Rupesh Kantilal Savla
people.relation: Promoter; heads the second promoter family (not related by blood to Paras Savla, per SEBI 2017)
people.stake: 400 shares personally; as trustee of the Rupesh Savla Family Trust he controls 31.49% (June 2026)
people.bio: Holds a commerce degree from Gujarat University and an MBA from Bentley College in the USA. He has more than 28 years in the energy sector and oversees coordination and execution of the company's projects. He is also Managing Director of Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India), the listed offshore-vessel subsidiary Deep took over through insolvency. He drew ₹46.4 lakh in FY26. In 2017 SEBI exempted his family trust from an open offer when it took over family members' shares in the group's then-listed company.

people.name: Rohan Vasantkumar Shah
people.since: With Deep for about 14 years; board since June 2021
people.bio: A chartered accountant with more than 20 years in finance, accounts, audit and compliance, most of it at Deep, where he held several senior finance roles before becoming CFO. He won the Financial Express CFO of the Year award in 2019 (small enterprises, services). He is also an executive director of Dolphin Offshore Enterprises. He was paid ₹54.6 lakh in FY26 and was re-appointed as a director at the September 2026 AGM.

people.name: Dharen Shantilal Savla
people.since: Named senior management as of March 2026
people.relation: Member of the Shantilal Savla promoter family
people.bio: Listed as President in the FY26 annual report's senior management list. The company discloses no further profile for him.

people.name: Shail Manoj Savla
people.relation: Relative of Chairman Paras Savla (AGM notice); son of promoter Manoj Savla
people.bio: Appointed President from 14 May 2026, initially without pay; shareholders approved a salary from 1 October 2026 at the September 2026 AGM as a related-party 'office of profit'. The notice says he is responsible for providing leadership and direction to the business, but gives no education or career details.

people.name: Rajeev Kumar Sinha
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in petroleum engineering from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and has more than 30 years in the oil and gas industry. His experience covers project management, operations and maintenance, production management, asset management and business strategy. The board made him senior management personnel from 1 August 2026.

companies.changes: Company Secretary Shilpa Sharma resigned with effect from 31 July 2026. COO Rajeev Kumar Sinha was named senior management from 1 August 2026. Shail Savla became President in May 2026. Independent director Ashok Patel died in December 2025.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Hinduja group: Gulf Oil International (Mauritius) owns 66.85% (June 2026). Chairman Sanjay G. Hinduja and his first cousin Shom Ashok Hinduja sit as non-executive directors. The business is run by a hired MD & CEO, Ravi Chawla, with a professional team.

people.name: Ravi Shamlal Chawla
people.since: Joined 2007 as President – Lubricants; MD since June 2014
people.bio: Has a commerce degree from Sydenham College and a Master of Management Studies (marketing) from Mumbai University. Before Gulf he worked at Wipro Consumer Products, CEAT, Polaroid and Mahindra & Mahindra's farm equipment division, and from 1998 to 2006 was in top management at Pennzoil-Quaker State India (a Shell company). He joined Gulf Oil Corporation in 2007 to run the lubricants business, which was demerged and listed in 2014, and he has been MD since. Under him Gulf grew two to three times faster than the industry and became a top-three private lubricant player. Since 2018 he also looks after the group's Asia-Pacific cluster markets; the annual report says he leads the move into high-growth areas such as e-mobility and acquisitions.

people.name: Manish Kumar Gangwal
people.since: CFO before 2019; Whole-time Director since 22 December 2025
people.bio: A rank-holding chartered accountant, a company secretary and a graduate member of the cost accountants' institute. He has more than 30 years in finance, planning, strategy, mergers, fund-raising, investor relations, accounts, secretarial work and tax. Earlier he worked at Gulf Oil Corporation, Poddar Pigments and Hindustan Development Corporation. He has also been a board member and finance cluster lead for Gulf's South-East Asian entities. He joined the board as a whole-time director in December 2025 for five years.

people.name: Abhijit Kulkarni
people.bio: Holds a B.E. from the Government College of Engineering, Pune, and an MBA from Symbiosis Institute of Business Management. He has more than two decades of experience at Unilever, Castrol and Coca-Cola, including 16 years at Unilever, where his last role was cluster general manager for the ice-cream business in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam. At Gulf he runs the B2C and B2B businesses (excluding OEM) and marketing, reporting to the MD.

companies.changes: Sandeep Bangia, Head – Strategy, Transformation and E-Mobility, resigned effective 31 August 2026. Company Secretary Ashish Pandey resigned effective 16 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Part of the D.P. Jindal group. The founder Dharam Pal Jindal is non-executive Chairman; his son Raghav Jindal is Managing Director. Day-to-day drilling operations are run by a hired CEO, Narayan Ramaswamy. Promoters own 66.78% (June 2026), mostly through group companies such as Jindal Global Finance, Sudha Apparels, Stable Trading, Crishpark Vincom and Jindal Pipes.

people.name: Raghav Jindal
people.relation: Son of Chairman Dharam Pal Jindal
people.stake: 1,92,976 shares, 0.67% (FY26 annual report); promoter group together 66.78%
people.bio: Holds an MSc in Business Management from the London School of Economics. He is Managing Director of Jindal Drilling and also Joint Managing Director of Maharashtra Seamless and Managing Director of Jindal Pipes, both D.P. Jindal group companies. His father is non-executive chairman of Maharashtra Seamless too, so his time is split across the group. He drew ₹4.32 crore in FY26, by far the highest pay in the company.

people.name: Narayan Ramaswamy
people.bio: A mechanical engineer (B.Tech, University of Calicut, 1989) with more than 31 years of experience at appointment, including hands-on offshore, project and operations management. The company describes him as coming from an upstream jack-up rig operations background, with skills in strategic planning, safety management and equipment commissioning. He was appointed CEO and key managerial personnel on 23 January 2023. He was paid ₹1.17 crore in FY26.

people.name: Pawan Kumar Rustagi
people.bio: A chartered accountant. He was already CFO when he was also named Compliance Officer in September 2021, and he held the Company Secretary post as well from March to May 2022, when a separate secretary was hired. He was paid ₹49.4 lakh in FY26.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the FY26 annual report. Independent director Sunil Arora resigned in July 2025.

companies.styleNote: Founder-run by two brothers: Vikas Jain (Chairman & MD) and his younger brother Piyush Jain (Joint MD). Both were re-appointed for three years from 20 November 2026 at the September 2026 AGM. The Jain family owns 65.94% (July 2026).

people.name: Vikas Jain
people.relation: Founder; elder brother of Piyush Jain
people.bio: Holds an MBA from Johnson & Wales University, USA. He founded the company in 2006 and has been with it since incorporation, with more than 22 years in exploration and mining. He handles business development, finance, overall strategy and client relationships. His new three-year term carries a commission of 0.5% of profits on top of salary.

people.name: Piyush Jain
people.relation: Co-promoter; younger brother of Vikas Jain
people.bio: Has an MSc in Management and Entrepreneurship from Nottingham Trent University, UK, and a BSc in Business and Management Studies from IILM, New Delhi (affiliated to the University of Bradford). He joined the board in 2009 and has about 18 years in exploration and mining. He runs operations, procurement, safety (HSE) and business development. His new term carries a 0.4% profit commission.

people.name: Dinesh Agarwal
people.bio: A graduate of the University of Allahabad who has been CFO since October 2017; he was earlier a director of Metro Tyres. The company publishes no fuller profile.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the FY25 annual report. Independent directors Meenakshi Anand and Shivi Sabharwal were re-appointed for second terms from August 2026.

companies.styleNote: Run by the Pilani family. Founder Ramesh Pilani was CFO until he stepped down on 12 May 2026 because of age and health; his son Rishi Pilani is Chairman & MD. Promoters own 39.02% (June 2026), partly through family firms such as Susram Financial Services & Realty (16.59%) and Ganesh Risk Management (6.9%). In 2024 a former CEO, Ramakant Pilani, was accused by the company of opening an unauthorised bank account and borrowing in a subsidiary's name by forging Ramesh and Rishi Pilani's signatures; he resigned and legal cases are under way. The CFO post has been vacant since May 2026.

people.name: Rishi Ramesh Pilani
people.since: Board since October 2006; CMD since 2011; re-appointed to September 2029
people.relation: Son of founder Ramesh Pilani; second-generation promoter
people.stake: nil since 26 August 2026: he gifted his 17,76,003 shares (2.47%) and his wife Poonam gifted her 1.50% to relative Ravi Pilani; promoter group unchanged at 39.02%
people.bio: A chemical engineer with master's degrees in industrial engineering and finance from the USA, who worked at General Electric in the United States before joining the family business. He has over 23 years of experience and has been Chairman & MD since 2011, driving strategy, operations and growth. The company credits him with the steady growth of its liquid storage terminal business at JNPT, Goa and Cochin. His pay is linked to net profit (₹1.64 crore in FY26, down 14%). He is also managing director of a material subsidiary.

people.name: Shyam Nihate
people.since: Joined 2019; board since April 2023 (term to April 2028)
people.bio: Holds a B.E. in electronics and power engineering from NIT Nagpur and an executive postgraduate programme in management from IIM Indore. He spent 17 years with a public-sector oil company before joining Ganesh Benzoplast in 2019 as GM – Operations and Admin. He has 26 years of experience in terminal operations, logistics, marketing and supply chain. He now oversees operations and infrastructure across the company's liquid storage terminals. He was paid ₹64.8 lakh in FY26.

companies.changes: Founder and CFO Ramesh Pilani stepped down on 12 May 2026; no new CFO has been announced. In August 2026 Rishi and Poonam Pilani gifted all their shares (3.97%) to Ravi Pilani, who became a named promoter. Independent director Jagruti Gaikwad's term ended in September 2025; Amruta Thali joined in August 2025.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by Dr. Kapil Garg through his company Oilmax Energy, which owns 56.01% (promoters 56.14%, June 2026). He is Managing Director; his son Aman Garg is a non-executive director. The chairman, N.M. Borah (ex-CMD of Oil India), is independent. Oilmax, Dr. Garg's oil and gas producing business, is being merged into the listed company, which would bring his whole business under one roof.

people.name: Dr. Kapil Garg
people.relation: Promoter (through Oilmax Energy); father of non-executive director Aman Garg
people.stake: nil directly; controls 56.01% through Oilmax Energy; promoter Ritu Garg holds 0.13% (June 2026)
people.bio: Holds a B.E. and a master's in chemical engineering from IIT Roorkee and a Ph.D. on modelling gas jet fires. He began as a production engineer at ONGC and later held production management roles at Enron Oil & Gas and GAIL, then rose to country manager and managing director of BG Group in India. He founded Oilmax Energy in 2008, which took control of Asian Energy and whose merger into it is now before the NCLT. He has also personally guaranteed some of the company's bank facilities, along with promoter Ritu Garg and his son Aman. He drew ₹2.77 crore in FY26 including a performance bonus.

people.name: Nirav Talati
people.bio: A chartered accountant and commerce graduate of H.R. College, Mumbai, with more than 20 years in accounting, tax, MIS and finance at listed companies. Before Asian Energy he worked at Samsara Shipping and Mercator, and also practised as an independent finance and tax adviser. He handles consolidation, investor presentations, projections, fund-raising, tax planning, compliance and treasury.

companies.changes: Three senior managers resigned in August 2026: Diveshkumar Sharma (VP – Seismic), Amit Pathak (GM – Procurement) and Ajay Agnihotri (Manager – O&M). Non-executive directors Mukesh Jain and Brij Mohan Bansal (independent) left in May 2025 and January 2026; Parikshit Datta joined as a non-executive director in May 2025.

companies.styleNote: A Parekh family business. Ramesh Parekh, with the company since it was formed, is Chairman & MD; his sons Samir (Vice Chairman & Joint MD) and Aslesh (Joint MD) each run a plant and a business line. The annual report confirms the three are related to each other. The wider Parekh family owns 66.6% (June 2026).

people.name: Ramesh Babulal Parekh
people.since: Since incorporation (1992); MD re-appointed to September 2030
people.relation: Founder-promoter; father of Samir and Aslesh Parekh
people.stake: 2,80,13,889 shares, 28.62% (FY26 annual report; 28.75% in June 2026); Parekh family and promoter group 66.6%
people.bio: A commerce graduate of the University of Mumbai with over 40 years in petroleum and specialty oils. He has been with Gandhar since it was incorporated and looks after overall management and performance. He is a director of the Manufacturers of Petroleum Specialities Association and of family companies including Gandhar Shipping and Logistics, Texol Lubritech FZC and Texol Oils FZC (the Sharjah business), and is a partner in Gandhar Life Spaces LLP.

people.name: Samir Ramesh Parekh
people.since: Joined 2003 as a sales executive; re-appointed JMD from October 2026 to September 2031
people.relation: Son of Chairman Ramesh Parekh; brother of Aslesh Parekh
people.bio: A commerce graduate of the University of Mumbai with over 20 years in making and selling petroleum and specialty oils. He joined the company as a sales executive in 2003 and now runs the Silvassa manufacturing plant. He is also a director of Gandhar Shipping and Logistics, Nature Pure Wellness and Gandhar Lifesciences, and a partner in Gandhar Developers LLP.

people.name: Aslesh Ramesh Parekh
people.since: Joined 2003 as a sales executive; re-appointed JMD from October 2026 to September 2031
people.relation: Son of Chairman Ramesh Parekh; brother of Samir Parekh
people.bio: A science graduate of the University of Mumbai with a postgraduate certificate in e-management and business administration from MET Asian Management Development Centre. He has over 20 years in petroleum and specialty oils, having joined as a sales executive in 2003. He runs the Taloja plant and heads the international business. He is a director of Texol Oils FZC, Nature Pure Wellness and Gandhar Lifesciences.

people.name: Jatin Dhamani
people.bio: A finance and procurement professional with over 30 years in specialty oils, lubricants and petrochemicals. He has managed international procurement and negotiated long-term supply contracts with refineries in the Middle East and South Korea, and his experience covers treasury, cash flow, tax, compliance, risk and import management. At Gandhar he oversees finance and procurement.

people.name: Indrajit Bhattacharyya
people.bio: Brings long experience in finance and administration. He was earlier CFO and a director of Interdril (Asia) and CFO of Valecha Engineering. He has been Gandhar's CFO since 5 January 2017, including through its IPO in FY24, which raised ₹500.69 crore.

companies.changes: Senior manager Sanjay Bharadwaj resigned in May 2026. Independent director Deena Mehta resigned on 12 May 2026; S.K. Sandhu (May 2026) and Shyam Agrawal (July 2026) joined as independent directors. Company Secretary Jayshree Soni left in December 2025; Binal Khosla replaced her.

companies.styleNote: A government-controlled refiner (a Navratna since June 2026) and subsidiary of Indian Oil, which owns 51.89%; Naftiran Intertrade of Iran owns 15.4% (June 2026). IOCL's Arvinder Singh Sahney is non-executive Chairman, and the MD and functional directors are career refinery officials appointed by the Petroleum Ministry, not owners. None of them is related to another.

people.name: H. Shankar
people.since: Board since October 2020 (Director Technical); MD since 2 April 2025, term to March 2029
people.bio: A mechanical engineer with an MBA in general management and more than three decades across all areas of refinery operations. He joined the CPCL board as Director (Technical) on 1 October 2020, leading work on new energies and digitalisation. He held additional charge as MD from 16 July 2024 and was made full MD by the Petroleum Ministry from 2 April 2025, while also holding the Director (Technical) post until January 2026. He was paid about ₹78.5 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Rohit Kumar Agrawala
people.bio: A chartered accountant with an MBA (gold medal) from Xavier Institute of Management, Bhubaneswar. He joined Indian Oil in 1997 and worked in its Guwahati, Paradip, Vadodara and Mathura refineries, with more than ten years in corporate finance and several change-management assignments. Before CPCL he was Chief General Manager (Finance) in IOCL's business development division in New Delhi. He was appointed Director (Finance) by the Petroleum Ministry and took charge on 1 March 2023.

people.name: P. Kannan
people.bio: A B.Tech in chemical engineering from Alagappa College of Technology, Anna University. He has spent more than 34 years at CPCL in manufacturing, process engineering and other roles, and headed operations at both the Manali and Nagapattinam refineries. He was Chief General Manager (Technical) before joining the board as Director (Operations) on 1 August 2023. His term on the board ends on 31 October 2026.

people.name: S.G. Venkatesh
people.bio: A chemical engineer from the University of Kerala with 31 years in refining operations, process design and optimisation, and petrochemicals. He was Executive Director (Petrochemicals) at Indian Oil, where he ran its petrochemicals business, before joining CPCL as Director (Technical) on 5 January 2026.

companies.changes: Director (Operations) P. Kannan's term ends on 31 October 2026; a successor has not yet been announced. Company Secretary P. Shankar left on 30 June 2026; Lalit Kumar Mohanty took over from 1 July 2026. V.C. Asokan joined as IOCL nominee director in April 2026.

companies.styleNote: A joint venture listed in 2025: Aegis Logistics owns 44.71% and Vopak India 42.23% (promoters 86.93%, June 2026). Raj Chandaria, who also heads Aegis Logistics as its MD, is Chairman & MD but takes no pay here. Day-to-day work is led by President Sudhir Malhotra, on deputation from Aegis, and a team mostly transferred from Aegis. Vopak has two non-executive nominees. No directors or managers are related to each other.

people.name: Raj Kapurchand Chandaria
people.since: Board since May 2013; CMD since October 2024 (term to October 2029)
people.relation: Head of promoter Aegis Logistics (its Managing Director)
people.stake: nil directly (FY26 annual report); Aegis Logistics holds 44.71%
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. (Economics) from the London School of Economics and an MBA from Boston University's Graduate School of Management. He has more than 25 years in oil, gas and chemical logistics and has been with Aegis Logistics since 1999, where he is Managing Director. He draws no salary from Aegis Vopak for his current term. He sits on eight other public-company boards, mostly Aegis group companies, and signs board reports from Toronto. The IPO prospectus disclosed a pending factory-licence complaint (2024) naming him as a director of group company Aegis Gas.

people.name: Sudhir Omprakash Malhotra
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Shivaji University with a diploma in marketing management from Welingkar Institute and a postgraduate diploma in shipping and export management. He has more than 34 years in oil and gas and has been with Aegis Logistics since 1990; Aegis's website lists him as its Chief Executive Officer. He was made President of Aegis Vopak in October 2024 on deputation, and Aegis Vopak paid him nothing in FY25.

people.name: Manoj Sharma
people.since: CFO since November 2023; moved from Aegis Logistics in 2022
people.bio: A chartered accountant and commerce graduate of Devi Ahilya University, Indore, with more than 20 years in oil and gas, telecom and cement. Before Aegis Logistics he worked at Reliance Communications Infrastructure and Vasavadatta Cement (Kesoram Industries). He moved to Aegis Vopak in 2022 and became CFO on 2 November 2023. He was paid ₹45.8 lakh in FY25.

people.name: Prakash Lachmichand Hiranandani
people.bio: A chemical plant engineering graduate of the University of Bombay with more than 31 years in oil and gas. He moved from Aegis Logistics to Aegis Vopak in 2022 and runs the liquids terminal business. He was the best-paid manager in FY25 at ₹2.23 crore.

people.name: Priju Thomas
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Shivaji University with more than 29 years in oil and gas. He moved from Aegis Logistics in 2022 and heads the LPG terminal business. He was paid ₹1.52 crore in FY25.

companies.changes: Vice President – HR & Administration Girish Gurkhe retired in February 2026. Vopak nominee Wimal Samlal joined the board in October 2025. No executive changes since the FY26 annual report.

companies.styleNote: A Nirani family company, listed in 2025. Founder Vijaykumar Nirani is MD; his younger brother Vishal Nirani is an executive director; his wife Sushmitha Nirani is a non-executive director. Their father Murugesh Nirani and other relatives are also promoters. The family owns 70.55% (June 2026), and part of it is pledged to lenders. The chairman is independent (M.B. Dyaberi since July 2026).

people.name: Vijaykumar Murugesh Nirani
people.relation: Founder; son of promoter Murugesh Nirani; elder brother of Vishal Nirani; husband of Sushmitha Nirani
people.stake: 17.88% (June 2026 shareholding pattern); Nirani family together 70.55%, some pledged as loan security
people.bio: Aged 33, he holds a bachelor's degree in business (finance and accounting) from James Cook University, Singapore. He founded TruAlt in 2021 and has led it since, building it into what the company calls one of India's leading integrated bioenergy companies. The company says he works with policymakers and industry bodies on India's clean-energy policy. The family's Nirani Sugars is a group company, and his shares are among those pledged for group borrowings.

people.name: Vishal Nirani
people.relation: Promoter; younger brother of MD Vijaykumar Nirani; son of Murugesh Nirani
people.bio: Aged 29, he has been with TruAlt since incorporation and handles manufacturing, project execution, supply chain and operations, with about seven years of experience. The IPO prospectus and the annual report's director profile list Class XII (CBSE) as his qualification, while the 2026 AGM notice calls him a mechanical engineering graduate of Brunel University, London, a mismatch investors may want clarified. He is also Managing Director of Nirani Sugars and Riga Sugar and a partner in Accutrade Global LLP, so his time is shared with family businesses. His pay ratio to the median employee matches the MD's.

people.name: Anand Murugan Jakkampati Durairaj
people.bio: A science graduate of the American College, Madurai Kamaraj University, with a postgraduate diploma in industrial fermentation and alcohol technology from Vasantdada Sugar Institute, Pune. He has about 28 years of experience; earlier he was a general manager at Piccadily Agro Industries and a unit head at Sovereign Distilleries. He is the only executive director from outside the family.

people.name: Anand Kishore
people.bio: A commerce graduate of Patna University with an MBA from ICFAI University, Dehradun, and JAIIB and CAIIB (international banking) certifications. He spent his earlier career as a banker at South Indian Bank, Corporation Bank and Union Bank, rising to assistant general manager, with about 15 years in finance. He joined TruAlt on 19 February 2024 and was paid ₹65.5 lakh in FY25.

companies.changes: Chairman Y.B. Ramakrishna (independent) stepped down on 28 July 2026; independent director M.B. Dyaberi became Chairman for one year. The company has had three company secretaries since May 2025; Monu Kumar has held the post since February 2026.

companies.styleNote: No family runs EPL. Blackstone (through Epsilon Bidco) is the promoter with 26.38% at March 2026, and Indorama Ventures owns 24.82% after buying half of Blackstone's stake in May 2025. The board is chaired by an independent director, Davinder Singh Brar, and the business is run by a hired MD and CEO. Blackstone's Amit Dixit and Animesh Agrawal, and Indorama founder Aloke Lohia, sit as non-executive directors. After the planned merger with Indorama's Indovida India, Indorama is expected to become co-promoter with about 51.8% and Blackstone to hold about 16.6%. No directors are related to one another.

people.name: Hemant Bakshi
people.stake: nil (February 2026 postal ballot notice); granted 19,23,319 stock options
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in chemical engineering from IIT Bombay and an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. He spent about three decades at Unilever in India and Indonesia, including as CEO (President Director) of Unilever Indonesia, a $3 billion listed company, and later as its non-executive chairman. He also founded and led GroNext Technologies, a Unilever-funded business that sells to small traditional shops, and grew it to 12 markets in Latin America, Asia and Turkey with over $1 billion of gross merchandise value. Forbes named him business leader of the year in 2016 and 2019. He took over from Anand Kripalu on 1 January 2026 and will lead EPL through its merger with Indorama's Indovida business. He is new to packaging, so the first full year under him is the test.

people.name: Deepak Goyal
people.bio: A chartered accountant and a commerce graduate from the University of Rajasthan, with over 22 years in consumer goods, financial services and hospitality technology. He spent about 15 years at PepsiCo in strategy, planning, controllership, operations finance and commercial finance, ending as category and commercial finance director. He then became CFO of OYO Vacation Homes in Europe (based in Switzerland), where he led several acquisitions. He had earlier worked at GE Commercial Finance. He joined EPL as CFO in August 2023.

people.name: M. R. (Ram) Ramasamy
people.since: COO since 1 July 2015; at EPL for over 30 years
people.bio: Has an engineering degree in chemicals and plastics and an executive MBA from Lansbridge University, Canada. He has spent more than 30 years at EPL. Before becoming COO in July 2015 he ran all of EPL's global divisions as President, International Business. Earlier he headed manufacturing and technology globally, was Chief Technology Officer, Director of Corporate Affairs and Senior Vice President of Operations and Supply Chain. He also teaches manufacturing excellence and Six Sigma as visiting faculty at IIT Bombay.

people.name: Sonal Jain
people.role: Global Chief HR, Transformation and Marketing Officer
people.bio: Joined EPL in June 2023 as Global Chief Human Resources Officer and now also leads transformation and marketing. She has over 21 years of experience at large companies including Unilever, Johnson & Johnson and Wipro Technologies. She has been a member of CII's national committee on leadership and HR since 2021 and of the Forbes Human Resources Council since 2024. She is a certified executive coach.

people.name: Kamlesh Jain
people.bio: A chartered accountant with about 24 years of experience across retail, ports, outsourcing, pharmaceuticals and energy. Before EPL he worked at Prism Informatics, the Aegis-Essar group, Enercon, Future Group and Adani Ports. He joined EPL in 2014 and became Chief Information Officer in 2022, with responsibility for IT systems, digital tools and analytics.

people.name: Onkar Ghangurde
people.role: Head – Legal, Company Secretary & Compliance Officer
people.bio: A company secretary (associate member of ICSI) and a law graduate from ILS Law College, Pune, with about 14 years in legal, compliance and governance work for listed companies. Before joining EPL in September 2023 he worked at Aditya Birla Fashion & Retail, Kansai Nerolac Paints and Tata International on restructurings, joint ventures and fund-raising.

companies.changes: Anand Kripalu retired as MD & Global CEO on 31 December 2025, stayed as executive director to 31 March 2026 and has been a non-executive director since 1 April 2026. Hemant Bakshi took over as MD & Global CEO on 1 January 2026. Thomas Stephen (ex-Cummins, Grindwell Norton, Piramal Glass) joined in August 2025 as President, AMESA. The merger with Indorama's Indovida India (announced March 2026, CCI-cleared May 2026) still needs tribunal and shareholder approval and will make Indorama co-promoter.

companies.styleNote: A Kanoria family company. Saket Kanoria is Chairman and MD, and two of his sons, Akshay and Vidur, are executive directors; his third son Rishav is a non-executive director. The previous chairman, K. K. Kanoria, stepped down as executive chairman in February 2026 because of age and is now honorary Chairman Emeritus. Promoters (family members and family holding companies) own 55.74%. The only non-family executives are long-serving finance director S. G. Nanavati and CFO Jitendra Jain.

people.name: Saket Kanoria
people.since: On the board and MD since February 1991; also Chairman since 10 February 2026
people.relation: Promoter; father of Akshay, Vidur and Rishav Kanoria
people.stake: 0.47% (43,004 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 55.74%
people.bio: Holds an MBA in finance from George Washington University, USA. He has been Managing Director since February 1991, so he has run the company's day-to-day operations for about 35 years, through its growth from one Silvassa carton plant into a multi-plant maker of cartons, rigid boxes and flexible packaging. He became Chairman on 10 February 2026 when K. K. Kanoria stepped down, with no change to his pay or terms. He is 62. He was paid ₹7.24 crore in FY26.

people.name: Akshay Kanoria
people.relation: Son of Saket Kanoria; brother of Vidur and Rishav Kanoria
people.bio: A graduate of the University of Pennsylvania, USA. He supervises the day-to-day running of the plants at Silvassa, Haridwar, Goa and Guwahati and supports the MD on policy, strategy and business development. He has been a director since May 2016 and is 35. He was paid ₹2.44 crore in FY26 and was re-appointed on retirement by rotation at the August 2026 AGM.

people.name: Vidur Kanoria
people.since: Joined May 2016; Executive Director since 26 May 2023 (re-appointed to May 2029)
people.relation: Son of Saket Kanoria; brother of Akshay and Rishav Kanoria
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in business administration (finance, operations and technology management) from Boston University. He joined TCPL in May 2016 as an executive in business development and was made an executive director in May 2023. He supervises the plants at Silvassa, Haridwar, Goa, Chennai and Guwahati and supports the MD on policy and strategy. His re-appointment to May 2029 was approved at the August 2026 AGM, but with 10.7% of votes against, noticeably more dissent than for other resolutions.

people.name: S. G. Nanavati
people.since: With TCPL since 1989; Executive Director since May 2011 (re-appointed from June 2026 for three years)
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary. He has worked at TCPL since 1989 and has been an executive director since May 2011. He looks after finance, legal affairs and general administration, and has also acted as the company's compliance officer. He is 69, and shareholders re-appointed him for another three years from June 2026.

people.name: Jitendra Jain
people.bio: Became CFO on 1 April 2022, taking over from Vivek Poddar. The company does not publish a detailed profile of his education or earlier career. He is a key managerial person and handles capital allocation and financial reporting.

companies.changes: K. K. Kanoria stepped down as Executive Chairman on 9 February 2026 due to age and was named Chairman Emeritus (an honorary, advisory role); Saket Kanoria became Chairman and MD from 10 February 2026. Vidur Kanoria and S. G. Nanavati were re-appointed as executive directors at the August 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: Run by its two co-founders and their family. J. Lakshmana Rao is Chairman and MD; his brother-in-law and co-founder A. Subramanyam is Deputy MD; the CFO, A. Seshu Kumari, is Lakshmana Rao's sister and Subramanyam's wife; and Lakshmana Rao's son Rana Pratap joins the board as a whole-time director on 1 October 2026. Several other senior managers are listed as relatives of directors. A planned hand-over to the second generation is under way: both deputy MDs step back to advisory whole-time director roles on half pay from April 2027 and retire from the board in 2029. The promoter group owns 33.19%.

people.name: J. Lakshmana Rao (Janumahanti Lakshmana Rao)
people.since: Founder (promoted the company in 1985–86); on the current board since August 2008
people.relation: Co-founder; brother of CFO A. Seshu Kumari; brother-in-law of A. Subramanyam; father of Rana Pratap Janumahanti
people.stake: 9.25% (30,73,201 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 33.19%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati, and a postgraduate diploma in management (marketing and finance) from IIM Bangalore. He promoted Mold-Tek in 1985–86, took it public in 1993 and raised money through a QIP in 2021. Over four decades he built it into one of India's largest makers of injection-moulded packaging (paint and lubricant pails, food and FMCG containers, and now pharma packs), and he has always led strategy and business development. He is also Chairman and MD of the group's engineering-services company, Mold-Tek Technologies. He is 67 and was paid ₹3.28 crore in FY26; part of his future pay may come from Mold-Tek Technologies.

people.name: A. Subramanyam (Subrahmanyam Adivishnu)
people.role: Deputy Managing Director (becomes Technical Director from 1 April 2027)
people.since: Co-founder (1986); on the current board since August 2008
people.relation: Co-founder; brother-in-law of J. Lakshmana Rao; husband of CFO A. Seshu Kumari
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from REC Surathkal and a course in mould design and manufacture from CIPET, Chennai. He co-founded Mold-Tek with Lakshmana Rao in 1986. He runs all the plants and the in-house tool room, and heads research and product development. He developed the company's own robots and brought in-mould labelling (IML) with robotics, which the company says was a first in India. He is 72 and was paid ₹3.93 crore in FY26. Under the succession plan he steps down to Technical Director from April 2027 on half pay and leaves the board in March 2029.

people.name: P. Venkateswara Rao (Venkateswara Rao Pattabhi)
people.role: Deputy Managing Director (becomes Commercial Director from 1 April 2027)
people.stake: 0.45% (1,50,126 shares, FY26 annual report); classed as a promoter
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in arts from Osmania University and a diploma in materials management. He has over 44 years of experience in materials management, project execution and coordination, and is in charge of the company's marketing and commercial work, purchasing and legal matters. He is not related to the other directors but is part of the promoter group. He is 69 and was paid ₹2.89 crore in FY26. He moves to a Commercial Director role on half pay from April 2027 and retires from the board in March 2029.

people.name: M. Srinivas (Srinivas Madireddy)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Osmania University, Hyderabad. He has been with Mold-Tek for more than 34 years and manages all its manufacturing plants, covering planning, production, maintenance, delivery and product development. His expertise is plastics processing and engineering. He was paid ₹1.47 crore in FY26.

people.name: A. Seshu Kumari
people.relation: Sister of J. Lakshmana Rao; wife of A. Subramanyam
people.bio: Has over 25 years of experience in finance and accounts. As CFO she is responsible for financial planning and analysis, accounting, treasury and budgets, and also oversees legal and administration. She is a close relative of both founders, so the finance function is not independent of the family. She was paid ₹82.85 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Rana Pratap Janumahanti
people.role: Senior Vice President – Corporate; Director – Marketing & Strategy (whole-time director) from 1 October 2026
people.since: At Mold-Tek for over 14 years; board from 1 October 2026
people.relation: Son of J. Lakshmana Rao
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from IIT Delhi and an MBA in marketing and operations from IIM Lucknow. He has spent more than 14 years at Mold-Tek in business development, strategy and operations. He leads marketing and the pharma packaging division (key accounts, operations, sales and new products) and also oversees food and FMCG. He led the diversification into pharma packs, set up the company's design studio and worked on a tie-up with UK-based Vibe Generation Holdings for specialty caps and closures. He is 39 and is being brought onto the board to represent the next generation of the promoter family.

people.name: A. Durga Sundeep (Sundeep Adivishnu)
people.relation: Listed by the company as a relative of a director (the annual report does not say which)
people.bio: Holds an engineering degree in electronics from NIT and an MBA in finance and operations from Purdue University. He worked for about two years at an IT consulting firm and then in management consulting, project execution and digital transformation. At Mold-Tek he handles MIS, production and material planning, sales forecasting, costing and margin analysis, and checks the viability and costs of new projects.

companies.changes: Announced 26 August 2026: A. Subramanyam and P. Venkateswara Rao step down from Deputy MD to Technical Director and Commercial Director from 1 April 2027, on half pay, and retire from the board in March 2029; Rana Pratap Janumahanti joins the board as Director – Marketing & Strategy from 1 October 2026; C. Vasant Kumar Roy added as an independent director. A 1:1 bonus issue was also proposed. There were no KMP changes during FY26.

companies.styleNote: A Patel family business from Ahmedabad, listed in July 2026. Brothers Alpesh Patel (Chairman and MD) and Rashminbhai Patel (whole-time director) and their cousin Pravinkumar Patel (whole-time director) are the three promoters and hold all the executive board seats. The three promoters own about 43.5% after the IPO and the wider family about 70.6%. The CFO and company secretary are hired professionals. The company's offices, plants and the land for its new plant are leased from the promoters.

people.name: Alpesh Tulsibhai Patel
people.since: Director since March 2013; Chairman & MD since 18 July 2025
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Rashminbhai Patel; cousin of Pravinkumar Patel
people.stake: 16.63% after the IPO (20,354,250 shares, prospectus); promoter group together about 70.6%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in commerce from Gujarat University and a postgraduate diploma in management from Nirma University. He has over 32 years in the packaging industry. He is chairman of the Indian Institute of Packaging (Gujarat), president of the Poly Woven Association of Gujarat, vice president of the Indian Federation of Woven Technical Textiles, and has taken part in Bureau of Indian Standards work for the textile industry. He is also a director of the group's other companies, including Knack Energy, Knack International and ADP Packaging, and of its overseas ventures in South Africa and Mexico. He is 49.

people.name: Rashminbhai Tulsibhai Patel
people.since: Director since March 2013; current five-year term from 18 July 2025
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Alpesh Patel; cousin of Pravinkumar Patel
people.bio: Holds a diploma in mechanical engineering from N. M. Gopani Polytechnic, Ranpur, and a certificate in CNC turning and milling from the Indo-German Tool Room, Ahmedabad, plus short courses in drafting, office automation and programming. He has over 28 years of experience in production and manufacturing and looks after the plants. He is also a director of Knack Energy and of the group's Mexican venture. He is the largest individual shareholder and is 46.

people.name: Pravinkumar Ambalal Patel
people.since: Director since incorporation (March 2013); current five-year term from 18 July 2025
people.relation: Promoter; cousin of Alpesh and Rashminbhai Patel
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in commerce from Gujarat University and has over 32 years of experience in finance and accounts. He was earlier a partner in the firms Mark Plast and Knack Packaging, and was also associated with Knack Packaging when it was a proprietorship firm. He has been a director since the company was incorporated. He is 61.

people.name: Ajay Kumar Dubey
people.bio: A qualified cost and management accountant with bachelor's and master's degrees in commerce from Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Avadh University, a law degree from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, an MBA from Sikkim Manipal University and a PhD in commerce. He has about 18 years of experience. Before Knack he was CFO of Metalman Auto, head of costing, controlling and indirect tax at Beumer India, and held managerial roles at Exicom Tele-Systems and Sunbeam Auto; he began as a cost trainee at Indian Oil. He oversees finance, accounting, costing, budgeting, tax and legal, and was paid ₹53.5 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Ravikumar Ramnarayan Pasi
people.bio: Holds an M.Com and an LL.M and is an associate member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. He has more than 15 years of experience in company secretarial work, regulatory compliance, corporate affairs and treasury. He joined as company secretary a month after the listing.

companies.changes: Company secretary Saloni Hurkat resigned with effect from 24 July 2026, moving to another role in the Knack group; Ravikumar Pasi was appointed company secretary from 9 August 2026. The company listed on 8 July 2026; the promoters sold about 16.5 lakh shares in the IPO and their shares are under lock-in.

companies.styleNote: Founder Ashok Jaipuria is Chairman and MD and controls the company, with about 38.2% registered in his name (most of it held for a family partnership firm) out of a promoter total of 40.78%. Yamini Kumar (Jaipuria), who is classed as a promoter, is a whole-time director, and long-time associate A. K. Jain is director of corporate affairs. Day-to-day businesses are run by a professional Group CEO, Pankaj Poddar, and hired business heads. The annual report says no directors are related to one another. Pay at the top is high: the chairman earned 387 times the median employee in FY26.

people.name: Ashok Jaipuria
people.since: Founder; current term April 2024 to April 2029
people.relation: Founder and promoter
people.stake: 2.07% in his own right plus 36.14% registered in his name for the partnership firm Gayatri and Annapurna, 38.21% in all (FY26 annual report); promoter group together 40.78%
people.bio: A first-generation entrepreneur with over 40 years in business, he founded the company and has led it from a single BOPP film maker into a group spanning packaging films, specialty chemicals, rigid packaging, window and paint-protection films and the Zigly pet-care chain. He holds an Associate of Arts in business administration and a diploma in marketing science. He is an independent director of Hindware Home Innovation and has served on the boards of governors of IIT Indore, IIT Patna and the Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, and on FICCI's executive committee. He was paid about ₹24.4 crore in FY26, 387 times the median employee, and the company lent him ₹10 crore in FY25, since repaid.

people.name: Pankaj Poddar
people.since: Joined February 2011 as CFO; CEO since August 2013
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Shri Ram College of Commerce, a chartered accountant and holder of a diploma in management. Before Cosmo he held senior finance roles at large multinational companies, in finance, advisory and assurance. He joined Cosmo in 2011 as CFO, became President of India operations the same year and CEO in August 2013, and was later made Group CEO over Cosmo Films, Cosmo Speciality Chemicals, Cosmo Plastech, Cosmo Consumer, Zigly and Cosmo Ferrites. The company credits him with the record profits and the move into chemicals, consumer products and pet care. He has won HR and leadership awards including the NIPM 'People's CEO' award (2018).

people.name: Neeraj Jain
people.since: Not disclosed; in the role through FY26
people.bio: A chartered accountant and certified information systems auditor (CISA) with a commerce degree from Delhi University. He has about 25 years of experience at large Indian companies in corporate finance, strategy, mergers and acquisitions, banking and fund-raising, tax, accounting and risk management. As Group CFO he handles the company's debt reduction plan after the ₹1,200 crore capex cycle, and sits on its risk management committee.

people.name: Yamini Kumar (Jaipuria)
people.role: Whole-time Director – Corporate Strategy, ESG & CSR
people.since: Corporate adviser from 2020; whole-time director since 12 February 2025 (term to February 2030)
people.relation: Named in the promoter group; the company discloses no relationship with other directors
people.bio: Holds a master's in international relations from the London School of Economics and an MBA from the American College, London. She spent almost two decades as Vice President, Human Resources for GE in Europe, Asia and India, winning GE India President's awards five times. She advised Cosmo from 2020, reshaping its HR, social media and CSR work, and helped shape the move into pet care through Zigly. She is managing trustee of Cosmo Foundation and Zigly Foundation. She joined the board in February 2025 to lead strategy, ESG and CSR, and was paid 124 times the median employee in FY26.

people.name: A. K. (Anil Kumar) Jain
people.bio: Holds a commerce degree from Meerut University, is a cost accountant (AICWA) and a certified information systems auditor. He has over 40 years in finance, accounts and general management, having earlier worked at Mawana Sugars, A. F. Ferguson & Co. and the National Mineral Development Corporation. As director of corporate affairs he also sits on the boards of the group's subsidiaries in India and overseas, including Zigly Pet Ventures and Cosmo Speciality Chemicals.

people.name: Kulbhushan Malik
people.role: Global Business Head – Cosmo Films (flexible packaging)
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Shri Ram College of Commerce and a chartered accountant, with leadership programmes at Oxford's Saïd Business School (2017) and Thunderbird School of Global Management (2011). He has over 24 years of senior experience in strategy, operations, supply chain, business development, sales and finance. Before Cosmo he worked at MAHLE, Delphi (now Aptiv) and EY. He runs the core films business, which is most of the company's revenue.

people.name: Saurabh Jain
people.role: Business Head – Zigly Pet Care & Head, Corporate Development
people.bio: Holds a mechanical engineering degree from Delhi College of Engineering and an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies, Delhi. He has 16+ years in packaging films, investment banking and corporate strategy. He was previously Global CEO (overseas business) at Jindal Films and held roles at SB Packaging, Wodehouse Capital, Religare Capital Markets and Jaypee Capital. He runs Zigly, which plans to raise outside capital, and corporate development.

companies.changes: No change in KMP during FY26. Yamini Kumar retired by rotation and sought re-appointment at the 5 August 2026 AGM. VP – Information Technology Anurag Choubey left on 14 May 2026. Other business heads: Piyush Gupta (specialty chemicals), Himanshu Gupta (rigid packaging), Abhineesh Das (Sunshield and paint-protection film); company secretary Jyoti Dixit.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Somany (Hindware) group. Sandip Somany is Chairman and MD and the only executive director; his wife Sumita Somany is a non-executive director, and their son Shashvat, now head of strategy, has been proposed as Joint MD from 1 October 2026. Promoters own 60.39%, mostly through the family company Somany Impresa (50.84%). Day-to-day operations are run by a hired CEO, Rajesh Khosla, and a professional finance team. The company rents to and trades with promoter company Hindware.

people.name: Sandip Somany
people.since: On the board since September 1995; re-appointed CMD for December 2026 to November 2031
people.relation: Promoter; husband of director Sumita Somany; father of Shashvat Somany
people.stake: 8.72% (56,47,731 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 60.39%, including 50.84% through Somany Impresa
people.bio: A commerce graduate with a diploma in ceramic manufacturing technology from the US, he has over four decades in the ceramics and glass industry. He is a past president of FICCI, of the International Chamber of Commerce's India chapter and of the PHD Chamber of Commerce, and chairs the Indian Council of Sanitaryware Manufacturers. He is also a director of the group's listed Hindware Home Innovation and of JK Paper, HEG and Indraprastha Medical Corporation, so AGI is one of several demands on his time. He was paid ₹13.66 crore in FY25, and shareholders approved pay of up to 5% of net profit for his new term; in FY26 his pay was 137 times the median employee.

people.name: Shashvat Somany
people.role: Head of Strategy (Vice President); proposed Director and Joint Managing Director from 1 October 2026
people.since: Senior management; board appointment put to the 22 September 2026 AGM
people.relation: Son of Sandip and Sumita Somany
people.bio: Holds an MBA in technology and analytics from London Business School and a BA in economics and psychology from UCLA. Before joining AGI he worked in consulting for consumer appliance, FMCG and telecom clients. As head of strategy he shapes long-term direction, growth and innovation, and he founded Tattva, the company's corporate venture capital arm. He is a past chairman of the PHD Chamber's economic affairs committee and a director of Hindware Limited. He is 31, was paid ₹3.38 crore a year as head of strategy, and the proposal would let him earn up to 3% of net profit as Joint MD.

people.name: Rajesh Khosla
people.since: CEO and key managerial person since 2 May 2024
people.bio: Became CEO of AGI Greenpac on 2 May 2024 and is the most senior professional manager, running operations across the glass, PET and closures businesses and the new aluminium-cans project. Before that he ran the glass business as President and CEO of AGI Glaspac. The company does not publish his education or earlier career. He was paid 151 times the median employee in FY26, more than the chairman, and he had a loan from the company outstanding at March 2026.

people.name: Sandeep Sikka
people.since: Not disclosed (listed as senior management in FY25 and FY26)
people.bio: Named by the company as Group CFO and a member of senior management, and sits on the board's risk management committee. He oversees group finance, including the funding of the aluminium-cans plant and the FY26 prepayment of ₹193 crore of term loans. The company does not publish his education or earlier career.

people.name: Om Prakash Pandey
people.since: Not disclosed; KMP through FY25 and FY26
people.bio: The statutory CFO who signs the accounts, alongside Group CFO Sandeep Sikka. He was paid about 47 times the median employee in FY26. He has borrowed from the company in the past; the loan appears in the related-party notes. The company does not publish his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: Sandip Somany re-appointed CMD for five years from 1 December 2026 (postal ballot, June 2026). Shashvat Somany proposed as Director and Joint MD from 1 October 2026 at the 22 September 2026 AGM. Chandan Kumar Jha joined as CEO of the Plastek division (29 January 2026) and Dushyant Kumar as COO of the cans business (1 February 2026); Abhijeet Srivastava became VP, CMD Office, from 1 May 2026 after Nitesh Raj left that role in August 2025. Ram Babu Kabra joined as a non-executive director (April 2026) and Sushil Kumar Roongta as an independent director (July 2026). The company has held no public earnings call since January 2026.

companies.styleNote: The Indian subsidiary of Finland's Huhtamaki group, which owns 67.73%. There is no family; the business is run by managers appointed from the group. The board is chaired by an independent director, Murali Sivaraman, and the parent's nominees (Axel Glade and Thomas Geust) sit as non-executive directors. The whole executive team is new: the MD, CFO and company secretary all changed between January and August 2026, and both whole-time directors joined the board in March 2026. No director is related to another.

people.name: Kamal Taneja
people.bio: An Indian-born Australian citizen with a B.E. (Hons) in mechanical engineering and an M.Sc. (Hons) in economics from BITS Pilani. From October 2017 to June 2023 he was Global Managing Director at Essentra group companies in the UK and Singapore, and before that held senior management roles at Amcor Specialty Cartons and Ingersoll Rand in Singapore. He has also been a non-executive director at several companies around the world. The company describes him as a turnaround specialist focused on operations and innovation. He replaced Dhananjay Salunkhe, who resigned in October 2025 and left on 15 January 2026.

people.name: Amit Gupta
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a B.Com (Hons) from Delhi University and over two decades of industry experience. He has led finance teams across Asia, the Middle East and Africa at US, European and Asian multinationals in FMCG, pharma, consulting and consumer health, including Procter & Gamble Health, Merck, Sanofi India, Colgate-Palmolive India and ITC (in India and Singapore). He is the third person in the CFO seat since December 2025: long-time Executive Director and CFO Jagdish Agarwal left on 1 December 2025, and finance controller Anil Kaul held the post from February to April 2026 until Gupta joined.

people.name: Ramya Mohan
people.since: Board from 18 March 2026 (term to March 2029); with Huhtamaki since September 2021
people.bio: A lawyer and company secretary with more than 27 years of experience. She spent the first 13 years of her career at law firms and then about 10 years at Mondelez in various roles. She joined Huhtamaki in September 2021 as General Counsel and Vice President for Asia-Pacific. Her work covers domestic and cross-border M&A, corporate strategy, restructuring and compliance. She joined the Indian board as a whole-time director in March 2026.

people.name: Vinit Mahadevan
people.bio: Holds an MBA from IIM Bangalore and a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Mumbai, and completed INSEAD's strategic leadership programme. He is Vice President – Special Projects at Huhtamaki. He earlier held senior roles at Diageo, WNS, Accenture, Britannia Industries and Citigroup, working on corporate strategy, M&A and business transformation.

people.name: Nitin Mittal
people.role: Head of Sales – Regional Key Accounts & Field Sales
people.bio: A chemical engineer with about 25 years of leadership experience. His last job was Country Manager – South Asia (Graphics) at Avery Dennison, and he earlier worked at Huntsman, Deltech and Dow Chemicals, serving FMCG, consumer goods, retail, auto and industrial customers.

people.name: Akanksha Kandoi
people.bio: A qualified company secretary (fellow member of ICSI) with more than 23 years in corporate governance, secretarial, compliance and regulatory work, covering the Companies Act, SEBI rules and FEMA. She has led secretarial and compliance functions at large regulated and multinational companies. She replaced Abhijaat Sinha, who left on 10 June 2026.

companies.changes: A lot of turnover in a year: Executive Director & CFO Jagdish Agarwal resigned (left 1 December 2025); MD Dhananjay Salunkhe resigned (left 15 January 2026) and Kamal Taneja took over on 16 January 2026; Anil Kaul was interim CFO from 27 February to 27 April 2026, then Amit Gupta became CFO; Head of Operations Himanshu Desai left on 8 May 2026; company secretary Abhijaat Sinha left on 10 June 2026 and Akanksha Kandoi joined on 24 August 2026; Head of Sales (global key accounts) Saurabh Kothari left in December 2025. Parent-group directors also changed (Stefan Lotz and Sami Pauni out; Axel Glade and Thomas Geust in).

companies.styleNote: A tightly held Agarwal family company from Mumbai. Bijaykumar Agarwal is Chairman and MD; his son Jaiprakash is whole-time director and also the CFO; and Jaiprakash's wife Madhu is a whole-time director. There are no hired senior executives apart from the company secretary. Promoters own 74.94%, the most allowed for a listed company, including 27.57% through Yash Synthetics LLP and 9.50% through Credence Financial Consultancy LLP.

people.name: Bijaykumar Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; father of Jaiprakash Agarwal and father-in-law of Madhu Agarwal
people.stake: 6.91% (25,41,120 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 74.94%
people.bio: Has more than three decades of experience in the packaging industry and has been with Pyramid since 2002. He provides strategic leadership and oversees finance, raw material buying, customer service and business development. The company does not disclose his education.

people.name: Jaiprakash Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Bijaykumar Agarwal; husband of Madhu Agarwal
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in commerce from Mumbai University and an MBA from ICFAI University, Dehradun. He has over 20 years in the packaging industry and has been a director since June 2003. He looks after manufacturing, finance and accounts, sales and marketing and business development, and doubles as CFO, so there is no independent finance head. He is 43 and was re-appointed on retirement by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Madhu Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; wife of Jaiprakash Agarwal; daughter-in-law of Bijaykumar Agarwal
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in commerce from Calcutta University. She has been with the company since May 2006 and has about 18 years of experience in human resources, compliance and administration, which she heads at Pyramid.

companies.changes: The company secretary post changed three times in a year: Puja Sharma resigned in November 2025, Pramod Yadav served from 10 February to 25 March 2026, and Chandrika Khatri was appointed from 22 June 2026. No change in the executive directors.

companies.styleNote: An Agarwal family company from Kanpur. Manoj Agarwal is Chairman and MD, his son Shashank is Deputy MD, and his wife Usha Agarwal is a non-executive director. A long-serving professional, Sunil Mehta, is executive director for manufacturing. Promoters own about 68% through family members, family trusts and family companies, and have been adding shares through warrant conversions. In FY26 the company bought 76% of Valex Ventures, a UK distributor, from the chairman himself, paid for in new shares.

people.name: Manoj Agarwal
people.since: Leading the company for over 45 years; re-appointed for three years from 1 September 2026
people.relation: Promoter; husband of Usha Agarwal; father of Shashank Agarwal
people.stake: 11.66% (28,53,484 shares incl. warrant conversions, FY26 annual report); promoter group about 68%
people.bio: Holds a master's degree in management studies from BITS Pilani and has run the company for more than 45 years, with a background in operations, administration and export marketing. He is a former chairman of the Plastics Export Promotion Council and still sits on its committee of administration, and a former president of the TiE UP chapter. He sold his controlling stake in UK distributor Valex Ventures to the company in FY26 for new shares. He was paid ₹1.93 crore in FY26.

people.name: Shashank Agarwal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Manoj and Usha Agarwal
people.stake: 9.03% (22,11,346 shares incl. warrant conversions, FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Holds a B.Eng. (Hons) in manufacturing engineering and operations management from the University of Nottingham, UK. He has helped run the company for more than 15 years and led backward integration, new product lines and sustainability work. He chairs the board's CSR committee. His pay terms were changed at the 2026 AGM, and he was paid about ₹1 crore in FY26.

people.name: Sunil Mehta
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in textile technology from TIT Bhiwani and has more than 35 years of experience in the woven sacks industry. He joined Kanpur Plastipack in 2002 as vice president and has overseen the expansion of manufacturing across several locations. He is the only non-family executive on the board; shareholders last re-appointed him as executive director in September 2024.

people.name: Shobhit Agarwal
people.bio: Became CFO and a key managerial person on 10 June 2024. The annual report does not give his qualifications or earlier career, or say whether he is related to the promoter family.

companies.changes: Manoj Agarwal re-appointed as Chairman & MD for three years from 1 September 2026, and Shashank Agarwal's pay terms revised, at the 2026 AGM. Independent director Akshay Kumar Gupta retired on 31 March 2026; Basant Seth joined as independent director on 10 November 2025. Company secretary is Ankur Srivastava.

companies.styleNote: Co-founder Arvind Singhania stepped back from Chairman & CEO to non-executive chairman on 26 March 2026, and a hired CEO, Vaibhav Jha, now runs the business. The family stays close to the top: his son Ayush Vardhan Singhania is a whole-time director. Promoters own 62.71%, almost all through group companies, chiefly Wilemina Finance Corporation (50.54%) and MOVI Limited (7.90%); Arvind Singhania no longer holds shares in his own name. Company loans carry his personal guarantee, and he has waived his dividend.

people.name: Vaibhav Jha
people.since: Deputy CEO first; CEO since 27 March 2026
people.bio: Holds an MBA from IIT Bombay and a B.E. from Nagpur University, and has over 21 years of experience across functions, industries and countries, including running multicultural joint ventures. Before Ester he worked at Infosys Technologies, GEP Worldwide and Reliance Industries. He joined Ester as Deputy CEO and was promoted to CEO when the founder stepped back in March 2026. He now leads the business through a period of heavy debt and the ELITe recycling joint venture build-out.

people.name: Ayush Vardhan Singhania
people.since: On the board since 1 June 2021; current term from 1 June 2024
people.relation: Son of Chairman and co-founder Arvind Singhania
people.stake: 0.96% (9,34,318 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 62.71%
people.bio: A graduate of Bentley University with an MBA from IE Business School, Madrid. He was earlier Head of Business Development and Marketing at Ester and has worked in business development, marketing, strategic planning and expansion. He has been a whole-time director since June 2021 and is 39. He raised his direct stake during FY26 and was up for re-appointment by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Pradeep Kumar Rustagi
people.stake: 400 shares (FY26 annual report), a negligible stake
people.bio: Has more than 38 years of experience in leadership roles covering financial planning, accounts, budgeting and MIS, dealing with banks and financial institutions, and statutory compliance. As Executive Director – Corporate Affairs he is part of the company's central leadership team with the chairman, CEO and CFO, and certifies the company's CSR spending. He is not related to any director.

people.name: Sourabh Agarwal
people.bio: The company's CFO and a key managerial person, and a member of its central leadership team. He handles a stretched balance sheet: gross debt of about ₹722 crore, euro loans that caused currency losses in FY26, and funding for the ELITe joint venture. The annual report does not give his qualifications or earlier career.

companies.changes: Arvind Singhania moved from Managing Director (Chairman & CEO) to non-executive Chairman on 26 March 2026 (approved by postal ballot on 23 May 2026), shortly after being re-appointed as MD from 1 April 2026. Deputy CEO Vaibhav Jha became CEO on 27 March 2026. Pradeep Kumar Rustagi re-appointed as whole-time director from 1 April 2026. Non-executive director Archana Singhania resigned in April 2025 and independent director Alok Dhir in August 2025. Company secretary is Poornima Gupta.

companies.styleNote: Founder Mark Saldanha is Chairman, Managing Director and CEO; his wife Sandra Saldanha is a whole-time director. Promoters own 43.9%, almost all of it held by Mark Saldanha. PE investor OrbiMed holds 8.6% and has a board seat.

people.name: Mark Saldanha
people.relation: Founder and promoter; husband of Sandra Saldanha
people.bio: Mark Saldanha is a science graduate and the founder promoter of Marksans. Before Marksans he was a whole-time director of Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, the company founded by his father Gracias Saldanha; Marksans began in 2001 as a Glenmark subsidiary and was spun off as a separate company in 2003. He has worked across R&D, marketing, production and finance, and built the business through acquisitions: Bell, Sons & Co. and Relonchem in the UK, Time-Cap Labs in the US and Nova in Australia. In FY26 he also drew about ₹1.3cr from the US subsidiary Time-Cap, on top of his pay from the listed company.

people.name: Sandra Saldanha
people.since: Whole-time director; re-appointed at the August 2026 AGM
people.relation: Wife of Mark Saldanha
people.bio: Sandra Saldanha holds a master's degree in arts (Sociology). Her areas at Marksans are human resources, business development, projects and supply chain. She is a director of the main overseas subsidiaries, including Marksans Pharma (UK), Relonchem, Bell, Sons & Co. and Time-Cap Laboratories in the US. Shareholders re-appointed her as a whole-time director at the 27 August 2026 AGM.

people.name: Varddhman V. Jain
people.bio: Varddhman Jain has an M.Pharm and about 27 years in the pharmaceutical industry. He has worked across manufacturing, quality, research and development, compliance and regulatory affairs for both active ingredients and finished medicines. He has handled inspections by the US FDA, the UK MHRA, Japan's PMDA and the WHO. He chairs the company's CSR committee.

people.name: Jitendra Sharma
people.bio: Jitendra Sharma has been Marksans's chief financial officer since September 2002, almost from the start of the company. He is also a director of several overseas subsidiaries, including Marksans Pharma UK (since 2008), Bell, Sons & Co. (since 2017), Relonchem, Nova Pharmaceuticals Australasia and Marksans Pharma Inc. There was no change in the company's key managerial personnel during FY26.

companies.changes: No change in key managerial personnel in FY26. Other senior leaders named in the FY26 annual report: David Mohammed (MD, Australia), Sathish Kumar (MD, UK) and Anjani Kumar (COO, US).

companies.styleNote: The Patel family controls Zydus through the Zydus Family Trust (about 75%). Chairman Pankaj Patel is non-executive; his son Dr Sharvil Patel is Managing Director and runs the company, with a deep bench of hired professionals below him.

people.name: Dr. Sharvil P. Patel
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Pankaj R. Patel
people.stake: 14,775 shares in his own name (FY26 annual report); family, mainly through the Zydus Family Trust, about 75%
people.bio: Dr Sharvil Patel has a bachelor's degree in chemical and pharmaceutical sciences and a doctorate focused on breast cancer research. He has nearly 30 years of leadership experience in the group and has driven its shift to specialty medicines, new molecules and overseas expansion. He is President of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance, the lobby group of large Indian drug makers, and Honorary Consul of Belgium. He is also an independent director of Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation. BioSpectrum named him Businessperson of the Year 2025.

people.name: Ganesh N. Nayak
people.bio: Ganesh Nayak holds a B.Sc. and an MBA from Newport University, and attended the General Management Programme at Harvard Business School. He has been with the Zydus group since 1977, over 48 years in pharma. He has led the group's joint ventures and global alliances and worked on its sales, marketing and M&A. He stopped being a key managerial person in July 2025 but was re-appointed a director in employment for five years to July 2030. He is an independent director of Zydus Wellness.

people.name: Tushar D. Shroff
people.bio: Tushar Shroff is a Chartered Accountant and Cost Accountant with over 29 years of experience, 20 of them in pharma. He worked at ABB, Piramal Healthcare and Intas Pharmaceuticals, and at Zydus itself from December 2010 to January 2019. Just before rejoining he was CFO of Sterlite Technologies. He rejoined as President-Finance in April 2025 and became CFO on 1 September 2025, when Nitin Parekh retired.

people.name: Swati Dalal
people.bio: Swati Dalal has a pharmacy degree from PKM Kundnani College of Pharmacy and a management degree from JBIMS, Mumbai. She has over 30 years in pharma, starting at Wockhardt Nutrition and moving through Boots, Knoll, Solvay and Abbott. At Abbott she ran Abbott Nutrition and Abbott Primary Care, then was Managing Director of Abbott India until June 2025. She now runs Zydus Healthcare, the subsidiary that holds the Indian branded-medicines business.

companies.changes: CFO Nitin Parekh retired on 31 August 2025 and now heads special projects; Tushar Shroff took over as CFO. Harish Sadana moved from MD of Zydus Healthcare to President-Corporate Matters. Samir Desai (Biologics) died in August 2025. Mayank Satpal left senior management in March 2026 in a reorganisation. At Zydus Wellness, the head of sales and the CMO resigned in July and September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder C. C. Paarthipan is non-executive Chairman. His sons Ashok and Vivek Partheeban became non-executive Vice-Chairmen in November 2025; Vivek had been COO until then. Day-to-day running is by a hired MD, Dr Sridhar Ganesan. The promoter group owns about 70.6%.

people.name: Dr. Sridhar Ganesan
people.since: On the board since 2014; re-appointed MD to August 2028
people.bio: Dr Sridhar Ganesan, 71, holds an MS in Pharmaceuticals and a doctorate in homeopathic medicine, and has more than 42 years in the pharma industry. He has worked in profit-centre management, global marketing, new plant projects, production, product development, quality assurance and factory management. Before Caplin he held several international roles, with a focus on South Asia, the Middle East and Africa. India's pharma export council (Pharmexcil) has named him an 'Honorary Expert'. He joined the board in February 2014 and was re-appointed MD for two years from 25 August 2026.

people.name: D. Muralidharan
people.since: CFO since February 2016; whole-time director since August 2026
people.bio: D. Muralidharan, 70, is a commerce graduate, a qualified company secretary (ACS) and a cost and management accountant (CMA). He has over four decades in finance; his job before Caplin was at Merck Specialities. He has been CFO since 19 February 2016 and sits on the risk management committee. The board made him a whole-time director from 12 August 2026 for two years; shareholders voted on this at the September 2026 AGM.

companies.changes: Vivek Partheeban gave up the COO role on 5 November 2025 when he and his brother Ashok became non-executive Vice-Chairmen. CFO D. Muralidharan joined the board as whole-time director on 12 August 2026. Three senior managers left in April–July 2025: the chief transformation & digital officer, the SVP of formulation R&D and the VP of corporate affairs.

companies.styleNote: Founder Satish Mehta is MD & CEO and becomes Chairman from the 21 September 2026 AGM. His daughter Namita Thapar and son Samit Mehta are whole-time directors, and Namita's husband Vikas Thapar heads corporate development. Co-promoter Sunil Mehta (not related, per the annual report) is also a whole-time director.

people.name: Satish Mehta
people.role: Managing Director & CEO; Chairman from the September 2026 AGM
people.relation: Founder; father of Namita Thapar and Samit Mehta
people.stake: 39.77% (FY26 annual report); with Samit and Namita 49.6%
people.bio: Satish Mehta founded Emcure in 1981 and has run it ever since. He holds a postgraduate degree in chemistry from Pune University and a PGDM from IIM Ahmedabad. Under him Emcure grew into a company selling in more than 80 countries, with its own plants, research and biotech arm (Gennova). He has also served on government and policy advisory committees. The board made him Chairman from 21 September 2026, when Berjis Desai stepped down; he keeps the MD & CEO roles.

people.name: Namita Thapar
people.relation: Daughter of Satish Mehta; wife of Vikas Thapar
people.bio: Namita Thapar is a Chartered Accountant with an MBA from Duke University's Fuqua School of Business. Before Emcure she worked at Guidant Corporation in the US.
