The only executive director is a hired MD & CEO, Arnab Banerjee, a CEAT employee since 2005.

people.name: Arnab Banerjee
people.since: Joined 2005; COO 2018; MD & CEO since April 2021, re-appointed to March 2028
people.bio: An engineer from IIT Kharagpur with an MBA from IIM Calcutta; he also attended Harvard Business School's Advanced Management Program and is a certified coach. Before CEAT he worked at Marico and Berger Paints. He joined CEAT in 2005 as Vice President, Sales and Marketing, became Chief Operating Officer in 2018 and took over as MD & CEO in April 2021. He has more than 30 years of experience in consumer and manufacturing businesses. The board re-appointed him from 1 April 2026 for two more years, to 31 March 2028.

people.name: Kumar Subbiah
people.bio: A commerce graduate from the University of Madras and a qualified cost accountant who also studied with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. Before CEAT he worked at Hindustan Unilever and Unilever in finance and commercial roles in India and Asia. He joined CEAT in 2015 as a Senior Vice President and became CFO in January 2017. He was named one of the leading CFOs at the CFO Excellence Awards in 2022 for capital allocation and business partnering.

people.name: Amit Tolani
people.since: Joined 2004; CEAT Specialty head since 1 June 2021
people.bio: A CEAT employee since 2004 who has worked across sales, marketing and supply chain. He became Vice President, Marketing in 2019 and was Chief Marketing Officer before taking charge of CEAT Specialty, the farm, off-highway and industrial tyre business, on 1 June 2021. He leads the business's push into Europe and the Ambernath farm radial plant expansion.

people.name: Lakshminarayanan B
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Sardar Patel College of Engineering with an MBA from NMIMS. He had about 18 years in sales and marketing when he joined, most recently as Head of Marketing at Asian Paints, and earlier worked at Samsung India Electronics. At CEAT he runs marketing for car, two-wheeler, truck and bus tyres across markets.

companies.changes: Arnab Banerjee was re-appointed MD & CEO from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028. SVP-HR Somraj Samin Roy resigned in January 2026 and Rahul Gama replaced him. Other senior managers named in the FY26 report: Jayasankar Kuruppal (SVP Manufacturing), Jignesh Sharda (SVP Quality & Sustainability), Kunjan Chikhlikar (VP Strategy), Renji Issac (SVP R&D), Vishal Pawar (SVP Global Sales & Supply Chain) and Gaurav Tongia (Company Secretary). No KMP changes announced since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Singhania family's JK Organisation. The promoter group owns about 51.7% (Bengal & Assam Company 45.43% plus 51 group entities with 6.29%). Dr Raghupati Singhania, 79, has been MD since 1975 and is Chairman & MD; the board has re-appointed him for five more years from 1 October 2026. Anshuman Singhania, also of the promoter family, is MD/CEO. Raghupati's brother Bharat Hari Singhania and his wife Sunanda Singhania sit as non-executive directors. The CMD and MD were each paid ₹30cr of commission for FY26 on top of salary.

people.name: Dr Raghupati Singhania
people.since: Board since May 1967; MD since 1975; re-appointed for five years from 1 October 2026
people.relation: Promoter; brother of director Bharat Hari Singhania; husband of director Sunanda Singhania
people.stake: 0.57% (16,44,117 shares, FY26 AGM notice); promoter group together about 51.7%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in science and has about 59 years of experience running group businesses in tyres, power-transmission belts, oil seals, hybrid seeds and steel. He has been on JK Tyre's board since 1967 and MD since 1975, and took the company from a 5 lakh-tyre plant in Rajasthan in 1977 to one of the world's top 20 tyre makers, including the Tornel (Mexico) and Cavendish (Birla Tyres) acquisitions. He is a past Chairman of the Automotive Tyre Manufacturers' Association and past President of the PHD Chamber, was inducted into the US Tyre Industry Association Hall of Fame in 2015 and received Mexico's Order of the Aztec Eagle. He also sits on the boards of JK Lakshmi Cement, Bengal & Assam Company and JK Agri Genetics, and chairs J.K. Fenner (India). He was paid about ₹43.6cr for FY26 including commission.

people.name: Anshuman Singhania
people.since: Joined January 2007; Whole-time Director March 2016; MD since 21 October 2020
people.relation: Member of the Singhania promoter family; the company's filings do not state his exact link to the Chairman
people.stake: Not disclosed in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Holds a BBA (Honours) in business and management from Oxford Brookes University, UK, and a postgraduate degree in marketing from the International Management Institute, New Delhi; he also completed London Business School's Emerging Leaders Programme. He joined JK Tyre as an executive on 1 January 2007, starting on the shop floor as an apprentice, and worked in planning, production, product development, quality, purchase, finance and sales and marketing. He became Vice President (Operations), joined the board as a whole-time director in March 2016 and has been MD since October 2020. He was paid about ₹39cr for FY26 including commission.

people.name: Dr Arun K. Bajoria
people.since: Joined 1997; President since 2003; Whole-time Director since January 2010
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from BITS Pilani with a diploma in advanced management from London Business School and a Wharton certificate course on mergers and acquisitions. He has decades of experience running manufacturing companies, including 32 years with the Birla Group. He joined JK in 1997 when it bought Vikrant Tyres and is credited with turning that business around. He became President in 2003 and a whole-time director in 2010, and led the 2008 purchase of Tornel in Mexico and the 2016 purchase of Birla Tyres' Laksar plant at Haridwar. He now runs the international business.

people.name: Dr Mandar Vighnahari Deo
people.bio: Aged 50, he holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Pune University, a master's and a PhD from Pennsylvania State University, and an MBA from Indiana University's Kelley School of Business. His last job was MD & CEO of Exide Energy Solutions, Exide Industries' lithium-ion cell subsidiary, where he helped set up India's first lithium-ion cell plant (over ₹6,000cr of investment). Before that he spent about 20 years at Cummins India and Cummins Inc., running P&Ls, plants, technical centres and sales, including roles in the USA, and was a board director of Cummins Generator Technologies.

people.name: Sanjeev Aggarwal
people.bio: A rank-holding chartered accountant (1990) with over 35 years in finance, accounts, tax, legal and commercial work, including equity, debt and structured finance. Before JK Tyre he was CFO of Penna Cement Industries. He was named among the 'Most Influential CFOs of India' by CIMA in 2016.

companies.changes: Mandar Deo joined as President – India on 14 April 2026. The board re-appointed Raghupati Singhania as CMD for five years from 1 October 2026, subject to the August 2026 AGM. Independent director Shreekant Somany's term ended in March 2026; Nand Gopal Khaitan joined as an independent director in February 2026. Other senior managers named in the report: V.K. Misra (Technical Director), Dr Arun Jaura (CTO), Srinivasu Allaphan (Sales & Marketing Director), A.K. Makkar (Group Chief Sustainability Officer) and Kamal Kumar Manik (Company Secretary).

companies.styleNote: The Indian management bought the business out in 2005 and those managers are now the promoters. Rajiv Mittal, who set up WABAG's India unit in 1996, is Chairman and MD, and long-time colleague S. Varadarajan is a whole-time director; the annual report says no directors are related. Promoters own only 19.08% (Mittal 15.57%, Varadarajan 3.51%); Rekha Jhunjhunwala holds 8.02%. Mittal's son Rohan was made a key managerial person in 2026, and a hired Deputy MD, Bhupesh Nagineni, joined in May 2026 as part of what the company calls its succession plan.

people.name: Rajiv Mittal
people.since: Set up WABAG's India business in 1996; MD & Group CEO from 2014; Chairman since 2022
people.relation: Promoter; father of Rohan Mittal
people.bio: A chemical engineer from the University of Mumbai's Department of Chemical Technology (UDCT) with over four decades in the water industry. He started at Dorr Oliver and then worked at John Brown Engineering in Glasgow before joining WABAG UK, which sent him to India in 1996 to set up a water business unit. He led the 2005 management buyout, the 2007 reverse acquisition of the former Austrian parent and the 2010 listing. He is a Fellow of the International Water Association and has won several industry awards, including GWI's list of the world's 20 most transformative water leaders (2021).

people.name: S. Varadarajan
people.relation: Promoter; not related to other directors
people.bio: A commerce graduate with a postgraduate degree in public administration, and an associate member of both the cost accountants' and company secretaries' institutes, with over 40 years of experience. He joined in 1997 as Senior Manager – Finance and Company Secretary and later served as CFO, overseeing finance, HR, IT, treasury and legal. He took part in the demerger, the 2005 management buyout, the 2007 reverse acquisition of the Austrian parent and the 2010 listing, and once ran the O&M business. As Chief Growth Officer he works on people strategy across regions and heads the capital projects business. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Bhupesh Chowdary Nagineni
people.bio: An industrial and production engineering graduate from Shivaji University with a postgraduate business degree from Annamalai University, and over three decades in infrastructure, energy, mining, steel, ports and logistics. He was most recently Executive Vice President and Chief of Operations for the energy and industrial business at Tata Projects, and before that President – International Business and an executive council member at the Kalpataru Group. He has also held senior roles at Khimji Ramdas, the Adani Group, Larsen & Toubro, JSW and McNally Bharat Engineering. He joined as Deputy MD in May 2026 under the company's succession plan.

people.name: Rohan Mittal
people.since: About eight years at WABAG; KMP since 21 May 2026; current title from 1 September 2026
people.relation: Son of the Chairman Rajiv Mittal
people.bio: A chemical engineering graduate (B.Tech) from Alagappa College of Technology, with certificates from Stanford Graduate School of Business and Michigan State University. He has worked at WABAG for about eight years in projects, sales and strategy, including the Koyambedu recycling plant and winning the 400 MLD Perur desalination project in India. Since FY24 he has led business growth in the Gulf, where the company has won projects such as Yanbu, Al-Haer and Hadda in Saudi Arabia and Doha in Kuwait. He was made a key managerial person in May 2026 and Chief Commercial & Development Officer for the Middle East and Africa from September 2026; shareholders are asked to approve pay of up to ₹1.5cr a year.

people.name: Skandaprasad Seetharaman
people.since: not disclosed in the annual report
people.bio: He is the group CFO and a key managerial person, and signs the financial statements with the Chairman. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: Bhupesh Chowdary Nagineni joined as Deputy MD and Rohan Mittal was made a KMP on 21 May 2026; Rohan Mittal was re-designated Chief Commercial & Development Officer – MEA from 1 September 2026. Samaresh Parida joined as an independent director in June 2026. Other senior managers: Shailesh Kumar (CEO – India Cluster), Mahmut Gedek (CEO – Europe Cluster) and V. Arulmozhi (CFO – India Cluster).

companies.styleNote: The promoter group (the Sharma and Patni families and their companies) owns 25.43%. Promoter Rajesh Sharma, with the company since 1974, is Executive Chairman, but since October 2024 day-to-day running has been with a hired MD & CEO, Indraneel Dutt (ex-GE and Danaher). Rajesh Sharma's brother Dinesh Sharma and Aankur Patni (son of director M.P. Patni) stepped back from executive roles in October 2024 and are now non-executive Vice-Chairmen, though each is paid about ₹3.2cr a year as an adviser.

people.name: Rajesh Sharma
people.since: Joined January 1974; Chairman & MD until September 2024; Executive Chairman since 1 October 2024
people.relation: Promoter group; brother of Vice-Chairman Dinesh Sharma
people.stake: 5.65% (NSE shareholding pattern, June 2026); promoter group together 25.43%
people.bio: He joined Ion Exchange in January 1974 and, over a 50-year career there, held roles in marketing and exports and served as Vice Chairman & MD and then Chairman & MD. He led the company's expansion abroad and its global partnerships. He handed the MD role to Indraneel Dutt in October 2024 and stayed on as Executive Chairman, with FY26 pay of about ₹7.1cr. He chairs the CII National Committee on Water. The company does not disclose his education.

people.name: Indraneel Dutt
people.since: CEO since 11 September 2023; MD since 1 October 2024
people.bio: A mechanical engineering graduate from Jadavpur University with a management programme (PGDM) from IIM Calcutta, and about 30 years in energy, renewables, water and environment. He started at L&T and the Tata Group, then spent 20 years at General Electric (1999–2018) leading several GE businesses in South Asia. Before Ion Exchange he ran Danaher's water businesses (including HACH, Trojan UV, Pall Water and ChemTreat) in South Asia. He joined as CEO in September 2023 and became MD in October 2024; he runs the company and its 22 subsidiaries across 23 countries. FY26 pay was about ₹4.7cr.

people.name: Vasant J. Naik
people.since: With the company since 2002; Group CFO since 3 February 2023
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Mumbai University and a chartered accountant since 1990, with over 33 years in finance, banking, tax, general management, strategy and M&A in manufacturing and services. He has been with Ion Exchange since 2002 and took over as Group CFO in February 2023 when Nandkumar Ranadive retired.

companies.changes: No executive changes filed since the annual report. Company Secretary is Nikisha Solanki (appointed March 2025). The annual report lists about 15 other senior managers (presidents and executive vice-presidents for projects, services, manufacturing, HR and the product divisions).

companies.styleNote: Run by two founder brothers and their wives: Sanjay Jain is Chairman and whole-time director, Manish Jain is MD, and their wives Ritu Jain and Shachi Jain are whole-time directors; Ritu Jain's brother Piyush Jain is COO. Promoters own 70.19%. A governance flag: shareholders voted down Sanjay Jain's re-appointment at the August 2025 AGM; the board then re-appointed him and added both wives as whole-time directors, and all three were approved by postal ballot in October 2025.

people.name: Sanjay Jain
people.since: Co-founder, with the company since incorporation in June 2009; re-appointed 3 October 2025
people.relation: Promoter; brother of MD Manish Jain; husband of Ritu Jain
people.bio: Aged 53, a chemical engineering graduate (B.Tech) with about 30 years of experience; before the company his last employer was M/s Enviro Engineers. He has been with the company since it was set up in 2009 and leads it as Chairman, covering operations, strategy, finance and governance. His re-appointment failed to win shareholder approval at the August 2025 AGM, so he briefly left the post before being re-appointed through a postal ballot on 3 October 2025. FY26 pay was ₹80 lakh.

people.name: Manish Jain
people.since: Co-founder, on the board since 19 June 2009
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Chairman Sanjay Jain; husband of Shachi Jain
people.bio: Aged 50, a chemical engineering graduate from Punjab University with over 27 years in water and wastewater treatment, earlier at M/s Enviro Engineers. He runs operations, finance, legal and project execution from bidding to completion. Under him the company has moved beyond sewage and water plants into solar and wind power. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM; FY26 pay was ₹80 lakh.

people.name: Ritu Jain
people.since: Non-executive director earlier; Whole-time Director since 29 August 2025
people.relation: Promoter; wife of Chairman Sanjay Jain; sister of COO Piyush Jain
people.bio: Aged 53, she holds a master's degree in science (home science). She was a non-executive director and became a whole-time director in August 2025, confirmed by shareholders in October 2025. The company gives no further detail of her specific responsibilities.

people.name: Shachi Jain
people.since: With the company since July 2009; Whole-time Director since 29 August 2025
people.relation: Promoter; wife of MD Manish Jain
people.bio: Aged 49, she holds a diploma in business administration (HR) and has been employed by the company since July 2009. She joined the board as a whole-time director in August 2025, confirmed by shareholders in October 2025.

people.name: Piyush Jain
people.relation: Brother of Ritu Jain (the Chairman's wife)
people.bio: Aged 49, he holds a master's in computer applications and has 28 years of experience; he joined from Vaddmaan Innovation LLP in April 2023 and runs operations as COO. He was among the three best-paid employees in FY26 at about ₹52 lakh.

people.name: Sunil Chauhan
people.bio: He is the CFO and a key managerial person. The annual report gives no details of his education or career. He is supported by Deputy CFO Deepak Malhotra, a cost accountant with 30 years' experience who joined from APCO Infratech in October 2024.

companies.changes: Sanjay Jain's re-appointment was rejected at the 28 August 2025 AGM; he was re-appointed as Chairman and whole-time director, and Ritu and Shachi Jain were made whole-time directors, all approved by postal ballot on 3 October 2025. Mukul Jain joined as an independent director in October 2025. No executive changes filed since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: A family company controlled by founder Ramveer Singh, who is Executive Chairman and owns 67.85% himself (promoters 69.7%). His son Ashish Tomar is MD and also CFO, and Ashish's wife Kritika Tomar is a whole-time director. A hired CEO, Harish Kumar Kansal, a former chief engineer at UP Jal Nigam, joined in November 2025. The chairman and MD are each paid ₹6cr a year.

people.name: Ramveer Singh
people.since: Founder; with the company since December 2010
people.relation: Founder promoter; father of MD Ashish Tomar; father-in-law of Kritika Tomar
people.bio: Aged 63, an engineer by qualification with more than 35 years in civil construction and business development. He founded the company and leads project bidding, marketing, overall management and finances. His pay is ₹6cr a year.

people.name: Ashish Tomar
people.since: Co-founder; with the company since December 2010
people.relation: Co-founder promoter; son of Chairman Ramveer Singh; husband of Kritika Tomar
people.bio: Aged 37, a civil engineer with an MBA and 16 years of experience in sewerage and power transmission and distribution projects. He co-founded the company with his father and is both MD and CFO, certifying the accounts alongside the CEO. His pay is ₹6cr a year.

people.name: Kritika Tomar
people.relation: Wife of MD Ashish Tomar; daughter-in-law of the Chairman
people.bio: Aged 32, she holds an MSc in biotechnology from Mody University, Rajasthan. She has been with the company since October 2022 and handles administration. Her pay is ₹1.2cr a year.

people.name: Harish Kumar Kansal
people.bio: Aged 63, a civil engineer with 38 years of experience. He was previously Chief Engineer (Level 1) at the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), the state water and sewerage agency. He joined as CEO in November 2025 on ₹60 lakh a year.

companies.changes: Harish Kumar Kansal joined as CEO on 14 November 2025. Company Secretary Nand Kishore Sharma resigned on 17 January 2026; Himanshu was appointed Company Secretary from 15 April 2026. No other changes filed since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 2001 by the Kallarakal family, whose Antony group also runs vehicle-body businesses. Founder Jose Jacob Kallarakal is Chairman and MD and his brother Shiju Jacob Kallarakal is an executive director; another promoter, Shiju Antony Kallarakal, is a non-executive director and Chief Sustainability Officer. Promoters own 46.09%, spread across many Kallarakal family members and the group companies Antony Motors and Antony Garages.

people.name: Jose Jacob Kallarakal
people.since: Founder; Chairman & MD since inception in 2001 (current term to December 2028)
people.relation: Founder promoter; brother of Shiju Jacob Kallarakal
people.bio: A mechanical engineering graduate from Bharati Vidyapeeth's College of Engineering, University of Mumbai, who also attended the Authentic Leader Development programme at Harvard Business School. He founded the company in 2001 and has led it since, with over two decades in municipal solid waste management. He drives business development and strategy and has spoken for the industry at the Waste Management Innovation Conference at Ohio State University. His current five-year term runs to December 2028.

people.name: Shiju Jacob Kallarakal
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Chairman Jose Jacob Kallarakal
people.stake: 5.25% (14,90,510 shares; FY26 AGM notice and June 2026 shareholding); promoters together 46.09%
people.bio: Aged 49, a chemical engineering graduate from Bharati Vidyapeeth's College of Engineering, University of Mumbai. He has been with the company since 2001 and was earlier Executive Director and CFO, running accounts, finance, treasury and legal. As Chief Risk Officer he now focuses on enterprise risk and on technology such as GPS/RFID fleet tracking and geo-fencing. After the merger of the subsidiary AG Enviro Infra Projects, which paid his salary until then, the board fixed a new term and higher pay for him in July 2026, put to the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Subramanian N G
people.bio: He is the Group CFO and a key managerial person with 27 years of work experience, and certifies the accounts with the MD. He was paid by the subsidiary AG Enviro Infra Projects until its merger into the company. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier employers.

people.name: Mahendra Ananthula
people.role: Group President – Operations, Business Development & Diversification
people.bio: Named by the company as senior management, with 34 years of work experience, heading operations, business development and new businesses across the group. The annual report gives no details of his education or earlier employers.

companies.changes: In July 2026 the board fixed the term and revised pay of Executive Director Shiju Jacob Kallarakal after the merger of AG Enviro Infra Projects into the company; this goes to the 2026 AGM. No change in senior management during FY26. Company Secretary is Harshada Rane.

companies.styleNote: A family company. Founder Vijay Agarwal is Chairman & MD; his wife Mona, son Sorab and daughter Surbhi Garg are all whole-time directors. The four executive directors are promoters; the other four board members are independent. Hired professionals run finance, sourcing and investor relations (President Vyom Agarwal), plants (COO Hitesh Kumar Agarwal) and forklifts. Promoters own 65.4%.

people.name: Vijay Agarwal
people.relation: Founder; husband of Mona Agarwal; father of Sorab Agarwal and Surbhi Garg
people.stake: 28.76% (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); family together 65.42%
people.bio: A mechanical engineer with an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), Delhi. He worked at Bhartiya Cutler Hammer and then for over a decade at Escorts before leaving in January 1995 to start ACE in Faridabad with about ₹15 lakh of his own savings; the first crane rolled out in March 1996. He built ACE into India's largest maker of mobile and pick-and-carry cranes. He has about 55 years of industry experience and is 77. Forbes listed him among the world's billionaires in 2024.

people.name: Sorab Agarwal
people.since: Board since March 1998; re-appointed to September 2028
people.relation: Son of the Chairman Vijay Agarwal and Mona Agarwal; brother of Surbhi Garg
people.bio: A mechanical engineer who has been with ACE since 1998 and has about 29 years in material handling and heavy engineering. He leads the cranes and equipment business and has overall strategic and operational responsibility, including sales, service, quality and client relationships. The company credits him with building its all-India sales and service network and taking it into new products and markets. He also sits on the boards of the ACE KATO joint venture and other group companies. He is 49.

people.name: Mona Agarwal
people.relation: Wife of the Chairman Vijay Agarwal; mother of Sorab Agarwal and Surbhi Garg
people.bio: A promoter who has been with ACE since it was set up in January 1995. She works on administration, human resources, business management and employee engagement. She oversees the company's CSR work, notably the ACE Emergency Response Service, which runs advanced life-support ambulances in Palwal and Faridabad. She is 70.

people.name: Surbhi Garg
people.relation: Daughter of the Chairman Vijay Agarwal and Mona Agarwal; sister of Sorab Agarwal
people.bio: A promoter and whole-time director since November 2011. She looks after administration and human resources and has helped the company set policies on performance evaluation. The company credits her team for HR awards such as 'Dream Companies to Work For – Construction Sector' (2019). She is 48.

people.name: Rajan Luthra
people.bio: A cost accountant (ICWA) and company secretary with a postgraduate diploma in personnel management from FMS, Delhi University. He has about 38 years of experience at companies including ABB, Talbros Automotive and Federal-Mogul Goetze. He joined ACE as CFO in June 2010 and handles planning, tax, compliance, fund-raising and investor relations, and speaks on earnings calls.

people.name: Vyom Agarwal
people.bio: A gold medallist in economics from Hansraj College, Delhi University. He spent eight years at Axis Bank as a financial analyst in corporate and forex banking. At ACE he runs strategic sourcing and vendor development, cost control, supply chain, insurance and investor relations, and opens the company's earnings calls.

people.name: Chetan R. Gole
people.bio: A production engineer from Birla Vishwakarma Mahavidyalaya (S.P. University, Gujarat). Before ACE he worked at Elecon Engineering and Godrej & Boyce in project marketing and business development for material-handling equipment. He has been with ACE for about 15 years (as of 2024) and runs the forklift business, where the company says it has steadily gained share.

companies.changes: No changes to the board or senior management in FY26 or since, per the FY26 annual report and exchange filings to date. Sorab Agarwal retired by rotation and was re-elected at the 18 Sep 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by the MEIL group: MEIL Holdings owns 50.02%. MEIL's MD, P V Krishna Reddy, has been non-executive Chairman since July 2025, and MEIL's Peketi Rajesh Reddy sits on the board as a non-executive director. Day-to-day the company is run by a hired MD, Mahesh Babu Subramanian (ex-CEO of Switch Mobility), with a long-serving CFO. No executive is a promoter or family member.

people.name: Mahesh Babu Subramanian
people.bio: Holds a postgraduate degree in engineering from BITS Pilani and is a Fulbright Scholar. He did leadership programmes at Carnegie Mellon's Tepper School of Business, IMD Switzerland and Yale. He has over 30 years in the mobility industry and was MD & CEO of Mahindra Electric and then CEO of Switch Mobility, Ashok Leyland's electric bus and van arm, before joining Olectra. He has served on government, CII and FICCI committees on electric vehicles. He replaced K V Pradeep, who resigned as Chairman & MD in July 2025.

people.name: B. Sharat Chandra
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a master's degree and over three decades of work experience. He has been Olectra's CFO since December 2017, through the build-up of the electric-bus business and its MEIL-backed order book, and signs the accounts with the MD.

people.name: K. N. M. Rao (Kallepalli Nagamalleshwar Rao)
people.role: Vice President – Product Development (e-Bus / Mobility Division)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Osmania University, Hyderabad, with over three decades in product and platform development for electric and diesel vehicles. He held senior roles at Switch Mobility, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra & Mahindra and Tata Motors before joining Olectra to lead product development.

people.name: Rajesh Sharma
people.role: Vice President – Sales, Marketing & Communications (Mobility Division)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Osmania University with a postgraduate diploma in marketing from Symbiosis. He has over 30 years in the automotive and engineering sectors, including more than seven years in electric vehicles, with senior roles at QUCEV Technology, Switch Mobility, Pinnacle Industries and Neuton Auto, where he ran sales and marketing for electric trucks, buses and light commercial vehicles.

companies.changes: Chairman & MD K V Pradeep resigned in June 2025 (relieved 4 Jul 2025). Peketi Rajesh Reddy was a whole-time director from 5 Jul to 8 Nov 2025 and is now non-executive. Mahesh Babu Subramanian became MD on 27 Sep 2025. New VPs for product development (Feb 2026), HR (Suhas Athma, Feb 2026) and sales (Mar 2026); AVP-HR Sanjay Rastogi resigned in March 2026. No KMP changes filed since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Two founding families own 80%: the Vijay family (Krishnaswamy Vijay, Kalyani Vijay and their trusts, about 45.5%) and the John/Hansen family (Jacob Jiten John, Susie John and their trusts, about 34.5%). Co-founder Krishnaswamy Vijay stays on as Executive Chairman, but the business is run by a hired MD & CEO, Shubhabrata Saha, since January 2023. Jacob Jiten John left the executive role in May 2026; his family now has a non-executive nominee on the board. Three CFOs have left in the past year and the post is vacant again.

people.name: Krishnaswamy Vijay
people.since: 1992 (co-founder; on the board since July 1992); current term to September 2029
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; not related to any other director or KMP
people.stake: 4.50% in his own name (AGM notice 2026); with Kalyani Vijay and the Green Haven and Ohana trusts, the Vijay side holds about 45.5% (June 2026 shareholding)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from IIT Madras. Before Ajax he worked at Tractors Engineers Limited and Larsen & Toubro. He has been with Ajax since it was incorporated in 1992 and has about 42 years in manufacturing. As Executive Chairman he sets strategy, while day-to-day management sits with the hired CEO. He is 75 and retired by rotation, seeking re-election, at the 28 September 2026 AGM.

people.name: Shubhabrata Saha
people.stake: 161 shares, about 0.00% (FY26 annual report); holds stock options (11.4 lakh options granted under the 2024 ESOP plan)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in science (engineering) from Aligarh Muslim University and a master's in management studies from Bombay University. He spent over two decades at Mahindra & Mahindra in leadership roles, ending as CEO of its Farm Division. He then joined the Adventz group as MD & CEO of Mangalore Chemicals and Fertilisers and deputy CEO of its agri business. He joined Ajax as MD & CEO in January 2023 and led it through its February 2025 listing.

companies.changes: Heavy turnover in the finance role: CFO Tuhin Basu resigned 30 Sep 2025; interim CFO Ganesh B J (from 31 Dec 2025) resigned 2 Jun 2026; CFO Ketan Pendse (from 2 Jun 2026) resigned 7 Sep 2026 for personal reasons, and no successor has been announced. Whole-time Director Jacob Jiten John (promoter) resigned 18 May 2026; Sachin Nandgaonkar joined as a nominee of his family trusts. Chief Marketing Officer Gautam Eunny left in June 2025. Independent directors Raghavan Sadagopan (Mar 2026) and Rajan Wadhera (Jun 2026) left; Shishir Joshipura joined in Sep 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder-run: co-founders Tarun Mehta (CEO) and Swapnil Jain (CTO), IIT Madras graduates who started Ather there in 2013, are the two executive directors. They own only about 5% each. Hero MotoCorp, the largest shareholder at 29.2%, is also classed as a promoter; promoters together hold 39.6%. The board is chaired by an independent director, Neelam Dhawan, and the directors are not related. A preferential issue approved in August 2026 includes warrants for Hero MotoCorp and the two founders.

people.name: Tarun Sanjay Mehta
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; not related to other directors
people.stake: 4.89% (shareholding pattern, July 2026), plus about 0.28% through two family trusts
people.bio: Holds a dual bachelor's and master's degree in engineering design from IIT Madras, where Ather was started in 2013. He has led the company, covering product, business and growth, and raises its capital. He has over ten years in electric vehicles. He was named in Forbes India's '30 under 30' (2018) and Fortune India's '40 under 40' (2019, 2021, 2023), and received the AIMA 'Young Entrepreneur' award.

people.name: Swapnil Babanlal Jain
people.role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chief Technical Officer
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter; not related to other directors
people.stake: 4.89% (shareholding pattern, July 2026), plus about 0.34% through two family trusts
people.bio: Holds a dual bachelor's and master's degree in engineering design from IIT Madras. He co-founded Ather in 2013 and runs its long-term technology roadmap and engineering team, covering hardware, software, electronics and mechanical design. He has over ten years in electric vehicles and shares the AIMA and Forbes/Fortune recognitions with his co-founder.

people.name: Sohil Dilipkumar Parekh
people.bio: A chartered accountant with bachelor's degrees in commerce and law from Gujarat University. Before Ather he worked at Claris Limited and had earlier roles in waste-to-energy, pharmaceuticals, market research, BPO and IT services. He oversees financial strategy, reporting, fund-raising and tax, and took the company through its April 2025 IPO and the 2026 QIP. He is an ultra-endurance athlete who has represented India in full-distance Ironman triathlons.

people.name: Ravneet Singh Phokela
people.bio: A commerce graduate from Delhi University with a postgraduate diploma in business management from IMT Ghaziabad. Before Ather he worked at Nokia UK, Flipkart, Lowe Lintas, PAYBACK (Loyalty Solutions & Research) and Whirlpool of India. He runs marketing, sales, after-sales and service, the Ather Grid charging network, analytics and customer service, and is leading the push into overseas markets.

people.name: Sanjeev Kumar Singh
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from IIT Kharagpur. Before Ather he worked at Genpact, Bosch, ACME Tele Power and Tata Motors. He runs manufacturing across Ather's factories, including the Hosur plant and the new AURIC plant in Maharashtra, plus programme management and planning.

people.name: Harendra Saksena
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Jamia Millia Islamia with a master's in engineering management from the University of Technology, Sydney, and a supply-chain certificate from Stanford Graduate School of Business. Before Ather he worked at Johnson Electric, Siemens VDO Automotive, Motherson Auto and Daewoo Motors India. He runs sourcing and supplier management.

people.name: Milind Suresh Kothekar
people.role: Head – Product Management & Chief of Staff to the CEO
people.bio: Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering from IIT Bombay and previously worked at Eaton Technologies. He leads product management across the scooters, charging, the AtherStack software, accessories and ownership experience, and is chief of staff to the CEO.

companies.changes: Chief Human Resource Officer Sunitha Lal resigned in June 2025; Surabhi Loshali became CHRO on 5 Jan 2026. Anjani Kumar joined as Chief Digital & Information Officer on 29 May 2025. Hero MotoCorp nominee Niranjan Kumar Gupta left the board in May 2025; Vivek Anand joined as a non-executive director in Nov 2025. No KMP changes since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Bengaluru-based VST Group, controlled by the extended VST promoter family, which holds 55.6%. Promoter family member V.T. Ravindra is Managing Director. The non-executive Chairman is Arun V. Surendra, Group MD of the VST Group, and another family member, V.V. Pravindra, is a non-executive director. Day-to-day operations are run by a hired CEO, Antony Cherukara (since 2020), and a hired CFO. Former Chairman V.K. Surendra, who led the company from 1996 to 2024, died in January 2026.

people.name: V.T. Ravindra
people.since: February 2021; re-appointed for three years from April 2024
people.relation: Promoter family; the company says he is related to Chairman Arun V. Surendra, director V.V. Pravindra and the late V.K. Surendra
people.bio: Holds a postgraduate diploma in management. He has over 30 years in the VST Group's businesses, setting up and running two-wheeler and car dealerships, spare-parts distribution and plantation management, and helped build the group's car dealerships across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. He became MD in February 2021, succeeding V.P. Mahendra, and the company reached its highest-ever turnover under him. He also sits on the boards of VST group companies, including VST Zetor and the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries–VST Diesel Engines joint venture.

people.name: Antony Cherukara
people.bio: A hired professional who joined as CEO in 2020 and runs the business day to day. He previously worked at Mahindra & Mahindra and then at Kirloskar Oil Engines, which he joined in 2012 and where he worked on corporate strategy and the revamp of its agri-business. At VST he speaks for the company on strategy, such as its plan (announced in 2022) for an electric tractor for the US market.

people.name: Nitin Agrawal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with nearly 20 years of experience in business finance, financial planning and analysis, costing, working capital, tax, compliance and finance automation. He replaced Pankaj Khemka as CFO in May 2023.

companies.changes: No KMP changes in FY26 or since, per the FY26 annual report and filings. Independent director Siva Kameswari Vissa retired on 28 Jul 2026 and Shuba Kumar joined on 27 Jul 2026. Former Chairman V.K. Surendra died in January 2026.

companies.styleNote: A founder-family company. Co-founder Ranbir Singh Khadwalia is Chairman & MD; his son Anshul is a whole-time director and his other son Shubham heads international business and cranes sales. The other founding promoter, Sunita Saini, holds 22.2% but has no executive role. Promoters own 70.6% in all, including 9.1% through Futuristic Mining and Construction Solutions LLP, which the two founders own. Half the board is independent. The CFO is a young chartered accountant hired in 2023.

people.name: Ranbir Singh Khadwalia
people.relation: Founding promoter; father of Anshul and Shubham Khadwalia
people.bio: Holds a diploma in mechanical engineering from the Haryana State Board of Technical Education. Before starting Indo Farm he worked in production at Eicher Farm Machinery. He has been with the company since it was set up in 1994 and has over three decades in farm equipment manufacturing. He oversees the whole business, including new plants and business development. He is 65.

people.name: Anshul Khadwalia
people.since: Board since May 2014; whole-time director since August 2023
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD Ranbir Singh Khadwalia; brother of Shubham Khadwalia
people.bio: Holds a BSc in business and management from Aston University, UK. He ran sales and marketing for the company's farming division and now looks after sales and marketing strategy for tractors and spare parts, brand building and market expansion. He was named in Hindustan Times' 'Top 30 Under 30' and is a TEDx speaker.

people.name: Shubham Khadwalia
people.role: Executive Vice President – International Business (earlier Sales & Marketing, Construction Equipment)
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD Ranbir Singh Khadwalia; brother of Anshul Khadwalia
people.bio: Holds a BSc (Hons) in operations management from Lancaster University and an MSc in strategic marketing management from Aston University, UK. He has run sales and marketing for the cranes and construction-equipment division and international business, and is now listed as EVP – International Business. He received a 'Young Achiever' award from Dainik Bhaskar.

people.name: Amit Kumar
people.bio: Holds an MBA and a bachelor's degree in engineering from Maharshi Dayanand University, Rohtak. He has over 14 years in manufacturing, operations, procurement and plant management, including vendor development, supply chain and ISO/IATF quality systems. He replaced Charan Singh Saini, who ran plant operations, as whole-time director.

people.name: Varun Sharma
people.bio: A chartered accountant and commerce graduate from Punjab University. Before Indo Farm he had short stints at Infosys, Reckitt Benckiser and Bunge India in finance and accounts. He was 28 when the January 2025 IPO prospectus was filed.

companies.changes: Whole-time Director Charan Singh Saini resigned on 28 Oct 2025; Amit Kumar joined as whole-time director on 12 Nov 2025. No KMP changes filed since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by the Gainwell group since January 2024: TIL Global Private Limited holds 61.3%. Gainwell's promoter and chairman, Sunil Kumar Chaturvedi, a former IAS officer, is TIL's Chairman & MD. Two Gainwell executives sit on the board as executive directors (Alok Kumar Tripathi, Director & President, and Ayan Banerjee, Gainwell's Group CFO, as Director–Finance). There are no family ties among the directors. The previous promoters were reclassified as public shareholders in June 2024.

people.name: Sunil Kumar Chaturvedi
people.relation: Promoter of the Gainwell group, which controls TIL through TIL Global Private Limited
people.stake: No shares in his own name (FY26 annual report); controls TIL through Gainwell's TIL Global Private Limited, which holds 61.3% (Sep 2026)
people.bio: A fellow chartered accountant who spent about two decades in the IAS. In government he was a Director in the Finance Ministry's Department of Economic Affairs, private secretary to the Railways Minister, a Director in the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Project Director of the NATRiP automotive testing project, and a special secretary in West Bengal. After retiring voluntarily in 2008 he was Executive Director and COO of Bharat Forge's capital goods business until 2013. He joined Gainwell (then Tractors India Private Limited, a Caterpillar dealer) in January 2014, led its management buyout in 2016 and has chaired it since. He took over TIL in January 2024, putting in ₹120cr, and also sits on the board of Vesuvius India.

people.name: Alok Kumar Tripathi
people.bio: An engineering graduate from BMS College of Engineering, Bengaluru, with a PGDBM from IMT Ghaziabad. He began at BEML and HMEED, then joined Tractors India (now Gainwell) in 1995, where he held roles in branch operations, parts marketing, spare parts and construction-machine sales, ending as Gainwell's National Product Support Head. At TIL he runs operations, product support and customer engagement. He retired by rotation and sought re-election at the July 2026 AGM.

people.name: Ayan Banerjee
people.bio: A chartered accountant trained at Lovelock & Lewes, with about three decades in heavy engineering, refractories, electronics and media, including start-ups. He is Group CFO of the Gainwell group and oversees finance at TIL as an executive director.

people.name: Kanhaiya Gupta
people.bio: A commerce (Hons) graduate who is a fellow chartered accountant, company secretary and cost accountant, with over 23 years in finance. He was CFO of Rashmi Metaliks, deputy CFO (finance controller) at ACC (Lafarge-Holcim group), and earlier worked at IFB Industries and ITC.

people.name: Pinaki Niyogy
people.bio: A TIL veteran who joined as a management trainee in 1992 and has over 31 years with the company in product development, engineering operations and technology. He leads TIL's product portfolio and engineering work under the new owners.

companies.changes: No KMP changes during FY26 or since, per the FY26 annual report and filings. Vijay Singh Chauhan joined as an independent director on 22 Dec 2025 and Anurag Srivastava as a non-executive director in Nov 2025. TIL bought 60% of Tulip Compression in February 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder-led: Bhavish Aggarwal founded Ola Electric in 2017 and is Chairman & MD; he is the only executive director. He holds 26.5% directly, and promoters hold 33.0% in all, including Ani Technologies (Ola Cabs, 3.5%) and the Indus Trust (3.0%). SoftBank's SVF II holds 12.3%. No directors are related to each other. The team around him has churned: the CFO changed in January 2026, one of the two COOs left in September 2026, and the company secretary has changed twice in 15 months.

people.name: Bhavish Aggarwal
people.relation: Founder and promoter; not related to other directors
people.stake: 26.52% directly (shareholding pattern, June 2026); promoter group together 32.97%
people.bio: An IIT Bombay computer science and engineering graduate who worked briefly at Microsoft Research India. He co-founded ANI Technologies (Ola Cabs) in 2010 and set up Ola Electric in 2017, leading it through the Futurefactory scooter plant, the cell 'gigafactory' and the August 2024 IPO. He also founded the AI company Krutrim. He runs the business hands-on, often announces plans on social media (which the company then files with the exchanges), and draws no remuneration from Ola Electric's subsidiaries.

people.name: Deepak Rastogi
people.bio: A chartered accountant and MBA with over 30 years in finance. He has been President, Group CFO or head of finance at Puravankara, Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals, Tata AutoComp Systems, Timken, Alcatel, DuPont, Castrol and Raymond, and has sat on the boards of listed companies. The company says he has worked on about $1 billion of equity deals, including IPOs and cross-border M&A. He replaced Harish Abichandani, who resigned for personal reasons.

people.name: Shaun William Calvert
people.bio: A manufacturing executive who was Deputy CEO at VinFast in Vietnam before joining Ola Electric. Earlier he spent many years at General Motors, including as director of operational excellence, director of vehicle assembly operations and in its Australian supply chain. He is one of Ola Electric's senior management personnel in charge of operations.

companies.changes: CFO Harish Abichandani resigned 19 Jan 2026; Deepak Rastogi took over 20 Jan 2026. COO Hyun Shik Park resigned 5 Sep 2026. Senior Director (New Business) Vishal Chaturvedi left 31 Dec 2025. Company Secretary Pritam Das Mohapatra left in Jun 2025; successor Abhishek Jain left 28 Aug 2026; Deepa Bansal appointed 28 Sep 2026. Independent director Ananth Sankaranarayanan left in Dec 2025. The board approved a rights issue on 28 Sep 2026.

companies.styleNote: A family company run by the Aryas of Hisar, Haryana. Niraj Arya is Chairman & Whole-time Director, his son Kunal is MD, his brother Deepak is a whole-time director and his daughter Sayuri is a non-executive director. Niraj, Deepak and Kunal hold about 24.3% each; promoters own 72.8%, and some promoter shares are pledged. In April 2026 the company hired an outside CEO, Divyanshu Agarwal. The September 2026 preferential issue gives the three promoters ₹85cr of warrants at ₹853 a share.

people.name: Kunal Arya
people.relation: Son of the Chairman Niraj Arya; nephew of Deepak Arya; brother of director Sayuri Arya
people.bio: A promoter who completed his senior secondary schooling (CBSE) in 2013 and had about five years in electric vehicles and batteries in the IPO draft prospectus. As MD he sets business strategy and runs business planning, purchasing, production, inventory, dispatch and sales and marketing. He speaks for the company on its expansion plans. He was 28 in the IPO draft prospectus.

people.name: Niraj Arya
people.relation: Father of MD Kunal Arya and director Sayuri Arya; brother of Deepak Arya
people.bio: A promoter who completed his senior secondary schooling (Haryana Board) in 1989 and has about 18 years in the electric vehicle and battery business. He handles general administration, accounts and finance, legal and compliance. He was 52 in the IPO draft prospectus.

people.name: Deepak Arya
people.relation: Brother of the Chairman Niraj Arya; uncle of Kunal and Sayuri Arya
people.bio: A promoter with a BA from Dayanand College, Hisar (Kurukshetra University) and about 12 years in electric vehicles and batteries. He is responsible for human resources and customer relationship management. He was 46 in the IPO draft prospectus.

people.name: Divyanshu Agarwal
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a B.Com (Hons) from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata, who trained at Price Waterhouse (PwC) in Kolkata. He joined Navi Limited in November 2021, worked with its founder and chairman on cross-functional projects and on Navi's IPO papers and private-equity fund-raising, and from October 2024 headed Navi's UPI business. He is the first outside CEO at Zelio and is not related to the promoters.

people.name: Shubham Garg
people.bio: A chartered accountant (ICAI member since 2023) with about four years in finance, accounts, tax and compliance in the IPO draft prospectus. He oversees accounting, banking, tax and corporate finance.

people.name: Sanjay Kumar
people.bio: Holds a diploma in mechanical engineering from the Haryana State Board of Technical Education and has over 15 years in production, process improvement and quality in the automotive industry. Before Zelio he worked at Jindal Mobilitric, E-Sprinto Green Energy, Okaya EV, Okinawa Autotech, Mahindra & Mahindra and Suzuki Motorcycle India. He runs plant operations, including production, quality, inventory and dispatch.

companies.changes: Divyanshu Agarwal was appointed CEO on 15 Apr 2026. No other executive changes were found on the company's investor page; an FY26 annual report was not found online, so the KMP list is based on the October 2025 IPO documents and later filings.

companies.styleNote: A Singhal family business from Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, founded in 1972 by the late Kanohar Lal Singhal. Brothers Dinesh Singhal (Chairman & MD) and Adesh Singhal run it with Dinesh's sons Vivek and Abhishek Singhal as whole-time directors; Adesh's sons Virat and Aditya also work in the company and are promoters. The family owns its 74.64% through the K Sons Family Trust (72.08%) and Kanohar International (2.56%). The board had no independent directors until July 2025. Each of the four executive directors gets 1.5% of pre-tax profit on top of fixed pay; family pay was ₹16.8cr in FY26, about 13% of profit.

people.name: Dinesh Singhal
people.since: With the company since 1976; chairman since August 2025
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Adesh Singhal and father of Vivek and Abhishek Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust, which holds 72.08% after the IPO
people.bio: Dinesh Singhal, 71, has a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from IIT Roorkee and more than 40 years in transformer making. He was president of the Federation of Indian Micro and Small & Medium Enterprises and of the Indian Industries Association, and is an independent director of Shivalik Small Finance Bank. He was paid ₹3.85cr in FY26 (fixed ₹1.25cr a year plus 1.5% of pre-tax profit).

people.name: Adesh Singhal
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Dinesh Singhal and father of Virat and Aditya Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust
people.bio: Adesh Singhal, 68, has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from IIT Roorkee and more than 40 years in transformer making. He leads engineering and quality assurance. He was paid ₹3.6cr in FY26 (fixed ₹1cr a year plus 1.5% of pre-tax profit).

people.name: Vivek Singhal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Dinesh Singhal and brother of Abhishek Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust
people.bio: Vivek Singhal, 48, has a B.Tech in electrical engineering from IIT Bombay and over 25 years in marketing, business development and strategy. He drove the company's expansion across India and into contracting for substations and transmission lines. He was paid ₹3.35cr in FY26.

people.name: Abhishek Singhal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Dinesh Singhal and brother of Vivek Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust
people.bio: Abhishek Singhal, 46, has a B.Tech in electrical engineering from IIT Delhi and over 23 years in design, technology development and systems integration. He leads design and development and oversees ERP, engineering software and IT, and he led the Q1 FY27 earnings call. He was paid ₹3.35cr in FY26.

people.name: Virat Singhal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Adesh Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust
people.bio: Virat Singhal, 43, has an engineering degree from Nagpur University and an MBA from the International University of Japan. He has over 9 years of commercial and legal experience at the company and was paid ₹0.45cr in FY26. His firm, Virat Singhal & Associates, was paid legal and professional fees of ₹1.05cr in FY24 and ₹0.69cr in FY25, nil in FY26.

people.name: Aditya Singhal
people.relation: Promoter; son of Adesh Singhal
people.stake: No shares in his own name; trustee and beneficiary of K Sons Family Trust
people.bio: Aditya Singhal, 39, has a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani and an executive MBA. He has 13 years of experience in gas-insulated switchgear design and manufacturing at the company and was paid ₹0.43cr in FY26. His firm, Aditya Singhal & Associates, was paid professional fees of ₹1.04cr in FY24 and ₹0.69cr in FY25, nil in FY26.

people.name: Shiv Kumar Kamboj
people.bio: Shiv Kumar Kamboj is a chartered accountant with a commerce degree from Meerut University and more than 30 years in finance and accounts, almost all at Kanohar, which he joined in 1996. He previously worked at Shivaya Laminations and Inter Software and Technologies. He was made CFO in August 2025, ahead of the IPO, and was paid ₹0.37cr in FY26.

people.name: Neha
people.since: Joined April 2025; company secretary since August 2025
people.bio: Neha holds commerce degrees from the University of Delhi and a law degree from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut, and is a member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India with over 13 years of experience. She joined in April 2025 and became company secretary in August 2025.

companies.changes: Ahead of the IPO: five independent directors appointed on 3 July 2025 (the board had none before); Dinesh Singhal made chairman and Shiv Kumar Kamboj CFO on 14 August 2025; independent director Anil Girotra resigned on 8 October 2025; whole-time director Brijesh Singhal (a promoter-group member and trust beneficiary) resigned on 26 November 2025 for personal reasons. No changes filed since listing on 16 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 2015 and run by its promoter, Vishal Budhia of Surat, who started Gujarat's first community boiler in 2014 and is Chairman and Managing Director. He holds 70.5% directly after the IPO, and three family trusts (trustees he and his wife Ritu; beneficiaries include their daughters) hold another 6.75%; promoters and group own 77.96%. The family's Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing group is both a large customer and a steam supplier, and the two executive directors came from Sanjoo-linked mills. Three of six directors are independent, one of whom sits with the promoter on another company's board. Executive pay is modest: the chairman was paid ₹0.54cr in FY26.

people.name: Vishal Budhia
people.since: Director since the company was formed in 2015; managing director since March 2021 (reappointed to March 2031); chairman since June 2023
people.relation: Promoter and founder; husband of Ritu Budhia
people.stake: 70.5% after the IPO (86.97% before; sold 75.3 lakh shares in the offer for sale), plus trusteeship of three family trusts holding 6.75%
people.bio: Vishal Budhia, 50, attended the B.Sc. course at South Gujarat University and has more than 30 years in textile processing and 11 in community boilers. He is secretary of the South Gujarat Textile Processors Welfare body and a director of Sachin Infra Environment (a common effluent plant), the family's Sanjoo companies, Aerohouse Aviation and Sanjoo Dyeing Inc. (US), from which Steamhouse charters an aircraft. He was paid ₹0.54cr in FY26 plus ₹0.29cr of reimbursed expenses.

people.name: Ritu Budhia
people.relation: Wife of Vishal Budhia
people.stake: 300 shares directly; trustee of the VSB, Budhia and VB Business Trusts
people.bio: Ritu Budhia, 49, is a commerce graduate of the University of Mumbai and earlier ran a proprietorship, Green Energy. She is a trustee of the three promoter trusts set up in August 2023.

people.name: Yadav Lalankumar Dayanand
people.bio: Yadav Lalankumar, 52, has no formal education and about 14 years in management, earlier at Sanjoo Dyeing; he is also a director of the Sanjoo companies and Aerohouse Aviation. He was paid ₹0.07cr in FY26 and holds no shares.

people.name: Ramprakash B. Sharma
people.bio: Ramprakash Sharma, 61, is a commerce graduate of the University of Rajasthan and an associate company secretary with 22 years of experience, earlier at Shilpa Dyeing & Printing Mills. He was paid ₹0.21cr in FY26.

people.name: Vaibhav Gattani
people.bio: Vaibhav Gattani is a chartered accountant and commerce graduate of JNV University, Jodhpur, and worked as a banker at Axis, Federal, Kotak, AU Small Finance and YES Bank before joining. He led the Q1 FY27 call's guidance on volumes and ₹1,000-a-tonne profit. He was paid ₹0.64cr in FY26.

people.name: Suchi Goenka
people.bio: Suchi Goenka is a commerce graduate of VNSGU, Surat, and joined from Sanjoo Dyeing when the company was formed. She was paid ₹0.24cr in FY26.

people.name: Mehulkumar B. Chatniwala
people.bio: Mehulkumar Chatniwala is a mechanical engineer from South Gujarat University who worked at Hindalco (Birla Copper), GHCL, Nirma, Baroda Rayon and Gujarat Glass. He was paid ₹0.18cr in FY26.

people.name: Shyam Bhadresh Kapadia
people.bio: Shyam Kapadia holds commerce and law degrees from VNSGU and is a fellow company secretary; he worked at Laxmi Diamond and Bigbloc Construction before joining. He was paid ₹0.13cr in FY26.

companies.changes: Head of projects and design Himmat Singh Chauhan retired in May 2026. The board of six (three independent: Richa Goyal, Vinay Sonthalia and Baldevsinh Rathod, a retired Gujarat pollution-board scientist) is unchanged for three years. One promoter-group member, Ambika Agarwal, refused to give information for the prospectus. No changes filed since listing on 17 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by KKR: its vehicle Hector Asia bought 54.3% from CVC on 30 May 2025 at ₹445 a share, and with founder Dr B.S. Ajaikumar (9.3%) the promoter group holds 64.2%. A hired CEO, Dr Manish Mattoo (formerly of Apollo), runs the business; the founder is non-executive chairman and is also paid as a consultant. The ten-member board has two KKR nominees (Akshay Tanna and Simrun Mehta), the founder, his daughter Anjali Ajaikumar Rossi, the CEO and five independent directors (Geeta Mathur, Rajagopalan Raghavan, Pradip Kanakia, Rajiv Maliwal and Bijou Kurien); Pradip Kanakia also sits on the board of ICRA, which rates HCG. There is no pledge, but KKR's HSBC acquisition loan carries an undertaking not to sell its shares. As a private-equity owner, KKR is expected to sell within a few years; the new 2026 option scheme lets options vest early on a change of control.

people.name: Dr B.S. Ajaikumar
people.since: Founder; CEO from 2005 to January 2021; non-executive since mid-2025
people.relation: Founder and promoter; father of director Anjali Ajaikumar Rossi
people.bio: A radiation and medical oncologist with an MBBS from St John's Medical College, Bangalore, and residencies in radiotherapy at MD Anderson (University of Texas) and in oncology at the University of Virginia. He practised in the US and India for over four decades and built HCG from a Bengaluru cancer centre into a national chain. In FY26 he received ₹2.57cr of medical consultancy charges and ₹2.0cr of professional fees, on top of ₹1.0cr of salary for April–May 2025. His Inviga Healthcare Fund I bought HCG's Milann fertility business in June 2026.

people.name: Dr Manish Mattoo
people.since: Mid-2025, after KKR took control; also interim CFO from December 2025 to May 2026
people.bio: Trained as a doctor (MBBS and MD in anaesthesiology, BJ Medical College, Ahmedabad) and holds an MBA from the Indian School of Business. He has over two decades in healthcare management: Regional CEO for Karnataka and the Central Region at Apollo Hospitals, Vice President at Fortis Healthcare, and roles at Medtronic and Monitor Group. He practised earlier at PGI Chandigarh and Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad.

people.name: Sanjeev Kumar
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary from Shri Ram College of Commerce, Delhi, with over 30 years in finance. He was Group CFO of Medanta (Global Health), where he led its IPO, Group CFO of InterGlobe Enterprises, and held senior finance roles at Bharti Airtel.

people.name: Akshay Tanna
people.relation: Represents KKR (Hector Asia), which owns 54.27%
people.bio: Partner and Head of India Private Equity at KKR, which he joined in Mumbai in 2023 after more than 13 years at TPG, latterly as a Partner. He began in investment banking at Merrill Lynch and Deutsche Bank in New York and London, and has a BS in economics from Wharton. He also sits on the boards of J B Chemicals, Baby Memorial Hospital, Healthium Medtech, Avendus Capital and others.

people.name: Simrun Mehta
people.relation: Represents KKR (Hector Asia)
people.bio: Managing Director in KKR's private-equity team, which she joined in 2012; she leads its Indian consumer, retail and hospital investments. She earlier worked at Nomura and Lehman Brothers and has a BA (Hons) in mathematics from St Stephen's College, Delhi. She is also on the boards of Baby Memorial Hospital, Vini Cosmetics and Avendus Capital.

people.name: Anjali Ajaikumar Rossi
people.relation: Daughter of the chairman
people.bio: Holds an MBA in entrepreneurship from Babson College. At HCG she helped set up central quality, clinical-excellence, operations and nursing teams and oversaw the Milann fertility centres, which were sold in June 2026 to a fund controlled by her father. She also supports the HCG Foundation and is on the board of Bharath Hospital and Institute of Oncology, Mysore.

companies.changes: KKR took control from CVC on 30 May 2025, and Dr Manish Mattoo replaced Meghraj (Raj) Gore as CEO; Mr Gore received ₹17.1cr when HCG bought back vested options for ₹58.1cr. The CFO resigned on 2 September 2025, the CEO doubled as interim CFO from 1 December 2025, and Sanjeev Kumar joined as CFO on 25 May 2026. New internal auditors were appointed in December 2025 and again in May 2026. Independent director Rajiv Maliwal was reappointed in May 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Mahendra Nahata is Managing Director and runs the company; there is no CEO and no regular chairman. Promoters own 28.29% (September 2026), almost all through his entities MN Ventures (13.92%) and NextWave (12.73%), down from 37.84% in December 2023, mostly through promoter sales in 2025 (about 11cr fewer shares, MN Ventures selling about 7.8cr); the group then took warrants for 7.5cr shares at ₹74 (₹138.75cr paid, ₹416cr due by about November 2027), which would lift the stake to about 31.6%. 90 lakh promoter shares are pledged, and most bank loans carry the MD's personal guarantee and an MN Ventures guarantee. The MD's relative Anant Nahata, MD and CEO of promoter-group firm Exicom (FY26 purchases from Exicom ₹64cr), will hold 6.5% of the new defence subsidiary HASPL. Non-executive directors include Arvind Kharabanda (a whole-time director in 1994–2016, now MD of preform subsidiary HFCL Technologies) and Dr R.M. Kastia. MD pay rose to ₹12.07cr in FY26 from ₹7.50cr.

people.name: Mahendra Nahata
people.relation: Founder and promoter
people.stake: 0.09% directly (FY26 annual report); his entities MN Ventures (13.92%) and NextWave (12.73%) take the promoter group to 28.29% (September 2026), plus warrants for 7.5cr shares at ₹74
people.bio: Mahendra Nahata is a commerce graduate (B.Com Hons) of St. Xavier's College, Kolkata. He co-founded HFCL (then Himachal Futuristic Communications) in 1987 and as MD leads its strategy, planning and new businesses. He has been on the board of Reliance Jio Infocomm since 2010, and his family holds about 0.54% of Jio Platforms. He was president of the Telecom Equipment Manufacturers Association of India and has sat on the boards of governors of IIT Bombay, IIT Madras and IIIT Allahabad; Voice & Data named him 'Telecom Man of the Millennium' in 2003. A 2007 SEBI order found that HFCL and its promoters had passed money to Ketan Parekh entities in 2000–01; it was settled in 2010 for ₹10cr. He was paid ₹12.07cr in FY26.

people.name: V.R. (Vijay Raj) Jain
people.bio: Vijay Raj Jain is a chartered accountant and company secretary with a commerce degree from the University of Jodhpur. Before HFCL he worked at Gujarat Heavy Chemicals and TransAsia Carpets. He handles financial strategy, fund-raising through debt and equity, working capital, internal controls and reporting. He was paid ₹4.42cr in FY26.

people.name: Harsh Pagay
people.role: Executive President – Optical Fibre & Optical Fibre Cable
people.bio: Harsh Pagay has a B.Tech from MITS Gwalior and an MBA from ICFAI, Hyderabad. He runs HFCL's fibre and cable plants at Goa and Hyderabad, the business behind the jump in the telecom margin and the long-term supply deals with global multinationals. Before HFCL he was CEO of Teracom and worked at Sterlite Technologies and Finolex Cables.

people.name: Manoj Baid
people.bio: Manoj Baid is a member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India with an undergraduate degree from the University of Rajasthan. He is the company secretary and compliance officer, and also secretary of the group company HFCL Trade-Invest. He was paid ₹1.29cr in FY26.

companies.changes: No CEO. Exits in the last two years: Subodh Kumar Garg (Executive Director – Growth Strategy, December 2024) and Manish Gangey (Executive President – Products, January 2026); independent directors Tamali Sen (December 2024) and Bharat Pal Singh (January 2026) left, and Bela Banerjee (December 2024) and Anil N. Shah (January 2026) joined. Management says an E&Y-led restructuring may split the businesses.

companies.styleNote: Part of Anil Agarwal's Vedanta group. Anil Agarwal is the non-executive chairman and controls Twin Star (Mauritius), which held 42.90% in March 2026 and about 40.7% after the July 2026 share sale, through Vedanta Inc. and the Anil Agarwal Discretionary Trust; promoters together hold 42.29%, down from 53.98% only through dilution from the 2024 and 2026 QIPs, not selling. His brother Pravin Agarwal is Vice-Chairman and a whole-time director, and Pravin's son Ankit Agarwal is MD. Promoters also hold 4.53cr warrants at ₹110 (25% paid; ₹373.7cr due by about September 2027), priced weeks before the $1.11bn hyperscaler award. ₹11cr of managerial pay exceeded legal limits and needed AGM approval, and the MD's wife is paid as a relative of key management. No pledge was declared in FY26.

people.name: Pravin Agarwal
people.since: With the Sterlite group since 1979; reappointed whole-time director from 30 October 2025 to October 2030
people.relation: Promoter group; brother of the chairman Anil Agarwal and father of the MD Ankit Agarwal
people.bio: Pravin Agarwal has been involved with the Sterlite group's Indian operations since it began in 1979, and the company credits him with taking its telecom and power businesses into many markets; it cites nearly four decades in business leadership. He is also non-executive chairman of Sterlite Electric (formerly Sterlite Power Transmission) and a director of Twin Star Display Technologies, STL Networks and Sterlite Tech Cables Solutions. The company's disclosures give no education details.

people.name: Ankit Agarwal
people.since: Joined 2010; MD since 8 October 2021, reappointed to October 2031
people.relation: Promoter group; son of the Vice-Chairman Pravin Agarwal and nephew of the chairman Anil Agarwal
people.bio: Ankit Agarwal has a BBA in finance from the University of Southern California's Marshall School (2004) and an MBA from London Business School (2010). Before STL he worked on Vedanta's corporate portfolio and acquisitions, including the purchase of Cairn India. He joined STL in 2010 and has been MD since October 2021, through the 2025 demerger of the services business and the shift towards data-centre customers. His wife is paid by the company as a relative of key management.

people.name: Venkatesh Murthy
people.bio: Venkatesh Murthy has a bachelor's degree in electronics and communication engineering from Nagpur University and more than three decades in manufacturing operations, business and projects. He was earlier chief operating officer of the optical networking business, running fibre-cable operations across India, Italy and Brazil, and is a director of several Sterlite group companies.

people.name: Ajay Jhanjhari
people.since: Interim CFO from 16 May 2025; permanent from 25 July 2025
people.bio: Ajay Jhanjhari is a chartered accountant with over 15 years in fund-raising, capital allocation, M&A, treasury and business partnering. He joined STL as a management trainee and rose through finance roles to CFO of the optical networking business before succeeding Tushar Shroff as group CFO. He raised the FY27 margin guide to 23% in July 2026 and set out the ₹20,000cr FY29 revenue target at the 3 September 2026 investor day.

people.name: Rahul Puri
people.since: CEO since November 2024; earlier Vice President and General Manager, EMEIA and APAC
people.bio: Rahul Puri has over 24 years in business development, sales, marketing, operations and product management, with earlier roles at Apple, Samsung, Sony Ericsson, Reliance and Airtel. At STL he ran the Europe, Middle East, India and Africa and Asia-Pacific regions before being promoted to head the optical business, which is now almost all of the company's revenue.

people.name: Dr Badri Gomatam
people.bio: Dr Badri Gomatam has a BE from Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, and an MS and PhD from the University of Massachusetts, Amherst. He began in optical communications research and spent about 25 years in the US semiconductor and optical communications industry before moving to India in 2011 to set up STL's Centre of Excellence. He leads its technology work, including multi-core and hollow-core fibre; STL holds 785+ patents.

people.name: Lakshmi Iyer
people.role: Chief M&A, Investor Relations and Capital Markets Strategy Officer
people.bio: Lakshmi Iyer most recently led strategic finance at Tata Power and is reported to have worked on more than $18bn of transactions across energy, infrastructure, industrials and technology. She joined STL as senior management on 23 September 2026.

companies.changes: Group CFO Tushar Shroff left on 31 March 2025; Ajay Jhanjhari was interim CFO from 16 May 2025 and permanent from 25 July 2025. CHRO Anjali Byce left in July 2025, interim CHRO Saumya Mondal died in April 2026, and Anshu Mordia became CHRO in April 2026. Ankit Agarwal was reappointed MD to October 2031 (April 2026) and Pravin Agarwal whole-time director to October 2030. Lakshmi Iyer joined on 23 September 2026. Three independent directors left at the end of their terms. The services business went to STL Networks in the demerger effective 31 March 2025.
